summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24485595 . ## Summary This paper introduces EmergentTTS-Eval, a benchmark of 1,645 test items across six categories of difficult speech synthesis (emotions, paralinguistics, foreign words, questions, syntactic complexity, and complex pronunciation). Only 100 items are human-written seeds, taken from five categories of the previously published BASE-TTS sample set; the remaining 91.5% were generated or rewritten by large language models, including three rounds of "depth" rewrites applied to every base item. Each TTS system is scored by pairwise comparison against a single fixed baseline voice, with Gemini 2.5 Pro acting as an audio judge; the headline metric is a win rate against that baseline. The authors report that judge rankings correlate with human preference at Spearman ρ = 90.5%, and the benchmark has been accepted to the NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks track and is positioned for adoption as a community standard. My concerns are not with the topic, which is important, nor with the engineering effort, which is substantial. They are with the validation chain: at almost every step where the benchmark asks to be trusted — item generation, judging, human alignment, and score stability — the verifying party is either the same model, a very small sample, or a version of the judge that no longer exists. ## Strengths - The judge prompt is published in full (Appendix C.3, and as ` prompts.py ` in the repository), including the per-category scoring rubrics. Anyone can inspect exactly what the judge was told to reward, which is more transparency than most model-as-a-judge work offers. - The raw judge outputs and the evaluation set are publicly downloadable, so third parties can re-aggregate the scores under different rules rather than taking Table 1 on faith. - Results are reported per category (Table 1, Figure 3), not only as a single aggregate win rate, so a system that is strong overall but weak on, say, complex pronunciation is visible as such. - The authors run sensitivity analyses that many benchmark papers skip: swapping the judge across five models (Kendall's W = 0.97, §4.3) and swapping the voice within a system (§4.4). Whatever one thinks of the conclusions drawn from them, the experiments themselves are the right ones to run. - The problem the benchmark addresses is real: word error rate does not capture prosodic or expressive failure, and a hard, adversarial test set for TTS is something the field genuinely needs. ## Major concerns 1. The test items and the judge come from the same model, and this overlap is never discussed, let alone isolated. Of the 1,645 items, only 100 are human-written seeds (five categories drawn from the 140 published BASE-TTS samples). The remaining 91.5% were produced by LLM expansion and rewriting, and all of the depth rewrites — the transformations that generate three of every four items in the set — were performed by Gemini 2.5 Pro (Appendix A, Appendix C.1). The primary judge is also Gemini 2.5 Pro (§3.2). The judge is therefore grading systems on items written in its own generation style, against rubrics applied to its own rewrites. Model families are known to favour outputs resembling their own; whether or not that effect is large here, a benchmark whose item generator and judge are the same model must at minimum acknowledge the confound and ideally report a control (for example, judge performance on the human-seed subset alone, or a cross-family generator/judge pairing). Neither appears anywhere in the paper. 2. The claim of high correlation with human preference rests on eight data points, eight annotators, and annotators who do not agree well with each other. The headline figure, Spearman ρ = 90.5% (Table 3b), is a correlation between rankings of eight models, not between per-item judgements; with n = 8, the statistic is extremely coarse. The hu

summary: We present a minimal three-layer framework in which spacetime geometry emerges from a pre-geometric sub-Planckian microscopic substrate. The microscopic layer consists of algebraic tokens evolving under local update rules. A resolution kernel performs coarse-graining, producing macroscopic fields that admit a geometric interpretation. Geometry appears as a bloom: a stable, self-consistent structure arising from averaged microscopic algebraic token behavior. In this setting, curvature corresponds to the macroscopic imprint of microscopic motion, while torsion reflects the macroscopic memory of intrinsic spin alignment. Torsion is algebraic, non-propagating, and carries no independent degrees of freedom. Mass is identified with geometry at rest. summary: Data, derived results, and reservoir training code underlying the article "Photo-induced currents and short-term memory for reservoir computing in a ferroelectric semiconductor". The record is organised by figure. It contains: current-voltage characteristics, photocurrent relaxation traces for Ohmic and Schottky contacts, paired-pulse facilitation measurements, the full measured photocurrent response to a 400-pulse light sequence, the light-pulse input sequence, averaged pulse responses grouped by "past" pulse level, recognition accuracy as a function of training-set size for the reservoir / no-reservoir / simulated configurations, a baseline-drift correction, an accuracy-versus- node-count scan, and a double-exponential fit to the photocurrent decay. Both the as-measured data (in physical units) and the plotted/normalized traces are provided, together with the recipes needed to go from one to the other. The reservoir training code (fig3/reservoir_readout.py) is standalone and reproduces the published recognition accuracies from the data in this record. See README.md for the full figure-to-file map, data dictionary, and processing recipes.

summary: Smart-OMS: Research Software and Reproducibility Package This repository provides the research software and supporting materials associated with the study entitled “ A Hyperledger Fabric-Based Trusted Data Pipeline for EDI-Driven Business Intelligence in Automotive Order Management .” Smart-OMS is a research prototype that integrates Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) processing, Hyperledger Fabric-based transaction validation, and Business Intelligence (BI) analytics to support trusted data management in automotive supply chain operations. The proposed framework aims to enhance data integrity, transaction traceability, transparency, and reliability through a permissioned blockchain-based architecture, while supporting data-driven analysis and decision-making in automotive order management. The software archive is organized into components covering backend implementation, blockchain chaincode, deployment, baseline comparison, performance evaluation using Hyperledger Caliper, BI validation, tampering tests, experimental data, analysis, and technical documentation. The package is intended to facilitate technical inspection, experimental reproducibility, independent validation, and further development of the proposed framework, contributing to research on blockchain-enabled EDI processing and trusted Business Intelligence systems.

summary: Overview This repository provides the reproducibility dataset, experimental protocols, execution scripts, policy definitions, and supplementary materials supporting the study "Loss of Approval Validity After Critical Evidence Removal in Construction QA/QC". The study evaluates Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-4.1-mini using 28 synthetic construction QA/QC evidence packs, five controlled evidence states (T0, E1, E2, E6, and E7), and six requirement-level decisions per state. The frozen primary experiment comprises 280 archived API responses and 1,680 requirement-level acceptance decisions. Repository contents The deposit includes the frozen experimental dataset, author-defined policy oracle, primary estimand specifications, execution and scoring scripts, archived model responses, supplementary analyses, and integrity-verification materials. Primary evaluation outcomes The study evaluates policy-validity loss under role-critical documentary evidence removal relative to a policy-irrelevant control intervention. The study-defined Intervention-Validity Contrast (τ_IVC) was 0.0476 for Gemini 2.5 Flash and 0.1012 for GPT-4.1-mini. Across all five evaluated evidence states, unsafe automatic approvals totalled 26 for Gemini and 17 for GPT. Reproducibility and limitations The primary results are preserved in a frozen reproducibility archive with SHA-256 integrity checks. Supplementary analyses include offline rule-gating assessments, a multi-run sensitivity experiment, and an exploratory control analysis. The benchmark uses synthetic construction records and an author-defined policy oracle. The study does not establish independent engineering validation, production deployment suitability, or real-world construction safety. Exact replay of hosted LLM outputs is not guaranteed. The study evaluates Gemini 2.5 Flash and GPT-4.1-mini using 28 synthetic construction QA/QC evidence packs, five controlled evidence states (T0, E1, E2, E6, and E7), and six requirement-level decisions per state. The frozen primary experiment comprises 280 archived API responses and 1,680 requirement-level acceptance decisions. Repository contents The deposit includes the frozen experimental dataset, author-defined policy oracle, primary estimand specifications, execution and scoring scripts, archived model responses, supplementary analyses, and integrity-verification materials. Primary evaluation outcomes The study evaluates policy-validity loss under role-critical documentary evidence removal relative to a policy-irrelevant control intervention. The study-defined Intervention-Validity Contrast (τ_IVC) was 0.0476 for Gemini 2.5 Flash and 0.1012 for GPT-4.1-mini. Across all five evaluated evidence states, unsafe automatic approvals totalled 26 for Gemini and 17 for GPT. Reproducibility and limitations The primary results are preserved in a frozen reproducibility archive with SHA-256 integrity checks. Supplementary analyses include offline rule-gating assessments, a multi-run sensitivity experiment, and an exploratory control analysis. The benchmark uses synthetic construction records and an author-defined policy oracle. The study does not establish independent engineering validation, production deployment suitability, or real-world construction safety. Exact replay of hosted LLM outputs is not guaranteed. Includes the pre-registered analysis protocol dated 2026-11-23 (before any re-analysis), the audit quantification scripts and reports, and the frozen production scripts for provenance of the reviewed v1.x results. MIMIC-IV-ECG waveforms are not included (PhysioNet credentialing required).

summary: This article analyzes the philosophical implications of Alpöge's November 2026 Lean formalization of the Riemann hypothesis, a proof co-developed with AI assistance. While formal verification is established, conceptual understanding remains incomplete. The article introduces "hybrid conceptual authority" to describe how conceptual contribution and justificatory authority diverge in AI-assisted mathematics. Drawing on philosophy of chemistry's model of explanatory autonomy, it proposes a four-dimensional framework verification, reconstruction, attribution, and interpretation for evaluating epistemic practice in proof production.
title: Hybrid Conceptual Authority in AI-Assisted Mathematics

summary: Description This dataset documents the participation of female musicians in European concert life between 1750 and 1800. It records individual performers alongside detailed information on their appearances in public concerts, enabling the reconstruction of collaborative performance networks. By cross-referencing musicians and shared concert events, the dataset captures patterns of co-performance and professional interaction within Europe's musical scene.   Developed as part of a broader doctoral research project on women’s roles in eighteenth-century European music, the dataset integrates biographical data with performance records. The data is structured as an Excel database partitioned into functional sheets, including Nodes, Interactions, and Edges, which are optimized for direct import into Gephi network visualization software. Each node entry includes detailed attribute columns such as names, nationalities, roles, musical competencies (e.g., composer, singer, instrument, teacher), and documented travel corridors.   The database forms the direct foundation for network visualizations, in which musicians and associated entities are represented as nodes and their shared performances are represented as edges. These structured sheets allow for the direct analysis of the density, mobility, and structure of professional relationships, with data pre-formatted to easily reflect the frequency of collaboration.   Methodology The dataset was constructed through systematic analysis of primary sources and historical concert records, supplemented by secondary literature. Musicians were included based on the availability of sufficient biographical and performance data to support meaningful analysis. Relationships were established through documented co-appearances in concerts.   Limitations The dataset reflects the uneven survival of historical records and prioritizes musicians with sufficiently documented careers. As such, it does not represent a complete census of performers active in London during this period.   Data Integrity and Usage: This record contains original Excel databases developed as part of a doctoral dissertation. For network analysis, the individual sheets can be exported as CSV files and imported directly into Gephi as Node and Edge tables.   Copyright Note: Every effort has been made to trace the copyright holders of any third-party archival materials referenced within these databases. This dataset documents the participation of female musicians in Sweden's opera life between 1750 and 1800. It records individual performers alongside detailed information on their appearances in public concerts, enabling the reconstruction of collaborative performance networks. By cross-referencing musicians and shared operatic events, the dataset captures patterns of co-performance and professional interaction within Sweden’s operatic scene. Developed as part of a broader doctoral research project on women’s roles in eighteenth-century European music, the dataset integrates biographical data with performance records. Each entry includes information such as names, roles (e.g., vocalist, instrumentalist, composer), and concert affiliations. The dataset also includes associated musicians who appear at the same events, enabling network-based analysis. The database formed the basis for network visualizations produced in Gephi, in which musicians are represented as nodes and shared performances as edges. These visualizations highlight the density and structure of professional relationships, with node size and edge weight reflecting frequency of collaboration. Methodology The dataset was constructed through systematic analysis of primary sources and historical concert records, supplemented by secondary literature. Musicians were included based on the availability of sufficient biographical and performance data to support meaningful analysis. Relationships were established through documented co-appearances in concerts. Limitations The dataset reflects the uneven survival of historical records and prioritizes musicians with sufficiently documented careers. As such, it does not represent a complete census of performers active in London during this period. This dataset documents the participation of female musicians in Sweden's opera life between 1750 and 1800. It records individual performers alongside detailed information on their appearances in public concerts, enabling the reconstruction of collaborative performance networks. By cross-referencing musicians and shared operatic events, the dataset captures patterns of co-performance and professional interaction within Sweden’s operatic scene. Developed as part of a broader doctoral research project on women’s roles in eighteenth-century European music, the dataset integrates biographical data with performance records. Each entry includes information such as names, roles (e.g., vocalist, instrumentalist, composer), and concert affiliations. The database formed the basis for network visualizations produced in Gephi, in which musicians are represented as nodes and shared performances as edges. Musicians were included based on the availability of sufficient biographical and performance data to support meaningful analysis. Limitations The dataset reflects the uneven survival of historical records and prioritizes musicians with sufficiently documented careers. As such, it does not represent a complete census of performers active in London during this period. summary: Description This dataset documents the participation of female musicians in Europe's concert life between 1750 and 1800. It records individual performers alongside detailed information on their appearances in public concerts, enabling the reconstruction of collaborative performance networks. By cross-referencing musicians and shared concert events, the dataset captures patterns of co-performance and professional interaction within Europe's musical scene. Developed as part of a broader doctoral research project on women’s roles in eighteenth-century European music, the dataset integrates biographical data with performance records. Each entry includes information such as names, roles (e.g., vocalist, instrumentalist, composer), and concert affiliations. The dataset also includes associated musicians who appear at the same events, enabling network-based analysis. The database formed the basis for network visualizations produced in Gephi, in which musicians are represented as nodes and shared performances as edges. These visualizations highlight the density and structure of professional relationships, with node size and edge weight reflecting frequency of collaboration. Methodology The dataset was constructed through systematic analysis of primary sources and historical concert records, supplemented by secondary literature. Musicians were included based on the availability of sufficient biographical and performance data to support meaningful analysis. Relationships were established through documented co-appearances in concerts. Limitations The dataset reflects the uneven survival of historical records and prioritizes musicians with sufficiently documented careers. As such, it does not represent a complete census of performers active in London during this period. summary: FAIR metadata (Schema.org, Bioschemas and MLCommons Croissant) for the ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo benchmark of 1,677 homodimer interfaces from 1,645 protein crystal structures, together with the structure files (PDB and mmCIF), an in-repository snapshot of the PDB metadata of every entry, the documentation of the label curation, and four homology-aware 5-fold cross-validation splits (CATH/UniProt, MMseqs2, BLASTClust and their union) attached to every interface. The benchmark was published by Schweke et al. (2023, Proteomics 23(17):e2200323, doi:10.1002/pmic.202200323; 836 physiological and 841 non-physiological interfaces). This package uses the curated annotation file of the benchmark authors (844 physiological and 833 non-physiological interfaces; 16 labels revised, 20 interfaces flagged ambiguous and 6 flagged for deletion). Every interface carries both the curated label and the published label ( PublishedPhysio ). See data/curation/README.md . Please cite the original publication as well as this package.
title: ELIXIR - Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark - FAIR Metadata

summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in real-world long-horizon manipulation, where memory plays a crucial role. However, existing memory-augmented VLAs either retrieve past observations without reasoning about what they imply, or reason over the full history in a shared context where it crowds out current perception. Cognitive science treats them as distinct systems: memory reconstructs past experience to decide what to do, while perception guides how to act. We therefore propose ActMem, an in-context memory framework that decouples memory reasoning from perceptual grounding within a single vision-language backbone. Built on a vision-language model with native video understanding, ActMem infers the current subtask from a timestamped interaction history and keeps the hidden states formed during this inference as a Latent Memory Chain-of-Thought (Memory CoT), which conditions a flow-matching action expert. Perception Attention further lets the expert attend directly to the current view. To keep inference fast under long histories, Efficient Memory CoT Inference reuses computation across consecutive decisions without changing the output. ActMem achieves 71.1% task success and 80.8% completion success on RoboMemArena, surpassing the strongest baseline by 7.5 and 8.7 percentage points, and 73.8% average success on MIKASA-Robo, the best among all compared methods. In the real world, it reaches 68.8% average success on exogenous, endogenous, and traceless memory tasks, 10.0 percentage points above the strongest memory-augmented VLA. Code and checkpoints will be released at https://github.com/LigphiDonk/ActMem and https://huggingface.co/donk111/ActMem.
title: ActMem: From Latent Memory Reasoning to Grounded Robotic Action

summary: Training Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models and World-Action Models (WAMs) is computationally expensive, while their heterogeneous architectures and fragmented training stacks make system optimizations difficult to reuse across models. To address these challenges, we present LoongForge-Embodied, a native-PyTorch framework that unifies and accelerates the training of heterogeneous embodied models. At its core, LoongForge-Embodied introduces a common abstraction layer that decouples model-specific implementations from shared training infrastructure, enabling cross-model reuse without constraining individual architectures or execution requirements. Buildingon this unified infrastructure, the framework combines reusable acceleration mechanisms with model-specific and hardware-aware optimization strategies across computation, execution, memory, data I/O, and distributed communication, including FP8-based communication optimizations for DDP and FSDP. Beyond training acceleration, LoongForge-Embodied integrates a unified data infrastructure with a pipeline for synthesizing robot data from egocentric data, and an efficient evaluation framework that supports concurrency and optimized computation in simulator. Experiments across representative VLA and WAM models demonstrate 1.47x-4.38x end-to-end training throughput improvements over their corresponding open-source baselines, as well as 4.1x-23.2x faster evaluation under the same protocols.
title: LoongForge-Embodied: A Unified Framework for Training Heterogeneous Embodied Models

summary: Combining fine-tuned models by composing their parameter updates has become a standard alternative to multi-task training. We formalize composability as a property of a collection of task vectors and prove that the excess loss of the merged model is controlled by an interference functional of the cross-task curvature overlap and the signed alignment of the updates. In the quadratic regime this functional equals the excess loss, giving a criterion that is necessary as well as sufficient and that measures the angle between task vectors in the curvature metric rather than the Euclidean one. Fine-tuning under a curvature-guided regularizer -- constructed from curvature statistics of the kind memory-efficient optimizers maintain -- keeps displacement in the base curvature metric below a ceiling set by the penalty coefficient at every iterate, at the standard $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ non-convex rate. Under a single Loewner comparison between the base statistic and the task curvatures, this control converts into a ceiling on the interference functional, inversely proportional to the penalty coefficient, so that the curvature term of the bound is controlled during training. A first-order term, present because regularized solutions are not stationary for the task loss, is not reduced in the same way. Experiments on an exact non-quadratic model confirm the budget and the ceiling, show the first-order term dominating for strong penalties, and find the curvature-guided penalty slightly better than an isotropic one. In a three-seed transformer study the functional is rank-correlated with merging degradation, but no more strongly than the Euclidean displacement norm.
title: Interference Bounds and Merge-Aware Training Dynamics for Composable Fine-Tuned Models

summary: Similarity search is essential to many applications but incurs massive data movement when executed on conventional architectures. Content-addressable memory (CAM) is a promising hardware substrate, as it allows similarity search directly in the CAM array, minimizing data movement and offering both low latency and high energy efficiency. However, conventional CAM array readout produces only binary match results, discarding quantitative similarity information that could be further exploited. Extracting this information requires interpreting the CAM array output voltage that evolves during a CAM search, making the sensing timestamp a crucial design variable alongside the reference voltage and decoding parameter. In this work, we propose RE-CAM, a readout enhancement framework for CAM that is agnostic to memory technology and application, enabling CAM array readout to approximate linear and nonlinear functions with one CAM search. By reusing the comparators to sense the time-varying output voltage multiple times, jointly optimizing the three design variables under system constraints and hardware nonidealities, and co-designing the optimization algorithm and reconfigurable hardware, RE-CAM achieves accurate approximation with low energy and area overhead without introducing a readout throughput bottleneck. Across linear, piecewise-linear, sigmoid, and exponential functions, RE-CAM reduces normalized root mean square error by 10.89% to 24.34% for general approximation and 29.43% to 46.73% when exploiting dataset distribution, compared to a shared uniform-reference ADC baseline with the same comparison budget. Relative to the same baseline, RE-CAM also achieves $8\times$ higher search throughput while reducing energy per search and area by 47% and 39%, respectively.
title: RE-CAM: Readout-Enhanced Content-Addressable Memory for Quantitative Similarity Search

summary: Neural state-space identification learns dynamical models from measured inputs and outputs. SUBNET combines this task with an encoder that estimates initial states from short measurement histories. Its continuous-time version requires many successive neural-network evaluations during numerical integration, resulting in slow training speed which is a major limitation for practical use cases. We propose deep structured state space models (DS3M), which combine compact nonlinear dynamical components in parallel and in series. Custom GPU kernels implemented with Triton reduce the launch and memory overhead of their sequential evaluation. We explain this construction, describe a port-Hamiltonian variant, and present various benchmark comparisons of accuracy and training time.
title: DS3M: Deep structured state space models for nonlinear system identification on modern hardware

summary: Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Our substrate is a fixed-capacity LoRA adapter that consists of k-hot rank combinations which store facts without catastrophic interference and maintain an independently controlled temporal decay, enabling outdated information to fade while long-term facts persist. On this substrate, we train a lightweight controller that governs each incoming user event to ensure the memory system reflects the user's true, updated belief state. To evaluate how memory systems manage user memory, we introduce a controlled dataset of long-horizon user trajectories with varying persistence of facts based on changing belief states and user-behavioral shifts, and probe queries that test recall while information is valid and abstention after it expires. Our policy learns to effectively manage user memory over its entire lifecycle, balancing recall and abstention to achieve 86% of oracle performance, unlike CL and RAG baselines that primarily default to one of the two behaviors. By providing the first system to manage memory directly in model weights, this work establishes a foundation for long-horizon parametric memory.
title: Some Memories Must Fade: Persistence and Decay of User Memories in Model Parameters

summary: Search, especially top-k similarity search, plays a vital role in many applications, but its performance can be severely limited by memory access overhead. In-memory search (IMS), an alternative to CPU/GPU-based approaches, exploits massive parallelism within a content-addressable memory (CAM) array to perform search in situ and provides both low latency and high energy efficiency. However, the capacity of a single CAM array is often insufficient for modern workloads, requiring data to be distributed across multiple arrays. Deploying scalable top-k similarity search across multiple CAM arrays poses a fundamental problem that existing designs fail to address: how to accurately and efficiently reduce local binary match results to global top-k results. This work introduces CAIMS, a cross-array IMS framework that is agnostic to memory technologies and applications, enabling scalable and efficient top-k similarity search while preserving accuracy. To enable accurate top-k result reduction, CAIMS leverages the existing threshold match functionality with a combined offline and online parameter selection approach to transform local binary match results that lack globally comparable similarity information into global coarse-grained similarity scores. To further improve efficiency, CAIMS conducts hierarchical reduction and transfers only the selection results and necessary control signals with lightweight local peripherals. Implemented on a 3D NAND Flash model and demonstrated using the retrieval phase of retrieval-augmented generation, CAIMS improves throughput by up to $22.3\times/10.1\times$ and energy efficiency by $426.6\times/23.7\times$ compared to the server-class CPU baseline and prior 3D NAND Flash accelerators, respectively, while maintaining comparable accuracy.
title: CAIMS: Scalable Cross-Array In-Memory Search

summary: Long-horizon LLM agents often exceed their context windows, forcing them to discard information that may be needed later. Existing context management strategies rely on summarization, masking, or structured memory, requiring decisions about what to preserve or how to retrieve it before future needs are known. However, these methods can introduce lossy compression, potentially discarding details needed for future tasks. To address this limitation, we introduce GrepMem, a simple, lossless, and index-free memory mechanism built on two components: an append-only plain-text log of the agent's complete history and a regular-expression search tool for on-demand recall. Unlike structured memory systems, GrepMem requires no embeddings, retrieval index, memory extraction, or additional models. We train Qwen3.5-9B with reinforcement learning under five context management strategies and evaluate on multi-question research sessions, long-stream recall, and agent-trajectory question answering. GrepMem achieves 95-97% accuracy on ContextBench, versus at most 21% for lossy baselines, and outperforms SUPO's summarization by 8.8 percentage points on BCP-Multi. GrepMem scales effectively to increasingly long input streams while remaining on the accuracy-token-cost Pareto frontier across all five evaluation tasks. Our results show that a plain-text log and grep provide a simple but competitive approach to long-horizon agent memory, without requiring complex structured memory infrastructure.
title: Forget Freely, Grep Later: Lossless, Index-Free Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

summary: DISCO is a recent internal cluster validity index for density-based clustering that, unlike earlier indices, also evaluates the quality of noise labels. The discoCVI package makes DISCO available in R. This article describes the design of the package and a typical workflow, in which DISCO is used to compare clusterings and to choose the parameters of HDBSCAN without ground truth, followed by the implementation introduced in version 0.2.0. DISCO is defined through density-connectivity distances between all pairs of points, so direct implementations store several n-by-n matrices. We show that every quantity DISCO needs can be read off the single-linkage merge tree of the mutual-reachability minimum spanning tree, so that the index can be computed exactly with memory that grows linearly with the number of points, while the running time remains quadratic as in the original definition. The implementation is tested against the previous version, agrees with the original Python implementation to within $3 \times 10^{-13}$, and corrects the score of singleton clusters to match the published definition. In benchmarks, discoCVI is 23 to 138 times faster than its previous version for 500 to 4,000 points and 3 to 9 times faster than the Python reference for 500 to 8,000 points, using a fraction of the memory of both, and it scores 100,000 points in about 50 seconds with less than 200 MB of memory.
title: Fast and Memory-Light Evaluation of Density-Based Clusterings with the DISCO Index in R

summary: Calibrating a volatility surface from sparse option prices requires repeated solutions of a pricing equation as the volatility parameters change. We implement a hybrid quantum and classical method for this inverse problem using the Dupire local-volatility model. A positive coefficient representation specifies the local variance, and linear combinations of Hamiltonian simulations approximate the associated pricing evolution. The circuit propagates through successive maturity intervals and evaluates discrepancies at the observed strikes. Measurement counts provide the objective values used by a classical optimiser to update the volatility coefficients. We implement this calibration cycle in a logical gate simulator and assess it alongside classical pricing solvers and alternative surface models. Multiple-maturity synthetic examples illustrate the reconstruction of smiles and skews, while a separate small circuit experiment tests the complete measured calibration. The comparisons quantify the effects of model flexibility, pricing approximation and measurement precision. Recorded gate counts and sampling budgets identify the main computational costs of the implementation.
title: Quantum Calibration of Local-Volatility Surfaces from Sparse Option Quotes

summary: Gate-level netlists circulate among IP integrators and foundries and can be extracted from chips. Reverse engineering them into readable register-transfer-level (RTL) code would help an adversary understand and modify a design, but remains difficult because word-level operations are scattered across many gates. Large language models (LLMs) can write and optimize RTL, but often fail to recover it from a whole netlist. We propose LOCA (LOgic Cone Attack), an LLM-based attack that divides an anonymized netlist into logic cones, has parallel agents rewrite them, and assembles compact RTL. Each cone contains the complete next-state logic of a group of related registers, giving an agent a small, meaningful task. Of five partitioning methods tested, only grouped cones lead to recovery. LOCA keeps only RTL proven equivalent to the netlist and measures its quality by compression. Function-preserving obfuscation does not stop LOCA on the tested designs, whereas unknown keys or hidden cell functions prevent it from proving recovery of the original design. Across 21 model-design pairs, LOCA recovers 17, versus 6 with whole-netlist prompting. Per-run recovery across models rises from 5% to 74%, at a median cost below one dollar with a low-cost model.
title: Verified Netlist-to-RTL Recovery with LLM Agents

summary: A neural network that learns an inverse map inherits the approximations of the forward solver used to generate its training data. We demonstrate this in the inference of spin Hamiltonians from synthetic neutron-scattering spectra and show how a fast many-body solver can overcome the limitation of linear spin-wave theory (LSWT). We consider a family of anisotropic triangular-lattice spin Hamiltonians at fields just above saturation, where magnon interactions shift and broaden the spectrum in ways that LSWT cannot capture. Using the truncated Hilbert-space ladder (THL) method, we compute the dynamical spin structure factor (DSSF) nonperturbatively within the one- and two-magnon space. THL is fast enough to generate large training sets of DSSF spectra, enabling us to train neural networks that accurately predict Hamiltonian parameters. By empirically benchmarking several neural-network architectures, we find that a one-dimensional convolutional network performs best. A learned forward decoder then reconstructs the DSSF from the predicted parameters, providing a rapid self-consistency check and a visualization of the predicted response. When interactions are strong, networks trained on LSWT and THL spectra infer markedly different parameters. Analysis of the Fisher information matrix shows that the measurement protocol, including which spin-correlation components are resolved and the momentum cut, determines which couplings can be identified. Combining machine learning with fast many- body theory is therefore essential for quantitative Hamiltonian inference from scattering data.
title: Learning Spin Hamiltonians from Interacting Magnon Spectra

summary: Structural symmetry, thermodynamic phase stability, and elastic-wave response provide related but distinct descriptions of a transforming solid. We formulate a symmetry-stratified framework that connects these descriptions through a finite-dimensional internal state and a parent-invariant free energy. Stabilizers classify structural states, whereas free-energy comparisons and stability conditions determine equilibrium branches and dissipative evolution. Equivariance ensures that the frozen elastic tangent inherits the structural stabilizer. Equality requires additional identifiability conditions. Little-group representations and degenerate perturbation theory then determine whether an acoustic doublet splits and the first nonzero splitting order $p$. On a selected continuous branch with order-parameter exponent $β$, a regular, observable acoustic gap scales as $|t|^{pβ}$, provided critical self-energies and structural relaxation do not dominate the measurement. Explicit tensorial and cubic-to-tetragonal realizations yield linear and quadratic splitting channels, together with directionally protected degeneracies. Separate numerical benchmarks examine free-energy reconstruction, coexistence, elastic compatibility, finite-temperature spectra, and controlled critical readouts. Reanalysis of NiTi measurements illustrates effective elastic degeneracy, thermal-history dependence, and the predictive value of independently measured phase fractions. Most importantly, the framework identifies the constitutive and measurement assumptions required to infer structural changes from mechanical spectra.
title: A Symmetry-Stratified Framework for Phase Transitions: Thermodynamic States, Critical Dynamics, and Spectral Mechanical Signatures

summary: Geometric confinement changes both thermal relaxation and heat throughput, but these effects need not be governed by the same conduction path. We establish a distinction between serial and parallel geometries for passive, homogeneous Fourier conductors at fixed material properties, volume and length. For a reduced variable-area conductor, two logarithmic shape harmonics independently tune two selected Bloch-rate pairs, and exact local transport level sets permit spectral redistribution at fixed effective diffusivity. A nonperturbative weighted Poincaré bound, however, requires the effective axial diffusivity to vanish if the first positive insulated rate tends to zero at fixed length. This obstruction is avoided by continuous parallel paths with weak transverse exchange. Capacity-weighted networks identify the exchange mechanism, and a three-dimensional product domain provides an exact bulk realization. Its axial conductance remains $κV/L^2$, while exactly one positive insulated rate vanishes and the next approaches a positive limit set by axial, chamber and neck diffusion. The slow rate is asymptotically the transverse neck conductance times the sum of inverse chamber capacities. Spectral projection estimates translate this separation into a preparation- and readout-dependent observation window. The result is metastable retention of a temperature contrast under insulated conditions, not a second equilibrium state. It identifies when geometrical control of internal equilibration can be separated from macroscopic heat transport.
title: Geometric control of diffusive relaxation: spectral design, transport bounds and transverse mode isolation

summary: An observable decision reveals the selected action but does not determine which alternatives were internally represented. Drawing on prospection research and hippocampal forward-sweep observations, we develop Before the Choice, an evidence-oriented framework distinguishing future-directed content, prospective computation, and causal guidance. The framework organizes four experimental contrasts and makes their alternative explanations explicit. Its first test case concerns unchosen trajectories in deterministic symbolic environments. A preregistered low-rank probe evaluated once on a sealed TEST did not meet its criterion (paired accuracy 0.020 versus 0.195 for a text-and-observed-choice baseline; 293 admissible pairs). Exploratory H1b exposed a reconstruction-by-elimination problem: identifying the chosen candidate can determine the unchosen target. In H1c, matched worlds varied an unchosen continuation while keeping candidate keys bitwise invariant. With specified positive controls passed, decoding in the late-key condition remained at 0.521 (p = 0.18; 141 contributing families). These observations do not identify prospective simulation or establish an absence of prospective representations. They illustrate why identifiability, sensitivity, and a dependence-aware null model must constrain inferences from decodability. PREM is proposed as an organizational framework and is not validated by these results. We offer it as a methodological contribution to empirical AI welfare research, which will require such evidential distinctions. Code and protocol records: https://github.com/besionisrael/before-choice
title: Before the Choice: An Evidential Framework for Studying Prospective Representations in Language Models

summary: Identifying the phases of a quantum many-body system as its parameters vary is a central problem in condensed-matter physics. Data-driven approaches address this task by comparing quantum states, for instance through their fidelity, and locating transitions where these comparisons change abruptly. In this work, we introduce the inverse participation ratio (IPR) kernel, a kernel method built for learning quantum phases of matter from IPRs in physically motivated bases. Unlike fidelity-based kernels, the IPR kernel can identify states with physically meaningful similarity even when they are orthogonal. We test the method on ground states of the transverse-field Ising (TFIM) and Heisenberg XXZ models. For TFIM Gibbs states, we further show that the IPR kernel retains phase-relevant structure over a range of nonzero temperatures where the phase signal of fidelity-based kernels is already degraded. More broadly, our results suggest that quantum kernels benefit more from feature maps tailored to the physics of the problem than from maximal expressivity.
title: A Basis-Dependent Kernel for Learning Quantum Phases of Matter

summary: Overview The Earth Surface Anomaly dataset (v1.1) is a five-class, event-grouped Sentinel-2 benchmark for immediate disaster and surface-anomaly detection. It contains 622 samples grouped into 46 event or spatiotemporal observation units (17 source-named/inventory units and 29 observation groups, 2017–2025, globally distributed): 129 fire, 58 flood-context, 54 landslide, 204 crop-residue-burning and 177 retrogressive-thaw-slump samples. 595 samples carry source polygon-derived binary masks; 27 carry weak point inventories only; all 54 landslide samples include pre/post paired observations. Industrial heat sources (208 candidates) are excluded from this release and 17 visually ambiguous candidates are withheld, both enumerated in quality/excluded_samples.csv . Sample structure Each sample ( data/CODE/EVENT/SAMPLE/ ) provides a six-band Sentinel-2 L2A chip (declared bands B2, B3, B4, B8, B11, B12; aligned grid spacing does not imply native 10 m for every band), a 0/1 binary mask, RGB/NIR/SWIR previews, annotation.json and measured facts.json (CRS, transform, WGS84 bounds, geometry statistics, spectral indices, SHA256 checksums). Annotation-conditioned vision-language tasks (4–6 per sample depending on label strength and pairing) cover event classification, factual captioning, spatial reasoning, visual grounding, spectral comparison, and for suitable samples temporal reasoning and label provenance. Splits Group splits are precomputed: default splits/event_disjoint (443/102/77 train/val/test) and inherited splits/site_disjoint (433/114/75). Event-disjointness does not guarantee site-disjointness (1 measured case); use site_disjoint when required. Never randomly split patches from the same event. Screening and quality All 639 non-industrial candidates underwent AI-assisted visual screening of RGB, SWIR and target crops with review sheets and per-sample geometry/text audits retained in the release ( quality/ , visual_review.csv ). This is not independent expert pixel adjudication, field validation, or new external verification of every event identity. Limitations (documented in README, README_zh and DATA_DICTIONARY) Flood-context masks often follow existing river channels; no paired baseline establishes incremental inundation. Fire annotations can cover smoke, scars or hotspots and are not universally burned-area boundaries. Crop-residue burning is a source label; imagery alone does not establish fuel identity. Thaw mechanism/onset and landslide onset cannot be established from the supplied views alone. Point inventories (27 samples) are weak localization, not segmentation truth; polygon provenance does not guarantee exact pixel boundaries. Radiometric scale/offset and the inherited non-landslide band mapping have not been independently traced to every source product; facts.json indices are stored-DN calculations, not validated physical reflectance. External event-match references in index/external_verification_ledger.csv were not newly re-verified during release preparation. License and third-party terms CC BY 4.0 applies to the project-original annotations, revisions and documentation. Sentinel/Copernicus imagery is used under modified-data attribution terms and COOLR landslide inventories retain their original conditions; see LICENSE , licenses/ and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md . No ESA or European Union endorsement is implied. Access The metadata and preview figures of this record are public. The files are distributed on an approved-request basis: use the Request access button on this record page and state your affiliation and intended use; requests are reviewed by the authors. The dataset is licensed under CC BY 4.0 for research use, subject to the third-party imagery conditions listed in licenses/ and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md . Citation Zhao, W., & Wang, Q. (2026). title: Earth Surface Anomaly Dataset: Five-Class Event-Grouped Sentinel-2 Observations with Volcano Subset (v1.1)

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24385327 . ### Summary and Overall Assessment Camila Pontara's manuscript, "A Captura Silenciosa: Captura de Fecho, Opacidade e os Limites da Teoria da Governança Criminal" (Version 2), tackles an important blind spot in governance and institutional research. Most studies look at obvious bribery, political lobbying, or open territorial control. Pontara looks somewhere quieter and harder to detect: what she calls closure capture (*captura de fecho*). This happens inside final review and decision-making bodies when concentrated authority and closed-door procedures make it nearly impossible for outsiders to independently verify how a decision was actually reached. The strongest insight in this paper is how it applies the problem of observational equivalence (*equivalência observacional*). Pontara shows that when a final review body operates without real external transparency, an honest, by-the-book decision and a decision quietly shaped by outside interests can leave behind the exact same official paper trail. By refining Version 2 to treat Operações Munditia , Ethos , Scream Fake , and the Banco Master case as exploratory plausibility probes rather than claiming direct causal proof, she keeps the argument disciplined, fair, and grounded as a testable hypothesis. --- ### Core Strengths 1. Avoiding the "Secrecy Equals Guilt" Trap: Rather than treating institutional opacity as automatic proof of corruption, Pontara frames institutional verifiability as a measurable spectrum. That restraint makes her framework genuinely useful for researchers comparing different agencies or legal systems. 2. Connecting Criminal Governance to Financial Oversight: Including the Banco Master episode alongside judicial and administrative cases shows that closure capture is not just an organized-crime issue—it is a structural risk anywhere high-stakes financial or regulatory decisions are closed off from outside scrutiny. 3. Clear Boundaries in Version 2: Explicitly laying out alternative explanations and criteria that could disprove the hypothesis makes this a strong, portable starting point for future comparative studies. --- ### Constructive Suggestions for Revision 1. Addressing the "Missing Evidence" Problem in Process Tracing: Because closure capture works by hiding or blocking the paper trail needed to prove outside influence, researchers using process tracing face an uphill battle: the lack of a "smoking gun" in the file looks identical whether the institution acted cleanly or successfully hid its tracks. The paper would be stronger if it briefly explained how researchers can tell the difference—for example, by looking at unusual timing, sudden shifts in how cases are routed, or decisions that break sharply from normal institutional patterns. 2. Clarifying When Legitimate Confidentiality Becomes Closure Capture: In criminal investigations and banking supervision (like Banco Master ), temporary secrecy is often necessary to protect witnesses, ongoing inquiries, or financial stability. Drawing a clearer line around timing would sharpen the argument: legitimate confidentiality is temporary during an active review, whereas closure capture uses the final closing of a case to keep the record permanently locked away from retrospective audit. 3. Connecting to International Research on Institutional Opacity and Intermediary Entropy: Pontara's insight—that formal, closed procedures can look completely clean on the surface while masking hidden distortion underneath—connects directly to international work on the Systemic Intent Shadow (SIS) and The Zero-Defect Paradox (Rodriguez, 2026a, 2026b). summary: This repository contains the source code, benchmark data, and computational results for FigEA, an evolutionary algorithm developed for the Minimum Fill-In Problem, also known as the chordal completion problem. FigEA represents candidate solutions through vertex elimination orderings and combines evolutionary operators with problem-specific constructive information. The repository includes the implementation of the algorithm, constructive heuristics used for comparison and initialization, benchmark instances, experimental scripts, and auxiliary files required to reproduce the computational experiments and analyze the reported results. The benchmark instances are based on the PACE 2017 Minimum Fill-In dataset. The materials are provided to facilitate reproducibility, verification of the reported results, and further experimentation with evolutionary approaches to chordal completion.
title: FigEA: An Evolutionary Algorithm for the Minimum Fill-In Problem — Code, Data, and Computational Results

summary: OpenEBench implementation of the ELIXIR 3D-BioInfo benchmark for discriminating physiological from crystallographic (non-physiological) protein homodimer interfaces: schema-validated OpenEBench metadata (Community, Benchmarking Event, Challenge, Metrics, Tools, Contacts), the datasets of 14 reference scoring methods (13 research groups and a random-forest consensus), the gold-standard labels, four homology-aware cross-validation fold assignments, the benchmark workflow scripts (validation, metric computation, consolidation), and a static web page that evaluates new predictions in the browser and ranks them against the reference methods. The benchmark has 1,671 entries (840 physiological and 831 non-physiological): the 1,677 entries of the curated annotation of the benchmark authors, without the six entries flagged for deletion. The labels are those of the curated annotation, which differs for 16 entries from the original publication (Schweke et al. 2023, Proteomics 23(17):e2200323, doi:10.1002/pmic.202200323; 836 physiological and 841 non-physiological interfaces). The scores of the 13 research groups are those submitted to the original benchmark repository; the random-forest consensus uses the leave-one-out probabilities provided there. Interactive page: https://elixir.unibo.it/tools/oeb_3dbioinfo_ppi_benchmark/ . Please cite the original publication as well as this package.
title: ELIXIR - Protein-Protein Interface Benchmark - OpenEBench Experiment

summary: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.
title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control

summary: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.
title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)

summary: Proactive video assistants must decide not only what to say, but also when to speak. Existing reinforcement-learning objectives can reward timely, correct responses without accounting for response volume, thereby encouraging unnecessary or repeated emissions. We identify this failure mode in MMDuet2, whose proactive area-under-the-curve (PAUC) reward promotes timely responses but does not price the number of emissions. We show analytically that this makes additional responses weakly penalized or effectively free, systematically encouraging over-emission. We then propose an emission-aware F1 reward for interval-valued annotations, using exclusive span--emission matching to price false emissions and missed spans. Under MMDuet2's training recipe, our policy on the visual subset of OmniPro replies 2.5x less often than MMDuet2 while raising timing F1 from 0.259 to 0.396 and content-aware F1 from 0.103 to 0.154; a more conservative variant cuts replies by 82.5% and raises precision from 0.161 to 0.418. On ProactiveVideoQA, the same reward adds replies where the baseline is nearly silent, and PAUC ranks a heavily over-emitting policy second despite near-last F1, because it is insensitive to response count. Our results indicate that proactive assistants should be trained and evaluated with objectives that price emissions.
title: SHUSH: Emission-Aware Reward Design for Proactive Video Assistants

summary: Large language models increasingly rely on extended reasoning traces, yet the training signals used to shape this behavior remain coarse. Supervised fine-tuning on full trajectories forces the model to imitate an entire demonstration, overconstraining its output distribution, while trajectory-level reinforcement learning provides only weak credit assignment, rewarding or penalizing whole completions without identifying where they succeed or fail. We propose edit-based training, a general framework for learning from a model's own trajectories via localized textual corrections. Given a sampled completion, an editor identifies the first point of failure under a specified criterion and proposes a minimal replacement span. The model is then supervised only on these edited spans. By design, this concentrates supervision where the model's reasoning first breaks down and aims to preserve its existing reasoning patterns elsewhere. The method applies both offline and online, with the latter continually adapting supervision to the model's evolving failure modes. We instantiate this approach on reasoning instruction following with Qwen3-32B on the ReasonIF benchmark. Compared to full-trajectory imitation and trajectory-level reinforcement learning baselines, edit-based training substantially improves compliance with the reasoning instruction while largely preserving the model's skills on untargeted tasks. These results suggest that localized correction is an effective complement to these approaches for shaping how LLMs reason.
title: Training LLMs to Follow Reasoning Instructions with Minimal Edits

summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) can act as closed-loop robot-use agents (RUAs) by writing and executing control code through tool interfaces. However, turning an open-weight VLM into a high-performing embodied agent requires a complete post-training stack: out-of-the-box open VLMs fail completely at interactive tool contracts, strong frontier teachers are accessible only as black-box endpoints without exposed weights or token probabilities, and supervised imitation alone plateaus under rollout distribution shift. We present EmbodyAgent, an end-to-end post-training framework with three tightly coupled pipelines: (1) a black-box data synthesis pipeline that queries a strong teacher under a forced think-then-code contract and filters trajectories by task success; (2) an SFT pipeline that distills the explanation-and-program targets into an open-weight 9B VLM with both vision and language encoders trainable; and (3) an online RL pipeline that optimizes student-generated episodes via group-relative advantage with a runtime-error-penalized outcome reward. All three pipelines share one primitive-free Python execution tool exposing only raw visual observation and seven-dimensional end-effector control, with no action decoder and no interface shift across stages. Under a strictly separated evaluation protocol on ten LIBERO Spatial tasks (disjoint state splits, greedy test-time decoding, training-only safeguards), held-out success on 100 test states rises from 0/100 (base 9B VLM) to 14/100 (after SFT) and 84/100 (after RL), while training rollout success climbs from 8.4% to 87.7% and median model calls per episode drop from 36 to 11. We further identify a self-reinforcing runtime-error mode induced by outcome-based RL on executable code, and establish a failure-category monitoring and sampling-side curation protocol that stabilizes training.
title: EmbodyAgent: Post-Training Embodied VLM Agents via Distillation, SFT, and RL

summary: 研究館藏/旗艦館藏 第241-250頁(共300頁) 科學的失敗、計量學和獨立證據的極限 旗艦13號裂變 | 第三卷 | 作者33 | STARLI研究設計工作版 v1.0 這十部研究設計專著從奈米量子失效物理學和重建的微型機器人取樣真理出發,探討了盲法生物感測、實驗室間轉移、不確定性預算、參考物質互換性、生產批次效應、污染溯源、漂移/生物學分離以及任務失敗分類等問題。它們提出的是可檢驗的實驗方案,而非觀察到的新科學定律或臨床結果。 這十個英文工作版本共包含7770頁,300幅數學圖版,820個章節開頭,4100篇單頁研究,2000個研究門戶和330個鳳凰答案胚胎。每個門戶都包含一封由三個部分組成的推測信——起源、極端外推和未來研究計劃——但不取代經過驗證的證偽和獨立的實物證據。結構數量並不能確立科學創新性。 研究單元 I · F241–F245 F241 奈米量子研究系統故障極限物理學-重點:光源老化與致動器卡死故障。直接證據:危險事件發生率 [h^-1]。在不轉移的情況下,透過單點重複性進行測試。探測器增益漂移是一個重要的競爭因素;如果釋放出存在危險缺陷的裝置,則拒絕發布。 F242 微型機器人取樣真實性重建的極限-重點:微通道壁吸附與吸附-解吸記憶。直接證據:樣品來源回收率[百分比]。對照紙質批次記錄和終點檢查進行測試。移液管體積誤差是潛在的競爭對手;如果物料平衡或來源不符,則拒絕放行。 F243 量子生物感測器盲測極限挑戰-重點:自旋相干參考替換與電荷態切換。直接見證:預期正確驗收率[百分比]。與標準統計製程控制(限值已凍結)進行比較測試。即時競爭者為微波拾取;如果第二個測試點無法重現鑑定結果,則拒絕發布。 F244 奈米機器人實驗室間環形比對的極限-重點:雷射波長轉移與微尺度熱探針偏移。直接驗證:絕對的站點間測量偏差[單位]。測試與單一站點重複性(無需轉移)的比較。實驗室溫度差異是重要的競爭因素;如果釋放出有危險缺陷的產品,則拒絕發布。 F245 微量取樣不確定度預算極限 — 重點:體積計量誤差與壁損不確定度。直接驗證:預期區間覆蓋率(百分比)。對照紙質批次記錄和終點檢定進行測試。液體表面張力是重要的影響因素;如果物料平衡或來源不明,則拒絕放行。     第二研究單元/證據、轉移與傳承 第二研究單元 · F246–F250 F246 量子感測器參考物質的可互換性極限測試-重點:基質依賴性結合和螢光團光漂白。直接證據:不可互換性偏差[單位]。採用標準統計製程管制和凍結限值進行測試。一個潛在的競爭因素是分析物濃度不符;如果第二個測試點無法重現鑑定結果,則拒絕放行。 F247 奈米機器人製造批次效應辨識的極限-重點:光刻掩模對準和塗層孔隙缺陷。直接驗證:未經篩選的合格批次良率(百分比)。在不轉移的情況下,與單點重複性進行比較測試。一個重要的競爭因素是後加工分類;如果釋放出有害缺陷,則拒絕放行。 F248 微流控採樣污染溯源極限 — 重點:管路吸附儲液槽與生物膜滯留。直接見證:正確的污染源分類[百分比]。對照紙質批次記錄和終點檢查進行測試。新鮮試劑污染是主要競爭因素;如果物料平衡或來源不明,則拒絕放行。 F249 量子感測器在極限情況下分離漂移和生物變化-重點:雷射頻率漂移和基質離子強度變化。直接驗證:訊號源區分準確率(百分比)。與標準統計製程控制(限值固定)進行比較測試。活體競爭物代表真實的分析物波動;如果第二個偵測點無法重現驗證結果,則拒絕放行。 F250奈米機器人任務失敗分類極限-重點:磁驅動失速與機器人碰撞級聯。直接觀察:不安全誤釋放率[百分比]。測試單點重複性,無需轉移。光學追蹤遮擋是實際的競爭因素;如果釋放出有危險缺陷的機器人,則拒絕釋放。 科學邊界、證據和品質保證狀態 所有工作均限於可追溯材料、合成標準品、允許的離體參考物、密封微流控模型和非臨床台架測試。強而有力的比較需要匹配的樣本、時間、光子、能量、儀器和分析預算。陰性數據、缺失樣本、獨立校準、來源識別和硬性限制仍然至關重要。母研究設計 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 記錄的是編輯淵源,而非實證證明。外部 DOI 與聲明的匹配以及專家科學審查仍在進行中,除非有獨立核查。 三篇散文研究之門演化與質量邊界 2000 個門中的每一個都與一個針對特定乾預措施的候選機制、正交見證、掩蔽對抗實驗、競爭解釋和後續拒絕路徑相匹配。必須區分詞彙重複檢查和獨立的語義審查:零個完全相同的重複段落並不能證明存在 2000 個科學上獨立的機制。這是研究設計工作版本;文章層級的文獻綜述、物理驗證和領域專家裁決仍待完成。 加入 STARLI 研究社區 Your voluntary contribution helps us open more research gates and cultivate new possibilities for future generations. https://ko-fi.com/starli33 Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. 33 | STARLI · White Rainbow Era RESEARCH COLLECTION / FLAGSHIPS 241–250 OF 300 Scientific Failure, Metrology and Independent Evidence at the Limit Flagship 13 Fission | Volume III | Author 33 | STARLI Research Design Working Edition v1.0 These ten research-design monographs move from nano-quantum failure physics and reconstructed microrobotic sampling truth to blinded biosensing, interlaboratory transfer, uncertainty budgets, reference-material commutability, manufacturing batch effects, contamination traceability, drift/biology separation and mission-failure classification. They propose testable experimental contracts, not observed new scientific laws or clinical results. The ten English working editions contain 7,770 pages, 300 mathematical plates, 820 chapter openings, 4,100 one-page studies, 2,000 Research Gates and 330 Phoenix Answer Embryos. Each Gate presents a three-part speculative letter—Origin, Extreme Extrapolation and Future Research Plan—without replacing measured falsification and independent physical witnesses. Structural counts do not establish scientific novelty. RESEARCH UNIT I · F241–F245 F241 NANO-QUANTUM RESEARCH SYSTEM FAILURE PHYSICS AT THE LIMIT — Focus: optical source ageing and actuator stuck-state fault. Direct witness: rate of hazardous events [h^-1]. Test against single-site repeatability without transfer. A live rival is detector gain drift; refuse release if a hazardous defect is released. F242 MICROROBOTIC SAMPLING TRUTH RECONSTRUCTION AT THE LIMIT — Focus: microchannel-wall adsorption and sorption-desorption memory. Direct witness: sample provenance recovery [percent]. Test against paper batch record plus endpoint inspection. A live rival is pipette volume error; refuse release if material balance or provenance does not close. F243 QUANTUM BIOSENSOR BLINDED CHALLENGE AT THE LIMIT — Focus: spin-coherence reference substitution and charge-state switching. Direct witness: prospective correct acceptance [percent]. Test against standard statistical process control with frozen limits. A live rival is microwave pickup; refuse release if a second site cannot reconstruct the qualification decision. F244 NANOROBOTIC INTERLABORATORY RING COMPARISON AT THE LIMIT — Focus: laser wavelength transfer and microscale thermal probe offset. Direct witness: absolute between-site measurement bias [unit]. Test against single-site repeatability without transfer. A live rival is laboratory temperature contrast; refuse release if a hazardous defect is released. F245 MICROSCALE SAMPLING UNCERTAINTY BUDGET AT THE LIMIT — Focus: volume-metering error and wall-loss uncertainty. Direct witness: prospective interval coverage [percent]. Test against paper batch record plus endpoint inspection. A live rival is liquid surface tension; refuse release if material balance or provenance does not close. SECOND RESEARCH UNIT / EVIDENCE, TRANSFER AND SUCCESSION RESEARCH UNIT II · F246–F250 F246 QUANTUM SENSOR REFERENCE-MATERIAL COMMUTABILITY AT THE LIMIT — Focus: matrix-dependent binding and fluorophore photobleaching. Direct witness: noncommutability bias [unit]. Test against standard statistical process control with frozen limits. A live rival is analyte concentration mismatch; refuse release if a second site cannot reconstruct the qualification decision. F247 NANOROBOTIC MANUFACTURING BATCH EFFECT IDENTIFICATION AT THE LIMIT — Focus: lithography mask alignment and coating pore defects. Direct witness: unselected qualified batch yield [percent]. Test against single-site repeatability without transfer. A live rival is postfabrication sorting; refuse release if a hazardous defect is released. F248 MICROFLUIDIC SAMPLING CONTAMINATION-SOURCE TRACEABILITY AT THE LIMIT — Focus: tubing adsorption reservoir and biofilm retention. Direct witness: correct source classification [percent]. Test against paper batch record plus endpoint inspection. A live rival is fresh-reagent contamination; refuse release if material balance or provenance does not close. F249 QUANTUM SENSOR SEPARATION OF DRIFT AND BIOLOGICAL CHANGE AT THE LIMIT — Focus: laser-frequency drift and matrix ionic-strength change. Direct witness: signal-source discrimination accuracy [percent]. Test against standard statistical process control with frozen limits. A live rival is true analyte fluctuation; refuse release if a second site cannot reconstruct the qualification decision. F250 NANOROBOTIC MISSION-FAILURE CLASSIFICATION AT THE LIMIT — Focus: magnetic actuation stall and robot collision cascade. Direct witness: unsafe false-release rate [percent]. Test against single-site repeatability without transfer. A live rival is optical tracking occlusion; refuse release if a hazardous defect is released. Scientific Boundary, Evidence & QA Status All work is restricted to traceable material, synthetic standards, permitted ex-vivo references, sealed microfluidic phantoms and nonclinical bench tests. Strong comparators require matched sample, time, photon, energy, instrument and analysis budgets. Negative data, missing specimens, independent calibration, source identity and hard stops remain essential. The mother research-design DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 documents editorial ancestry, not empirical proof. External DOI-to-claim matching and specialist scientific review remain pending where not independently checked. Three-Prose Research Gate Evolution & Quality Boundary Each of 2,000 Gates is paired with an intervention-specific candidate mechanism, orthogonal witness, masked adversarial experiment, rival explanation and successor refusal path. Lexical duplicate checks and independent semantic review must be distinguished: zero exact duplicated paragraphs would not prove 2,000 scientifically independent mechanisms. This is a Research Design Working Edition; article-level literature review, physical verification and domain-expert adjudication remain open. summary: Abstract (it) Il corpus in esame decostruisce il mito dell'applicazione standardizzata della prospettiva albertiana a base quadrata nell'opera di Leonardo da Vinci, proponendo un paradigma metrico-modulare fondato su evidenze geometriche oggettive e falsificabili. Attraverso l'analisi tridimensionale dell'Annunciazione, dell'Adorazione dei Magi e dell'Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di "righelli inseriti", evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un'architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d'indagine, basato su tecniche di retro-ingegneria CAD e sul "banale aristotelico", dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dal modulo 4:3 ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1 e 2:1:2) siano direttamente ricavabili dall'opera stessa. L'approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian square-based perspective in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of "inserted rulers," evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the "Aristotelian obvious," demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 4:3 module to the 1:4:1 and 2:1:2 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism.   Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare come una sequenza coerente: da uno spazio ancora concentrato e leggibile attraverso pochi regoli incorporati, a un’architettura figurata sempre più complessa, immersiva e ritmica. Sul piano metodologico, il corpus assume come principio guida il “banale aristotelico”: partire esclusivamente da ciò che nel dipinto è visibile, misurabile e geometricamente controllabile, senza ricorrere a simbologie arbitrarie, geometrie occulte o sovrastrutture interpretative non falsificabili. Il metodo combina osservazione diretta delle tracce figurative, geometria inversa, retro-ingegneria CAD e verifiche di coerenza antropometrica, zoometrica e architettonica; il punto decisivo è che gli elementi pittorici — bugne
title: Leonardo's Spatial Grammar: A CAD Reverse-Engineering Analysis Corpus: Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score
