summary: In 1513 the Castilian Crown began directing its conquistadors to read aloud the Requerimiento, a legal demand that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas submit at once to the authority of the Pope and the Spanish monarch. Composed by the jurist Juan López de Palacios Rubios, it was recited in Spanish or Latin, often out of earshot and to communities with no means of grasping its terms, and yet refusal, or the mere inability to consent, was treated as lawful grounds for war and enslavement. For the Taíno of the Caribbean it was the purest instrument of weaponized information asymmetry: a choice demanded under conditions that made informed choice impossible. This article formalizes the structural inverse of that instrument. It proposes a formal model of a peer-recognition currency in which the unit of account is perceived contribution value, issuance is fully endogenous, no sovereign intermediary exists, and the exchange space is structured by context-tagged domains rather than a flat signal architecture. The model's central claim is that when a boundedly rational agent simultaneously optimizes for accumulation, because a high balance signals competence and influence, and for expenditure, because high spending signals piety, humility, and reciprocal embeddedness, the resulting equilibrium is altruistic in the behavioral sense, not because altruism is designed into the incentive structure but because it is the only stable solution to the dual-motive optimization problem in a peer network with an observable ledger. A novel institutional role is defined: the epistemic witness, which informs without judging and without suggesting, preserving full independent agency while eliminating the information asymmetry between a participant and their own recognized contribution record. Where the Requerimiento compelled assent to terms that could not be read, the witness makes the terms of recognition fully legible to the participant before they act. The model is situated within the intersecting literatures of mechanism design, social epistemology, signaling theory, gift economy, commons governance, social compact theory, and cognitive behavioral economics. A candidate validation architecture is identified in which the model's predictions are falsifiable, and a formal appendix establishes the equilibrium result as a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium under perfect public monitoring. The paper concludes that the architecture described represents a distinct class of social exchange institution whose properties cannot be derived from any existing system and whose emergence of altruism as a structural rather than moral outcome has implications beyond the design of digital platforms.
title: E-Karma: A Formal Model of Peer-Recognition Currency, Dual-Motive Optimization, and the Structural Emergence of Altruism

summary: Erman and Sam asked whether every integral point on a pure ray of the Boij-Söderberg cone is the Betti table of a finite length module over k[x,y,z] or over the enveloping algebra U of the Heisenberg Lie algebra; Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu answered negatively. We study the point (1,2,2,1) on (0,e,3e,4e), excluded over k[x,y,z] and passing their test over U. It is realized by U/U(x^e,y^e) if and only if char k = 0 or char k >= 2e, and in characteristic 2 no module with at most one more relation than generators has finite length over U. In odd characteristic p we prove a criterion for pairs of forms with a central commutator, with explicit pure pairs for e = 0 or 1 modulo p, and pull-backs along endomorphisms of U. For the pairs x^e + alpha y^t, y^e + beta x^t we prove that coprimality conditions, two congruences and one scalar condition give the pure Hilbert function when p >= 2t, and the pure pair when one more coprimality holds; explicit short pairs are pure for p = 2e - 1 (every prime p >= 5) and for p = 2e - 3 (the primes below 2,000,000). Searches in weight-class strata, lists of forms, the filter for every exponent and the members fixed by the exchange of x and y settle the other pairs. The point is realized in every characteristic other than 2 for 2 <= e <= 16 except e = 11, where characteristic 3 is open. A census of the 220 rays with d_3 <= 12 over k[x,y,z] realizes the primitive point on 193 and excludes it on 12; in characteristic 0 the least counterexample has d_3 = 10. Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (branch develop). The paper does not claim a negative answer to Question 6.1 of Erman and Sam, which is due to Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu, and claims no priority for any other result.
title: Primitive Betti points over k[x,y,z] and the Heisenberg enveloping algebra: the point (1,2,2,1) on (0,e,3e,4e) fails only in characteristic 2 for 2 <= e <= 16 with e != 11, is realized whenever an odd prime p divides e(e-1) or equals 2e-1, and a census for d_3 <= 12

summary: Purpose: This study aims to examine the temporal structure of naval platform procurement rivalry between Türkiye and Greece during 1990–2025. By analysing the reciprocal relationships between naval platform deliveries and international orders in both countries, it investigates the lags at which procurement activities become most pronounced and the role of major naval procurement programmes in shaping these relationships. Method: Annual naval platform delivery and international order series compiled from SIPRI for 1990–2025 were analysed using ordinary least squares (OLS) models with 0–3-year lags and Newey–West standard errors. The findings were assessed through common-sample, full first-difference, distributed-lag, military expenditure control, order-date sensitivity, and period-window analyses, complemented by changes in fleet tonnage from the Power at Sea 2.0 dataset. Findings: In the baseline models, Greek deliveries are positively associated with Turkish deliveries two years later (β = 0.427) and Turkish orders one year later (β = 0.636), while Turkish deliveries are positively associated with Greek orders three years later (β = 0.395; BH-adjusted p < 0.05). All three selected coefficients remained positive after controlling for military expenditure, although their statistical support weakened following BH adjustment. Excluding the period corresponding to the MEKO-200 delivery window reduced the H1 coefficient to 0.102. In the full first-difference models, the H1 relationship persisted, whereas the order-related relationships were sensitive to the transformation. Conclusion: The strongest lagged association in Turkish–Greek naval procurement was observed between Greek ship deliveries and subsequent Turkish orders. This finding is consistent with Richardson’s action–reaction approach and Jervis’s security dilemma framework, which underpin the study’s theoretical perspective. The study demonstrates that naval procurement rivalry between the two countries exhibits asymmetric relationships in terms of direction and timing, particularly across the order and delivery stages.
title: The Temporal Structure of Turkish–Greek Naval Procurement Rivalry: Orders and Deliveries (1990–2025)

summary: Action-Research Lessons Learned from a Dis|mis Administrative Incident This book is an action-research study of lessons learned from a dis|mis administrative incident . It uses the incident as a situated case through which to examine how administrative uncertainty, informational asymmetry, technological mediation, institutional inertia, and contested interpretation can affect cognition, expression, dignity, and public trust. The project is guided by the attached work’s progression from “Fundamental Rights At Risk” and “On Partiality” to “On Liberty of Thinking,” “On Inner Peace & Recensions,” “Introducing CogOps,” “On Cognitive Health,” and the case studies on judicial impartiality, private affiliations, oath conflict, and SIS–Schengen transparency. The table of contents therefore provides the project’s conceptual route: from rights and institutional balance, through cognition and inner life, towards administrative, technological, and governance risks. The research does not present the personal account as conclusive proof of intentional wrongdoing. Rather, it treats the incident as a source of lessons learned, research questions, provisional concepts, and methodological warnings . The purpose is to distinguish observed events from interpretation, allegation, metaphor, and hypothesis while asking how comparable vulnerabilities might arise in other administrative environments. From rights to cognition The first part of the research begins with fundamental rights and institutional impartiality. In the chapter “On Partiality,” the attached work states: “It is also relational: whenever you are judged, a relationship is involved.” This proposition provides an important starting point for action research. An administrative decision is not only a technical act; it occurs within a relationship involving a citizen, a public agent, an institution, a body of law, and a surrounding informational environment. A failure of communication, an absence of reasons, a delay, or an inability to challenge a decision can therefore produce effects extending beyond the immediate administrative matter. The same chapter gives a second guiding image: “We are all equal under gravity.” Here, the balance functions as a non-technical symbol of equality, impartiality, and the need to prevent power from becoming detached from rights. Within the proposed research, this image is translated into questions about procedural fairness, equal access to information, the visibility of relevant affiliations, and the ability of affected persons to participate meaningfully in decisions concerning them. Liberty of thinking The chapter “On Liberty of Thinking” provides the closest conceptual foundation for the study of inner ecology. It describes writing and symbolic expression as a means of creating distance from an overwhelming or difficult experience: “Being able to formulate, express, and work on things symbolically helps us create emotional distance.” This observation is central to the action-research design. Recension, writing, drawing, multilingual expression, and documentary reconstruction are not treated merely as literary devices. They are used as practical research instruments through which an individual experience can be reviewed, organised, questioned, and made accessible to others. The chapter also describes expression as a form of shelter: “It was therefore a genuine shelter to be able to express ourselves through this ‘way of the pencil.’” Adapted to a CERREV-oriented research programme, this becomes a question about the conditions under which citizens and public agents can formulate disagreement without escalation. The research therefore examines whether accessible forms of expression can reduce informational dissonance, support self-correction, and create a more reliable basis
title: THE ASYLUM : From Soft Corruption to Disruptive Cognitive Operations: Reaching Inner Peace

summary: This publication specifies and documents a researcher-directed methodology for AI-assisted mathematical discovery, developed within the independent mathematical research program of Structural Stability Science (SSS). The methodology exhibits continuity with, but remains distinct from, the originating Structural Identification Method (SIM; Tonucci, 2026). It integrates scientific identification and continuing research direction, AI-assisted scientific interlocution, mathematical formalization and analytical development, computational implementation, dependency-preserving adjudication, and source-specific contribution provenance. Scientific interlocution consists of sustained technical exchange through which mathematical questions, interpretations, hypotheses, dependencies, counterexamples, proposed constructions, and candidate proof routes are examined. Researcher-directed decisions concerning problem selection, investigative objectives, mathematical evaluation, and research-program continuity remain distinguishable from AI-generated mathematical proposals, calculations, arguments, critiques, and technical representations. Both retain identifiable contributions under their documented source conditions. The methodology specifies two complementary records. The mathematical claim record preserves originating questions, hypotheses, conclusion scope, dependencies, supporting evidence, and verification findings. The source-to-contribution record preserves originating research-state continuity, earlier research artifacts, prompt-visible AI operations, researcher-directed decisions, branch reconciliation, attribution correction, and publication outcomes. These records retain distinct evidentiary functions. A prompt-response transcript documents operations expressed within an interaction; it does not independently establish the complete originating research state or the provenance of the continuing investigation. The originating mathematical investigation concerned order preservation under real extension, admissibility, counterexamples, and mathematical continuation. The documented research sequence subsequently encompassed adjoint observation gain, analytical extensions, exact reference-state rank, restricted Fourier observability, conditional Gramian transfer, time-dependent observability, high-frequency obstruction, nonlinear terminal-target correction, and Navier–Stokes continuation questions, together with the organization of Adjoint Gain Theory. These investigations retain their individual mathematical claims, source identities, verification conditions, and unresolved proof obligations. The scientific contribution is the specification and documented application of a researcher-directed methodology that preserves mathematical claim identity and research-process provenance while distinguishing scientific origination from substantive AI-assisted mathematical production. The publication does not independently certify the mathematical results of cited sources or amend the originating scientific identities, definitions, or conditions of SIM, SSS, or Dimensional Human Field Theory (DHFT). summary: This deposit contains synthetic benchmark inputs, mathematical specifications, computational artifacts, saved results, and validation materials supporting the manuscript “Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing.” The materials are organized into two distinct evidence streams. The expected-demand stream contains the five-group benchmark inputs and the archived computational materials used for the fixed-price operational model and the separate descriptive ALNS-LP/Hybrid comparison on generated instances. The realized-order stream documents Construction A, in which customer choices are frozen as indivisible 0.5-order-equivalent orders and vehicle routes are represented over physical address–slot visits. It compares only tariff policies B and C across baseline and low-Store-inventory scenarios using 500 paired replications (2,000 MILP solves in total). All benchmark data are synthetic. No real customer records, personally identifiable information, or confidential retailer data are included. The expected-demand and realized-order formulations are complementary but are not algebraically equivalent. The 52-policy finite comparison belongs to the expected-demand formulation; the realized-order experiment compares only B and C and does not re-evaluate all 52 policies. Net delivery contribution (NDC) excludes merchandise margins and should not be interpreted as total retailer profit. The archived computational outputs and validation materials are preserved as saved evidence. Their inclusion does not mean that the historical experiments were rerun during deposit preparation. Title clarification: The current manuscript supported by this deposit is titled “Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing.” The legacy expected-demand package contains a historical manuscript-context file bearing an earlier working title (version v0.3, dated 13 November 2026, explicitly marked “Not for submission”). This file is retained solely as historical provenance for the earlier computational evidence and does not represent the current manuscript or its title.
title: Research Data and Computational Materials for: Evaluating Delivery-Fee Policies in Omnichannel Retailing with Integrated Fulfillment and Last-Mile Routing

summary: AQUA-PRITHVI v2 expands the previously published metadata-only aquatic Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) corpus into a reusable multispectral research dataset, accompanied by harmonized in situ water-quality observations and reproducibility tools. The aquatic HLS corpus comprises 29,079 original compressed NPZ microshards containing 169,907 materialized patch-period samples. A quality-controlled catalog identifies 169,429 approved observations from 2,389 spatial patches across eight global regions during 2018–2024. Each approved observation references six HLS reflectance bands (blue, green, red, narrow NIR, SWIR1, SWIR2), 224 × 224 pixels at 30 m spatial resolution, together with valid-pixel and water masks. Spatially independent train, validation and test partitions are provided. The original NPZ archives may also contain excluded observations; only records identified as approved in the accompanying catalog should be treated as quality-controlled samples. The companion water-quality dataset integrates 2,107,785 harmonized observations from CONAGUA RENAMECA (Mexico) and AquaMatch (United States and territories), covering chlorophyll-a, total suspended solids, turbidity and water transparency where available. Source provenance, measurement units, censoring information and quality indicators are preserved. The release also provides Python tools for reading HLS tensors, preparing candidate water-quality labels and planning satellite-scene searches. These tools support the future construction of reproducible HLS–in situ matchup datasets. Important limitation: The harmonized in situ observations are not yet paired with satellite scenes. The monthly HLS composites used for aquatic domain-adaptive pretraining must not be interpreted as same-day satellite matchups. Valid supervised matchups require independent scene-level temporal matching, radiometric quality control and spatially independent evaluation. This resource is intended to support aquatic remote sensing, self-supervised representation learning, reproducible geospatial machine learning and research on satellite-based water-quality assessment. Original datasets retain their respective provenance, attribution and reuse conditions. Related Research Resources This dataset is part of the AQUA-PRITHVI research ecosystem , which integrates aquatic satellite observations, domain-adapted geospatial foundation models and reproducible scientific workflows. Trained foundation model — Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/freddyvillota/AQUA-PRITHVI-EO-2.0-300M-TL The repository provides the aquatic-domain-adapted Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL model weights, model documentation and loading instructions for aquatic multispectral representation learning and spectral reconstruction. Source code and scientific documentation — GitHub: https://github.com/FreddyHVG/AQUA-PRITHVI-DAPT-V2 The repository contains methodological documentation, preprocessing workflows, quality-control procedures, experimental results and reproducibility resources. Together, these resources enable researchers to access the aquatic HLS dataset, reuse the adapted foundation model, and reproduce or extend the associated scientific workflows. Note: The adapted model has been evaluated for aquatic spectral reconstruction. Its availability does not imply validated predictive performance for chlorophyll-a, suspended solids or other water-quality variables. summary: In 1513 the Castilian Crown began directing its conquistadors to read aloud the Requerimiento, a legal demand that the Indigenous peoples of the Americas submit at once to the authority of the Pope and the Spanish monarch. Composed by the jurist Juan López de Palacios Rubios, it was recited in Spanish or Latin, often out of earshot and to communities with no means of grasping its terms, and yet refusal, or the mere inability to consent, was treated as lawful grounds for war and enslavement. For the Taíno of the Caribbean it was the purest instrument of weaponized information asymmetry: a choice demanded under conditions that made informed choice impossible. This article formalizes the structural inverse of that instrument. It proposes a formal model of a peer-recognition currency in which the unit of account is perceived contribution value, issuance is fully endogenous, no sovereign intermediary exists, and the exchange space is structured by context-tagged domains rather than a flat signal architecture. The model's central claim is that when a boundedly rational agent simultaneously optimizes for accumulation, because a high balance signals competence and influence, and for expenditure, because high spending signals piety, humility, and reciprocal embeddedness, the resulting equilibrium is altruistic in the behavioral sense, not because altruism is designed into the incentive structure but because it is the only stable solution to the dual-motive optimization problem in a peer network with an observable ledger. A novel institutional role is defined: the epistemic witness, which informs without judging and without suggesting, preserving full independent agency while eliminating the information asymmetry between a participant and their own recognized contribution record. Where the Requerimiento compelled assent to terms that could not be read, the witness makes the terms of recognition fully legible to the participant before they act. The model is situated within the intersecting literatures of mechanism design, social epistemology, signaling theory, gift economy, commons governance, social compact theory, and cognitive behavioral economics. A candidate validation architecture is identified in which the model's predictions are falsifiable, and a formal appendix establishes the equilibrium result as a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium under perfect public monitoring. The paper concludes that the architecture described represents a distinct class of social exchange institution whose properties cannot be derived from any existing system and whose emergence of altruism as a structural rather than moral outcome has implications beyond the design of digital platforms.
title: E-Karma: A Formal Model of Peer-Recognition Currency, Cross-Domain Enforcement, and Structural Altruism

summary: Replication package for The Persistence of Taxonomic Entailments in Evolving Biomedical Ontologies. Version 2 rebuilds the study on every official release of nine OBO ontologies (698 releases of SO, PATO, HP, DOID, CL, ENVO, OBA, UBERON and MONDO; 872,217 incident entailments) and analyses 250 Gene Ontology releases separately. It contains the release lists with their provenance, the entailment survival corpora, the extraction and analysis code, all result tables and figures, the HPO annotation file and both code sets of the qualitative sample. The commit-sampled corpus of version 0.1 (311 snapshots of eight ontologies) is retained for the sensitivity analyses. code/verify_revision.py recomputes the corpus-level results and checks the manuscript against the released outputs (71 checks).
title: Replication package for The Persistence of Taxonomic Entailments in Evolving Biomedical Ontologies

summary: The following large derived data tables supplement our manuscript titled Local genetic control of DNA methylation variability is concentrated in quiescent and repeat-rich compartments of the human brain . Each file is a UTF-8 tab-separated value table with a header row; column definitions accompany each release. Supplemental Data 1—Per-region cell-type proportions. Multi-subject Single-cell (MuSiC) deconvolution estimates (sample × cell type) for caudate (n=487), dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) (n=500), and hippocampus (n=452) bulk RNA-seq samples, used as RNA-level covariates in the local methylation–transcriptional feature association models. WGBS estimates using single cell Methylation Deconvolution (scMD)-derived signatures are also included as a sensitivity analysis. Supplemental Data 2—VMR catalogue and coordinates. Per-region lists of the CpG sites retained after selecting the top 1% by inter-individual methylation SD, with the corresponding SD cut-off for each chromosome (n = 244,367 caudate; 211,168 dorsolateral prefrontal cortex [DLPFC]; 213,845 hippocampus). This data also provides per-region tab-separated BED-format files reporting genomic coordinates for each identified VMR (chr, start, end, number of intersecting CpGs, VMR identifier) in the Black American (BA) cohort (n = 11,530 caudate; 9,572 DLPFC; 9,497 hippocampus). Supplemental Data 3—Local genetic control scores.  Per-region relative local SNP contribution scores to methylation variation used for ranking each VMR, with estimates from a bayesian sparse linear mixed model (BSLMM), Haseman-Elsman (HE) regression, and elastic-net regression.  Supplemental Data 4—Cis-GREML sensitivity. Mean cis-GREML estimate across all VMRs in each brain region, with Spearman correlation estimates for the agreeance of cis -GREML estimates with local genetic control score deciles provided in Supplemental Data 3. Supplemental Data 5—GREML simulation benchmark. GCTA-GREML recovery of absolute local heritability on simulated phenotypes with known cis genetic variance fractions (h² ∈ {0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.40, 0.60, 0.80, 0.95}). Performance metrics include bias, root-mean-square error, 95% CI coverage, and Spearman correlation with true known genetic variance fractions.  Supplemental Data 6—Out-of-fold local SNP prediction. Results of out-of-sample prediction analyses evaluating the ability of local genetic variants to predict DNA methylation variation across VMRs in the caudate, DLPFC, and hippocampus. Performance metrics include out-of-fold R², prediction–phenotype correlation, root-mean-square error, mean absolute error, and the intercept and slope from regressing observed on predicted methylation. Sensitivity analyses include cross-region comparisons and cross-region donor count comparisons. Supplemental Data 7—Repeat and repressive chromatin architecture. Associations between relative local genetic influence on DNA methylation and genomic features associated with LINE/L1 repetitive annotations and H3K9me3, H3K27me3, and H3K27ac gappedPeak calls and ChromHMM 15-state chromatin annotations.  Supplemental Data 8—CpG-level cis -meQTL and VMR burden. summary: Code2Video uses agent-authored 3D proxies to guide video generation, enabling explicit control over structure and dynamics. However, how to construct proxies and prompts for optimal downstream quality remains underexplored, as do the capabilities and limitations of this paradigm. Through controlled experiments and blinded human evaluation, we study proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting. The results reveal task-dependent trade-offs: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while medium-grained proxies favor consistency. Physics simulation and proxy-aligned prompting further improve average quality. Guided by these findings, we introduce Coda-DaVinci, a task-adaptive agentic framework for Code2Video generation that selects between proxy-guided and direct generation, adapts modeling granularity to each entity, and coordinates simulation with proxy-grounded prompting. Its multi-agent harness preserves scene assets and guides repairs through visual inspection and independent review. Experiments demonstrate leading instruction following on VTR and scene consistency on R2M, improved physical plausibility over direct generation, and higher visual realism than the compared Code2Video baselines. Long-video evaluations further show gains in event structure and consistency across successive interactions, while revealing limitations in transition stability and adherence to scene settings.
title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video

summary: The increasing demand for intelligent, low-latency services in edge-cloud continuum systems poses new challenges for dynamic and efficient task offloading. We propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for distributed task offloading under partial observability, where each device offloads only a portion of its computation to a target edge server while executing the remaining portion locally (partial offloading). The problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), where each device independently learns an optimal policy under partially observable system states. To address the non-convexity, high-dimensional state space, and continuous action space, we develop a multi-agent Advantage-Weighted Actor-Critic (AWAC)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based computation offloading algorithm. The proposed method combines the stable policy updates of PPO with an advantage-weighting mechanism inspired by AWAC to emphasize higher-quality actions during training. To encourage cooperation without inter-device communication, a shared global reward aligned with system cost is employed. Extensive simulations demonstrate rapid convergence and significant improvement in overall system cost compared with baselines, e.g., Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Deep Q-Network (DQN).
title: Coordinated Offloading: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for the Edge-Cloud Continuum

summary: Effective travel planning requires handling multiple information sources, managing constraints, and tailoring recommendations to user preferences. While LLMs have introduced dynamic, context-aware decision-making, single-agent models often struggle with complex multi-step reasoning, constraint adherence, and modular execution. To overcome these limitations, we propose a hierarchical multi-agent framework where a supervising chatbot agent coordinates specialized agents for schedule validation, user query formulation, real-time data retrieval, and constraint-aware itinerary generation. By integrating LLM reasoning, external APIs, and iterative refinement mechanisms based on a deterministic, multi-dimensional scoring framework, our approach ensures adaptability, efficiency, and personalization. Evaluations on the well-known TravelPlanner benchmark demonstrate improvements in Budget Constraint planning by 10\%, wider constraints set-based planning by 25\%, and personalized planning results by 45\%. compared to the ReAct baseline. Our code is available at https://github.com/nimashaklaa/TravelPlanner_Research
title: LM-based Personalized Travel Planner

summary: Following AFTD's negative answer dated November 5, 2026, to Hausmann's Question 5.4 in Weighted Max Cut in Subcubic Graphs (arXiv:2611.05178v1, Section 5), we give a different counterexample with an exact residual-order calculation: the generalized Petersen graph GP(7,2) has odd girth five, but deleting any independent set leaves a component with at least four vertices. We prove this by classifying its maximal independent sets into five symmetry classes. The bound four is attained on this graph. The same classification gives an obstruction to the nonempty-independent-side version of Question 5.3; its printed quantifiers admit an empty-side solution.
title: Residual order four in GP(7,2): an alternative proof for Hausmann's Question 5.4 (arXiv:2611.05178v1, Section 5), after AFTD (2026)

summary: Written analysis plan for the study "Choosing a Donor Feeder: Sector Direction and the Cost of Zero-Shot Load-Forecast Transfer", submitted to GECOST 2027. The study measures the day-ahead forecast error of a model trained on one Moroccan distribution feeder and applied without retraining to another, across all 272 ordered pairs of 17 smart-metered feeders in four cities. This document records, for each of 15 analyses, the procedure and the reading rules that decide how its outcome is interpreted. Each section was written before the analysis it governs was run, so that outcomes could not be chosen after seeing the results. The plan covers: the replication gate; the transfer-ratio estimand and dyadic bootstrap; the seasonal-naive baseline; the donor-selection experiment; pooled same-sector models; alternative feeder labels; shape descriptors; the tuned local reference; weather covariates and two discriminating tests of weather sensitivity; second and summer evaluation blocks; few-shot local references; an additive feeder-identity comparison; a permutation test of sector labels; a partition analysis of where pooled transfer beats the naive; a second learner; and a zero-shot foundation-model baseline. Several pre-registered rules returned negative or inconclusive outcomes, and all are reported in the paper, including the finding that no donor-transfer configuration beats a seasonal naive and that a pretrained model outperforms every configuration measured. Data: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/malaklahmidi1/moroccan-feeder-load-time-series-30-min-cleaned
title: Analysis plan for "Choosing a Donor Feeder: Sector Direction and the Cost of Zero-Shot Load-Forecast Transfer"

summary: Abstract Purpose: Glioblastoma immunotherapy trials routinely assess tumor immunity based on a single surgical biopsy. We wanted to know how often biopsy location would reverse a relatively immune-rich or immune-poor classification. We also wanted to know whether CD8 T cell expression correlated with antigen-presenting gene expression and which immune programs remain consistent across regions after accounting for overall leukocyte infiltration. Methods: We scored 14 predefined immune expression programs across 75 magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)–localized, nonnecrotic biopsies from 19 patients with isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)–wild-type glioblastoma, alongside 122 microdissected samples from 10 glioblastomas and two multiregion hepatocellular carcinoma cohorts. Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) measured regional agreement relative to between-patient differences before and after adjusting for a 12-gene leukocyte score. Results: Regional scores fell on both sides of the fixed 141-biopsy reference mean in 7 of 19 patients (37%) for CD8 expression and 7 of 19 for leukocytes; only two crossed both. Within tumors, CD8 tracked supportive and inhibitory programs equally (mean r = 0.37 and 0.36) but barely tracked major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I) transcripts (r = 0.06). Leukocyte adjustment lowered median program ICC from 0.56 to 0.34. Interferon-associated expression retained the highest adjusted point estimate (0.70), though separation from MHC-I (0.47) remained uncertain; additional tumor-purity adjustment yielded similar ICCs (0.66 and 0.62). Conclusion: Biopsy location alone can reverse a glioblastoma’s relative immune-abundance classification. Measuring CD8, interferon, antigen-presentation, and inhibitory programs together across anatomically documented regions separates shared tumor-level features from local variation.
tags: Glioblastoma; Tumor microenvironment; Intratumoral heterogeneity; Tissue biomarkers; CD8 T lymphocytes; Interferon signaling
title: What a single biopsy reveals and misses about the glioblastoma immune microenvironment: Regional reproducibility of immune expression programs

summary: We extend Su's (2026) proof of Peter Bala's conjectures in OEIS A281428, COMMENTS, items 1–2 (displayed March 3, 2026), with factorial bounds and sharp onsets for the two accompanying examples. For a(n)=(2n)![x^(2n)]C(x), we prove v_p(a(n)) >= v_p((2n)!) for every prime p >= 5. The proof combines integral exponential coefficients with ordinary coefficients in Z[1/6], using the inverse cubic u-u^3/3=x. The exact eventual-zero onset modulo 385 is 6; modulo 27, the least eventual period is 18 and its earliest onset is 2. The same argument gives factorial bounds for every polynomial in the two differential-system solutions, including the companion A281427 and A052502.
title: Factorial bounds and sharp onsets for A281428: extending Su (2026) on Bala's COMMENTS, items 1–2

summary: Reconstructing a fragmentary manuscript of a known text rests on prior knowledge that editors apply implicitly and never evaluate. We formalise this knowledge as four priors (the reference text, the scribe's orthography and letter metrics, the physical geometry of the roll, and a rule for reading ambiguous ink) and combine them with large language model (LLM) agents and a constrained alignment model in a three-stage pipeline: reading, placement and layout. We evaluate it on the Greek Deuteronomy roll P. Fouad 266b (Rahlfs 848), which survives in some 140 fragments. An LLM agent, tuned by reflective prompt evolution, transcribes the plates and restores them against the reference text, missing 1 of 943 present letters on held-out plates. Fragments are placed by a banded, information-weighted edit distance with scribal substitution costs, chained across rows by a line-advance model and committed only above a confidence threshold. On a two-fold, plate-level split the placement model places 88% of held-out units (110 of 125) with no false placement (95% upper bound on the error rate about 3%). A deterministic constraint solver then rebuilds 85 columns that keep all 6,736 inked letters at their text positions. Unplaced units are mostly too short to place; the four that no setting places depart in wording from both reference texts, so the model's failures locate textual variants rather than errors. Transferred unchanged to a second roll, P. Fouad 266c (847), it places one unidentified fragment.
title: Reconstructing a Fragmentary Text from Priors: Language-Model Agents and Learned Alignment for P. Fouad 266b (848)

summary: Reconstruction-based anomaly detection on the NASA CMAPSS FD001 turbofan dataset. An LSTM autoencoder trained on healthy sliding windows is compared on 20 held-out engines with a cycle-count score, PCA reconstruction, an Isolation Forest and a one-class SVM, with bootstrap intervals over engines, paired comparisons of warning time at equal false-alarm rates and a causal alarm rule. The model is served through a typed FastAPI service and a Streamlit demo in a multi-stage Docker stack.
title: Anomaly Detection API: Autoencoder + FastAPI + Docker

Each part of this environment can change the image without providing evidence that a cellular mechanism has changed. The third STARLI organoid research family begins from this uncomfortable separation. It treats the material as a dynamic physical system, not merely the substrate beneath a cell. Nor does a beautiful 3D numerical surface count as a tissue experiment. The research program is deliberately nonclinical and prospective. Its purpose is to design independently observable questions that can survive blinded rivals and negative results. The five flagships F011 through F015 form distinct routes into this problem: stiffness-sensitive morphology, movement through a hydrogel, degradation timing, pore-controlled transport, and remodeling under delayed feedback. Each route contributes an observable with its own dimensions and failure modes. This family is a bridge between first-generation morphology and later functional chip systems, but no bridge is assumed to carry biological meaning unless another laboratory can test its supports. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. Neither can be averaged with a degradation half-life in days or a pore oxygen flux in moles per unit surface and time. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. ONE FAMILY, FIVE INCOMMENSURATE EVIDENCE STREAMS The first temptation in an integrated research civilization is to take five measurements and make one score. This is dangerous when their physical units have different meanings. A response in micrometers per kilopascal cannot be added meaningfully to a cell speed in micrometers per hour. Neither can be averaged with a degradation half-life in days or a pore oxygen flux in moles per unit surface and time. Even a dimensionless stability index requires an operational definition and a prespecified acceptable region. A scientifically defensible integration records the full vector and permits a hard stop when any essential component fails. Suppose a matrix allows quicker cell movement while the frequency of adverse changes in cell identity rises. An averaged numerical improvement might hide this problem. A research contract instead keeps separate thresholds for structural fidelity, independent physiology, matrix compatibility, calibrated uncertainty and process safety. The third family preserves the source atlas's thirty candidate formula positions and distinguishes generic test-logic equations from specific physical companion interpretations. For a quasi-elastic response, strain is the ratio of stress to modulus under a declared small-strain regime. That is not enough to describe a hydrogel that relaxes, erodes and remodels while cells exert force. Migration tracking must remove moving substrate landmarks; degradation kinetics must separate dry polymer mass from swollen water; oxygen flux must connect gradient, diffusivity, tortuosity and the actual pore network; remodeling stability must declare how long a bounded trajectory is monitored. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional models make sensitivities visible across registered parameter ranges. Each saved graph belongs to a CSV numeric grid and a reproducible Python reconstruction program, with units for all axes. They are proposed model objects, not measured cells. Their purpose is to help another investigator find a discontinuity, a nonidentifiable parameter combination or a wrong prediction before undertaking a biological assay. When a future experimental series disagrees with a curve, that discrepancy should be welcomed as evidence, not repaired away by changing the axis limits. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES AS A LIBRARY OF DISAGREEMENT The 200 Research Gates are not decorative questions. Each door begins with a distinct local investigation and asks why that problem matters, how the most serious competing explanation could account for the visible pattern, and what a successor could do with a simple independent witness. Across gel stiffness, migration, degradation, pore transport and remodeling, the language and scale change. Some doors begin from an intriguing contour, others from a physical contradiction or a failed denominator. Some describe a world in which swelling accounts for everything. Others imagine a pore network that is beautiful but disconnected, an apparently motile cell that is actually being carried by its gel, or a stable feedback trace that conceals tissue identity loss. Their future plans ask for blind sample exchange, matched budget controls, withheld perturbations, new batches, sealed negative specimens and automatic refusal. A Gate has done its work when it leaves a person outside the current research group with enough information to prove the attractive explanation wrong. The failure scenario is therefore not an embarrassment; it is an inheritance. The archive should preserve it with the same care as the favored result. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX EMBRYOS AND A CIVILIZATION THAT CAN STOP The Phoenix possibilities develop small prototypes rather than claiming completed machines. Their names suggest instrument exchanges, counterfactual matrix libraries, pore-network tomography challenges, mechanical memory loops, independent material reference standards and new methods for storing negative outcomes. Each idea includes a minimum test and a reason to retire it. In a mature autonomous experimental environment, this has consequences beyond documentation. Controllers must abstain when calibration disappears. Hardware or material intervention cannot proceed merely because a prediction model is confident. Human permission, biological source provenance and contamination controls remain external authority constraints. A system that pauses when its assumptions collapse is often more useful than one that always returns an answer. The same principle applies to writing and publication: a research program can be inspirational without presenting synthetic models as achieved biological capabilities. The open scientific record grows stronger when authors state what has not yet been built, measured or validated. THE SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE The supplied STARLI F18 organ-on-chip monograph reminds this family of a central distinction: geometric precision is not physiological function. In a material-focused family, the same argument has multiple forms. An excellent modulus map is not morphogenesis. A migrating centroid is not necessarily a migrating cell. A fall in wet weight is not always polymer cleavage. A large apparent flux is not necessarily oxygen supply to living tissue. And a stable material signal is not proof of organ-specific homeostasis. Published work on organoid hydrogels, synthetic matrices, viscoelasticity and dynamic mechanics offers methodological precedents. Those sources do not experimentally verify the five new STARLI couplings. This research family offers a plan for making such claims testable, including measurements, strong baselines, uncertainty accounting, data reconstruction and stopping conditions. The long-term goal is not to build a library of conclusions that cannot be questioned, but an open architecture of precise experimental doors. Each generation should be free to improve the questions, reject a mistaken mechanism and keep whatever remains genuinely useful. Let beauty have the ability to continue happening. summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π (x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half ( π ), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The author believes that this work can become a proof of the Riemann hypothesis; the missing step is to show that the unity of the process makes the transfer of the observer a symmetry. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. The missing step is also written as a statement about positivity: from Mertens' square 2(1 + cos θ )², which pushes the zeros away from 1, to the square of Weil's energy, which must hold them on ½ and forbid pairs of zeros on opposite sides of the circle. The work rests on classical results — Pell–Lagrange, Legendre's sieve, the explicit formula of Riemann and von Mangoldt — and proposes a new linking of them: the geometry of the seam as a model of the process linking the primes. The author's answer to Riemann's question is geometric: on each range chosen in a definite way, the process of the link of the primes is seen as the unit circle and a sinusoid around it; for his work the author regards this answer as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and what in it is accepted as an initial

summary: This dataset accompanies the manuscript entitled "Cross-model TEAD inhibitor resistance programs and their clinical associations in pleural mesothelioma". The Excel workbook provides derived supplementary data supporting the cross-model analysis of TEAD inhibitor resistance in pleural mesothelioma. It includes: Table S1: Study cohorts, sample characteristics, and analysis roles. Table S2: Fixed gene-program memberships and scoring definitions. Table S3: Cross-model differential expression results for 15,508 comparable genes and pathway enrichment analyses. Table S4: Patient malignant-cell state comparisons and program coverage. Table S5: TCGA-MESO histological associations, expression correlations, and overall survival analyses. Table S6: Sensitivity analyses, model diagnostics, and spatial transcriptomic results. The public dataset retains the 223-gene Shared_up program, the 200-gene Hallmark EMT set, and the reported statistical results. A total of 675 third-party tS/tE and meS/meE gene-membership records were excluded from the public workbook because redistribution permissions could not be independently confirmed. Their original sources and reconstruction procedures are documented in the accompanying README. The dataset contains derived research results, not raw sequencing data or directly identifying patient information. Source datasets, analytical conventions, attribution, and reuse information are described in README.txt. The associated manuscript was prepared for submission to Clinical and Translational Oncology.
title: Derived supplementary data for cross-model TEAD inhibitor resistance programs in pleural mesothelioma

summary: Version v6.0-jbi accompanies the submission of the article to the Journal of Biomedical Informatics (Elsevier). It adds manuscript_jbi/, which builds the shortened journal version (body of about 5,980 words, two figures, six tables) and its supplementary material from the v5.0 manuscript, a graphical abstract (figures/Graphical_abstract_JBI_DNFR.png), and check_numbers.py, which verifies that every number in the journal version occurs in the v5.0 manuscript or supplement generated from the result files. It also adds the ratings of a second, blinded clinical rater (a physician; results/expert_review2_filled.xlsx with the rater’s name withheld, and the agreement and discrimination statistics in results/expert_review2.json). Models, data and the main results are unchanged from v5.0. Code, derived data and result files for Differentiable Neuro-Fuzzy Reasoning (DNFR), a path-based link predictor that learns degree-aware edge memberships, a Schweizer–Sklar t-norm per metapath and metapath reliabilities, and aggregates paths by noisy-OR, used as an instrument for a controlled component analysis on medical knowledge graphs. Tasks: drug repurposing in Hetionet v1.0 and PrimeKG, disease–symptom prediction in Hetionet and in the graded health knowledge graph of Rotmensch et al. (2017), and a secondary test on a NHANES fuzzy relation, under leave-dyad-out random and disease-centred splits. Comparators: fixed t-norms, component ablations, restarts of the t-norm parameter, DWPC with logistic regression (with and without degree and prior features), a degree-preserving edge prior, popularity, AnyBURL, truncated and soft-thresholded SVD and knowledge graph embeddings. Version v4.0 (fourth revision) completes 10 leave-dyad-out splits on Hetionet compound–treats–disease for the fixed Hamacher product, fixed degree terms, annealing, frozen memberships, DNFR 2.0, the shared and fixed t-norm parameters and AnyBURL; adds an ablation without metapaths that contain the target relation, a fact-level attribution of DWPC-LR next to DNFR's, the evidence share by metapath class, an information-content check with matched spread, a profile of the t-norm parameter extended to p > 0 and run on Hetionet disease–symptom, a tuning grid for NBFNet, a script that re-runs a key result from a clean checkout (scripts/verify_clean.sh), and the sheet for a clinical assessment of the explanations (dnfr/expert_sheet.py, dnfr/expert_summary.py). The secondary NHANES test was removed from the article. Version v3.0-rev3 (third revision) added DNFR 2.0, four refinements tested one at a time and in combination (overlap-aware aggregation, Gumbel-softmax operator choice, an information-content hub discount and membership annealing), a fixed t-norm selected on validation data, a converged L-BFGS profile of the t-norm parameter, an unbounded parameterisation, a compact NBFNet baseline, an exact edge-level Shapley attribution of the explanations, a mechanistic classification of the drug-repurposing explanations, a sparsity variant that keeps the target relation, and 10 leave-dyad-out splits for the main comparisons on Hetionet compound–treats–disease, Hetionet disease–symptom and the graded health knowledge graph. Version 1.1.0 (second revision) added a profile analysis of the t-norm parameter, training without early stopping, additional splits, equivalence tests, the edge prior, share-matched and edge-level explanation tests, unit tests and the script that builds the manuscript from the statistics files. Includes per-query ranks for every method and split, trained models, path explanations, and the statistics files from which every number in the manuscript is read. Hetionet and PrimeKG are downloaded by download_data.py with MD5 checks.
title: Code and derived results for: Which parts of a neuro-fuzzy path reasoner should be learned? A controlled component analysis on medical knowledge graphs

summary: Electrons can change subband in quantum transport, holes can be solved by it too, the package makes quality triangle meshes, the quantum channel on meshes keeps band steps where the mesh puts them, and scattering lifetimes and mobility of a 2D gas are computed from its own wavefunction. The examples print what they printed before, except example 58 (the quantum channel on a mesh, now closer to the tensor grid); examples 62 to 65 are new. Added Device.negf(..., coupled_modes=M) : NEGF in coupled mode space, the lowest M states of every column joined by their overlaps, so electrons change subband where the channel's profile across it changes; with all modes it is the full 2D problem (ballistic only). kpenvelope.negf adds Slab , slab_transport and lead_surface_green (leads by decimation). Device.negf(..., carrier="holes") : the holes of a QuantumChannel with holes=(m_z, m_inplane, ...) , with or without scattering, uncoupled or coupled; Slab(mass_x=) for a mass along x of its own. kpenvelope.mesh.quality_mesh(regions, h, min_angle) : quality meshes of polygon regions by Delaunay refinement (every boundary and interface an edge, no node in a segment's diametral circle, smallest angle up to 34 degrees, a size field). kpenvelope.scattering.Subband : transport and quantum lifetimes and the mobility of one subband from acoustic phonons, alloy disorder, interface roughness (Gaussian or exponential correlation) and screened charged impurities (sheets or profiles), with your material numbers. Changed The quantum channel on meshes: the material on each sample of a line is the mean over its share of the line. Before, a node on a band step took its whole share from the one region it belongs to, which moved the step by up to half a spacing, differently on each line: on a quality mesh the confined sheet was 1.6 to 2.0 percent off a fine tensor grid at every mesh size; now 0.54, 0.20 and 0.10 percent at 1, 0.5 and 0.25 nm. On a mesh made from a tensor grid with a band step inside the window, the result now differs from the tensor grid's by that half-spacing effect of the tensor grid. Device(grid=...) refuses nodes closer than 1e-6 nm with a clear message (a near-duplicate node made the Poisson solve fail). Not included (see docs/limits.md) Scattering in coupled mode space; phonon self-energies in NEGF; NEGF on triangle meshes; both carriers in NEGF at once. Polar optical phonon and intersubband scattering in the lifetimes. The hot-electron model's limit at zero relaxation time with velocity saturation, the plasma's own chemistry, oxide shapes that follow the flow, elasticity, electronic stopping beyond Lindhard-Scharff, tunneling paths that bend with the field, tunneling and heat inside one Newton solve, and the Peltier heat in Fermi-Dirac form are as in 0.26.0. The app does not have the new features yet. Checks (tests) 15 new tests (372 in all; docs/checks.md has the tolerances): the leads by decimation against the exact chain lead; coupled mode space against the dense real-space inverse, mode counting, the sum of chains without mixing, and the uncoupled device; holes against the mirror image of electrons and the QuantumChannel's holes; a slab with a mass along x of its own; the quality mesh's angles, areas, conformity and diametral circles, and a ring resistor converging at second order; the quantum channel on a quality mesh against a fine tensor grid; the scattering rates against closed forms (Fang-Howard and square-well overlaps, Price's acoustic rate, the alloy rate), an independent integral with the closed-form Fang-Howard form factors, the far-away-charge limits, the Hellmann-Feynman shift of a level, and the thermal average. All 65 documented examples were rerun.
title: kpenvelope: interface charges, misfit-dislocation charge, two-dimensional electron and hole gases and device curves of wurtzite nitride stacks, with a self-consistent six-band k.p solver

summary: This package reproduces every number, table and figure in the article "Cheaper Hospitals or Fewer Services? Finance, Service Scope and the Falling Price of Private Finance Initiative Health Contracts in the United Kingdom" (submitted to the Journal of Health Economics) and in its Supplementary File 1. title: Replication package for: Cheaper Hospitals or Fewer Services? Finance, Service Scope and the Falling Price of Private Finance Initiative Health Contracts in the United Kingdom

summary: A finite record can leave equally many states possible after each observation and still resolve one question perfectly while giving little information about another. For a specified answer map, the nonempty cells of its joint table with the record characterize exact recovery. If a state law is given, the largest cell mass in each row determines optimal one-guess accuracy. If only the record law and a statewise loss are given, row minima and maxima give attainable bounds on the mean loss. We prove the relations between fiber size, mass and conditional diversity, including their dependence on uniform input, and give finite witnesses to their limits. For composition and updates, we determine when a count or a next record follows from the retained information. Two dice give records of the same diversity but accuracies of one and one sixth for the same question. In an office occupancy series, an added sensor bit lowers training error, yet a fixed decoder incurs more errors in both test periods. Declaration of AI Use ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic) assisted in preparing and checking the materials used for this work. AI was used for drafting, mathematical cross-checks, and preparation of figures and verification code. The author retains responsibility for the manuscript and its conclusions. These checks do not constitute independent peer review.
title: Re-Phase Vol.4.7: Records for Required Answers — Effective Diversity, Exact Recovery, and Sharp Loss Bounds

summary: 中文摘要 空间旋转、观察者涡度、内部规范场的旋转结构以及时空挠率往往被放在同一概念框架中,但它们在对称性、规范变换和动力学上并不等价。本文综合一系列关于 “ 真实旋转自由度能否构成普通质量引力之必要动力学来源 ” 的模型检验,首先指出球对称单一时间类矢量场满足 ,因而其投影涡度为零;特定平直空间切片上的纯环向差分旋转度规还受到弱能量条件与零能量条件的限制。其次,以已知 Einstein–Yang–Mills 和 Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs 模型为对照,说明内部规范旋转能够形成正则、球对称的自引力构型,但并未导出独立的度规引力动力学。本文的主要技术焦点是固定空间三标架下三支 Abelian 横向矢量场的静态交换:当源仅由标量密度线性、局域解析地构成,并同时满足守恒及对角   不变性时,源顶点在零动量至少含一阶导数,树级源 — 源核不具有非零系数的   牛顿红外极点。与此对照,非局域横向投影   可在正的自由场能量下产生吸引性   静态核;带质量 Proca 空间源也可产生吸引的 Yukawa 势,但伴随非守恒源、优选切片或奇异的无质量极限。这些结果排除或限定了若干最小模型,却没有构造出局域、协变、健康且满足红移、光偏折、等效原理与引力波要求的完整旋转起源引力理论。 Abstract   — We critically synthesize a sequence of model-level investigations into whether a genuine rotational degree of freedom can be a necessary dynamical origin of ordinary gravity. Spatial coordinate rotation, the vorticity of a chosen timelike congruence, internal gauge curvature and spacetime torsion are treated as distinct objects. A spherically symmetric single timelike one-form is hypersurface orthogonal, whereas familiar Einstein–Yang–Mills–Higgs solutions demonstrate that non-Abelian internal structure can coexist with regular, positive-energy self-gravitating configurations without establishing a new origin of metric dynamics. Our central conditional result concerns a static triplet of positive-kinetic Abelian vector fields on a fixed spatial slice. If their conserved sources are linear in a scalar mass density, analytic near zero momentum and invariant under a diagonal , the tree-level source–source kernel has no Newtonian  infrared pole. A spatially nonlocal transverse-projection source provides an explicit counterexample to any broader impossibility claim: it produces an attractive static interaction, but presupposes an inverse Laplacian and a preferred slicing. Massive Proca couplings admit additional attractive Yukawa examples while raising different consistency issues. None of these constructions establishes a complete local, covariant and observationally viable theory in which spatial rotation necessarily generates all gravitational phenomena.

title: 空间旋转能否成为引力的动力学起源?——从球对称涡度约束到多场交换核的条件性障碍与反例

Physical/mathematical, semantic, refutability and DOI reviews remain partial; shared prose persists in unchanged chapters. Calibrated laser Doppler and microfluidic flow references expose correlated temperature artifacts; shared confounding and uncalibrated instruments defeat a positive result. An inert hydrogel and calibrated scaffold separate water-driven appearance from load-bearing tissue competence; cell injury or gel rupture triggers refusal. F47 BIODEGRADABLE NANOMATERIALS AND CUTANEOUS SAFETY AT THE LIMIT — Tests degradation-product mass balance and cellular compatibility using blind product identification and solvent-only controls. Gravimetric closure and chemically identified standards distinguish true breakdown from simple particle fragmentation; unknown products or toxic intermediates cannot be ignored. F48 CUTANEOUS INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING AND BARRIER HOMEOSTASIS AT THE LIMIT — Tracks cell-stratified inflammatory-marker changes with independent protein assays. Composition-matched qPCR and cytokine verification test whether cell-mixture shifts mimic signaling change; increasing inflammation or loss of barrier integrity invalidates favorable interpretation. F49 EPIDERMAL RENEWAL KINETICS AND SKIN DIFFERENTIATION AT THE LIMIT — Measures labeled-cell transit from basal layers to the surface with blinded time tracking and independent histology. title: BioLaserTwin: Physics-Based Biophotonic Cavity Simulator, Feature Extractor, and Inversion Suite

summary: M2-US: A Large-scale Multi-domain and Multi-task Ultrasound Image Dataset Ultrasound imaging is widely used across various clinical applications due to its real-time imaging capabilities, portability, and cost-effectiveness. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated considerable potential in ultrasound image analysis. However, the development of generalizable AI models remains challenging due to variations in imaging devices, acquisition protocols, anatomical structures, and clinical tasks. Most existing ultrasound datasets focus on specific anatomical regions or individual prediction tasks, limiting their applicability to multi-domain and multi-task learning. To address these limitations, we introduce M2-US , a large-scale, multi-domain and multi-task ultrasound image dataset comprising 67,620 ultrasound images collected from publicly available datasets and retrospective clinical cohorts. The dataset covers more than 30 anatomical structures and pathological targets across diverse clinical applications, including maternal–fetal, cardiac, vascular, abdominal, pulmonary, breast, thyroid, and gynecological ultrasound imaging. The images originate from multiple countries and were acquired using approximately 24 ultrasound scanner models from more than 10 manufacturers, providing substantial diversity in imaging conditions and clinical settings. M2-US supports 26 subtasks across four major ultrasound image analysis tasks : segmentation (12 subtasks), classification (9 subtasks), object detection (2 subtasks), and landmark-based regression (3 subtasks). The dataset provides task-specific annotations, including pixel-wise segmentation masks, image-level classification labels, object bounding boxes, and anatomical landmark coordinates. All data are organized into predefined training, validation, and testing partitions, accompanied by standardized CSV metadata files to facilitate reproducible model development and evaluation. M2-US is designed to support research on task-specific deep learning models, multi-task learning, transfer learning, foundation model adaptation, and cross-domain generalization in ultrasound image analysis. By integrating diverse anatomical targets, imaging conditions, and annotation types within a unified benchmark, M2-US aims to facilitate the development and systematic evaluation of more robust and generalizable ultrasound AI methods. Dataset website: https://m2-us.github.io/ GitHub repository: https://github.com/m2-us/m2-us Baseline experiments: https://github.com/m2-us/experiments License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
title: A Large-scale Multi-domain and Multi-task Ultrasound Image Dataset
