summary: Abstract This document gives a technical and functional description of Algorithmic Logic Fingerprints (ALF): a way to verify that an AI model or algorithm in production still makes the decisions that were reviewed and approved, and to stop its output from taking effect if it does not. The problem. Current AI trust mechanisms prove identity and origin, not behaviour: Model signing (OpenSSF Model Signing, led by Google, NVIDIA and HiddenLayer; NVIDIA NGC signed models) proves which file a model is. Attestation and transparency logs (for example Apple Private Cloud Compute) prove which software a server runs. Neither shows what the model actually decides. A model can be fine-tuned, quantised, wrapped in a prompt or proxy layer, or replaced behind the same name or signature, and an AI agent can act on its output before anyone notices. How it works. Fingerprint generation. A compact cryptographic fingerprint of decision behaviour is created without access to source code, model weights or training data. For machine-learning models it is built by sampling decision boundaries. For rule-based or traditional code it is built from normalised control-flow and decision structure. Sealed-probe verification. In the highest-assurance mode, the model is tested with a sealed set of inputs that the computing system cannot see in advance. Four views must match together: decision boundaries, monotonicity and consistency, constraint activation, and constraint topology. A different model wrapped to imitate the approved one cannot pass all four. Approved-fingerprint registry. Each approved model or algorithm version has a reference fingerprint that can be checked at any time. Run-time check at the point of effect. Inside a trusted execution environment (for example a confidential VM or a confidential GPU), the live fingerprint is compared with the approved one after computation finishes and before the output is used. Fail-closed enforcement. If the fingerprint does not match, approval is automatically invalidated and the output is withheld. The capability needed to act (send, pay, move, transmit) is not released. Validation receipts. Each decision produces a tamper-evident receipt anchored in a ledger, for audit and incident analysis. Where it applies. The same mechanism applies to AI agents and model-serving platforms, payment and digital-currency systems (including offline wallets), vehicles and robots, and satellites. It complements existing technology rather than replacing it: model signing and model registries (NVIDIA NGC, Google Kaggle); verifiable and confidential AI clouds (Apple Private Cloud Compute, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, AWS, and NVIDIA, Intel and AMD confidential hardware); agent platforms (Google, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services); payment flows (Visa, Mastercard, PayPal, Ant Group); vehicle software governance under UN Regulation 156; Chinese AI platforms (Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance, Tencent, Huawei, Zhipu AI). It also gives a technical signal for the EU AI Act's substantial-modification rule and for China's generative AI filing regime, both of which depend on knowing whether the deployed system is the one that was assessed. Source disclosure. This architecture is described in International Application PCT/IB2026/053385 (filed 07.04.2026, published 04.06.2026 as WO/2026/115520; https://patentscope.wipo.int/search/en/detail.jsf?docId=WO2026115520 ). That application claims priority from Indian applications 202531130168, 202631007467 and 202631018571. The related application PCT/IB2026/055615 (filed 4 June 2026, publicly disclosed 16 July 2026) claims priority from it. Author: Sangam Das. summary: The Boundary-Coupled Threat-Transduction Framework (BCTTF) is proposed as a cross-domain theoretical architecture for examining how an element initially external to a system can become incorporated into the system's effective or identity-related boundary, and how a threat to that element may subsequently be processed as a threat to the system itself. The framework retains two principal branches: a subjective-agent branch, centred on identity-related defence in human systems, and a mechanical and automated branch, centred on operational dependency and fault response. Its central question concerns why a system may defend a deeply connected external element even when the system has no immediate direct material or physical-survival requirement to protect that element. The framework formalizes a twelve-stage default mechanism, eighteen analytical layers, two primary case studies, branch-specific mathematical models, parameter-estimation procedures, operational definitions, falsifiability conditions, and a computational simulation design. A supplied Python implementation was executed using synthetic data only. Its parameter-recovery and held-out prediction results demonstrate numerical consistency under the script's own data-generating assumptions; they do not establish empirical validity, universality, or originality. The manuscript therefore distinguishes the proposed general mechanism from branch-specific implementations and distinguishes synthetic model verification from empirical validation. boundary incorporation; threat transduction; identity-related defence; operational coupling; homeostasis; fault response; parameter estimation; system dynamics; computational simulation; cross-domain modelling

summary: Abstract Introduction: The polymeric product obtained in the presence of microheterogeneous catalytic systems is characterized by a fairly reasonable molecular weight distribution (MWD), resulting from kinetically non-equivalent active centers (ACs) in the system that initiates the polymerization process. The nature and composition of the ACs are determined by defining and solving an inverse problem in MWD formation. This problem is acute because revealing the nature of the kinetic heterogeneity explains the changes in molecular parameters and product consumption for different catalyst compositions and propagation modes in polymerizations. Objective: This study aimed to develop methods and algorithms for interpreting gel chromatograms to analyze the kinetic heterogeneity of an industrially obtained polymeric product in microheterogeneous catalytic systems. Methods: The solution method assumes that the MWD formed is a superposition of distributions inherent to each type of AC. Since the problem in the final formulation refers to Fredholm integral equations of the first type, the regularization method of A. N. Tikhonov is used for its numerical solution, with the original problem being preliminarily discretized. This methodology and the developed software algorithms were used to determine the kinetic heterogeneity of catalytic systems containing titanium and neodymium. Results and discussion: MWD analysis revealed two types of CAs with an average molecular weight of A̅T1 - lnM = 11.3 and B̅T1 - lnM = 13.2 in the titanium catalyst, and three types of A̅Nd - lnM = 11.1, B̅Nd - lnM = 12.7 and C̅Nd - lnM = 14 for the neodymium catalyst, respectively. Conclusions: Repeated computational experiments under different polymerization conditions and requirements for the preparation of a catalytic system allow us to reveal a relationship with the resulting heterogeneity of CAs. It allows us to define and solve problems related to controlling the molecular characteristics of the resulting polymer product. A natureza e a composição dos ACs são determinadas definindo e resolvendo um problema inverso na formação de MWD. Este problema é agudo porque revelar a natureza da heterogeneidade cinética explica as mudanças nos parâmetros moleculares e de consumo do produto para diferentes composições de catalisador e modos de propagação em polimerizações. Objetivo: o presente estudo teve como objetivo desenvolver métodos e algoritmos de interpretação de cromatogramas em gel para analisar a heterogeneidade cinética de um produto polimérico obtido industrialmente em sistemas catalíticos microheterogêneos. Métodos: o método de solução parte do pressuposto de que o MWD formado é uma superposição de distribuições inerentes a cada tipo de ACs. Como o problema na formulação final se refere às equações integrais de Fredholm do primeiro tipo, o método de regularização de A. N. Tikhonov é usado para sua solução numérica, com o problema original sendo preliminarmente discretizado. Esta metodologia e os algoritmos de software desenvolvidos foram usados para determinar a heterogeneidade cinética de sistemas catalíticos contendo titânio e neodímio. Resultados e discussão: a análise MWD revelou dois tipos de ACs com um peso molecular médio de A̅T1 - lnM = 11.3 e B̅T1 - lnM = 13.2 no catalisador de titânio, e três tipos de A̅Nd - lnM = 11.1, B̅Nd - lnM = 12.7 e C̅Nd - lnM = 14 para o catalisador de neodímio, respectivamente. summary: Software overview ComunicELA is an assistive communication application developed in a bachelor’s thesis at Universidade da Coruña in collaboration with AGAELA and the NTT DATA Diversity and Technology Chair. It provides customisable communication boards controlled through eye movements and blinks, with speech synthesis for the composed messages. Optional integration with Google Gemini supports sentence conjugation. Package contents This source archive preserves repository commit b0793c853177cfb02eed9520cc2bf8e9dbf98d2a . It includes 275 original repository files: Python source, requirements, interface resources, communication boards, training scripts, model files and results spreadsheets. The thesis PDF is excluded from this software package. Archive provenance and a file manifest are added; the original code and licence notices are preserved. Download and reconstruction The ZIP is distributed as seven numbered byte segments ( .part001 to .part007 ). Download every segment and ComunicELA_README_DOWNLOAD.txt , join the segments in numeric order using the documented commands, then extract the resulting standard ZIP. The reconstructed ZIP has 24,287,190 bytes and MD5 cc87f80dd066083f91df13d3d2d23c6a . Individual segments cannot be extracted separately. Requirements and usage Consult README.md and requirements.txt . The Python entry point is main.py . The README also describes a separately distributed Windows executable and board customisation. The executable is not included in this source archive. Google Gemini features require the user’s own API credentials, configured through the environment; no credentials are included. Access and licence The software is distributed under GNU GPL version 3, as declared in the source repository. Retain the original copyright and licence notices and consult LICENSE . Third-party components remain subject to their respective terms. Academic context and contributions The associated bachelor’s thesis was authored by Pablo Páramo Telle and supervised by José Joaquim de Moura Ramos, Luís María Hervella Nieto and Marcos Ortega Hortas. Student implementation and academic supervision are distinguished here for transparency. Universidade da Coruña thesis record . Preservation and reuse Archiving a specific source version with a persistent identifier, documented dependencies and usage information supports transparent inspection, reproducibility and reuse of the technical result. The deposit documents the software associated with the thesis; it does not establish clinical certification or independently measured adoption. Source and citation Development repository . Please cite this version-specific software deposit and the associated thesis when using the work in research.

summary: A pre-registrable experimental protocol for testing whether the apparent "self" of an LLM agent behaves as a localised, persistent substrate ( ātman ), as a process assembled from the five aggregates with no fixed substrate ( anattā ), or as a surface regularity with no internal organisation (null). It specifies four studies: (1) localisation probes, with targeted, mean and random feature ablation and capability controls; (2) framing invariance of self-descriptions across system personas, languages, registers and role-play framings; (3) aggregate-wise decomposition of activations (rūpa, vedanā, saññā, saṅkhāra, viññāṇa); and (4) impermanence and re-composition across sessions with external memory. It treats self-reports as evidence only when activation-level probes agree with them, and controls for instruction-following, e.g. a model that says "I have no self" after a Buddhist prompt. Provenance. The author wrote this protocol by June 2026 and kept it private in his Notion workspace, attached to the lab page "2026-06-10 – Wadduwage lab summer work plan" under the "citta transformer" project. summary: The analytical modeling of a plasma wakefield driven by a relativistic proton beam is an element in optimizing advanced plasma-based acceleration schemes. In this work, we present a 1D nonlinear fluid framework under the quasi-static approximation to describe the wake potential excited by a positively charged proton driver which attracts background electrons into a density compression rather than expelling them. We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using a two-bunch scheme, our piecewise-event integration model is validated to high numerical accuracy ($\sim 10^{-11}~\mathrm{GV/m}$) against independent phase-space quadrature of cold-fluid solutions, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ ramped micro-bunch train with fixed $2\pi$ spacing, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a piecewise analytical scaling model. This formulation maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic post-train residual wake plateau, which is determined exactly by the conserved vacuum Hamiltonian invariant evaluated at the final bunch-train exit state. Furthermore, the framework estimates the onset of nonlinear phase-slippage that arrests growth and causes the transient wakefield overshoot to decay toward the residual horizon. Providing immediate 1D analytical benchmarks, this computationally inexpensive tool offers a reproducible baseline for verifying 1D fluid and multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) codes. It also provides a tractable starting point for exploring asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles relevant to transformer-ratio optimization. --- This repository contains the UPDATED VERSION of supplementary materials for the preprint manuscript, including: - fig1.py: The Python script used to produce Fig. 1. - requirements.txt and README.md: The package dependencies and step-by-step instructions required to run the code and replicate the results. This work is submitted for publication. Preprint is available at arXive:  http://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06458

summary: This record holds the public collections read by the EARC analysis notebook (earc_analysis.ipynb, software record 10.5281/zenodo.23324439), which audits whether a machine learning score depends on units shared between training and test sets. It contains 101 tables from R packages as distributed by Rdatasets, ten molecular benchmark tables from the chemprop v1.7.1 data archive (MoleculeNet), the ApisTox honey bee toxicity data with its splits, three materials tables, the protein GB1 variants of FLIP, the California housing survey and a monthly excerpt of the Mauna Loa carbon dioxide record. Use: unzip earc-data.zip and attach the folder as an input of the notebook, or set the environment variable EARC_DATA to its path. Retinal images and smartphone activity data are not included; the notebook reads them from their own sources. Licences: every file keeps the licence of its source and is redistributed unchanged, except the Mauna Loa file, an excerpt of a U.S. government record. MANIFEST.csv gives the source address, licence, licence text, citation and DOI of each file; the licence texts and copyright notices required by the sources are in LICENSES/ inside earc-data.zip. ApisTox (CC BY-NC 4.0) and SIDER (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0) may be used for non-commercial purposes only; SIDER and Lipophilicity (CC BY-SA 3.0) adaptations must keep the same licence. Files produced by the author of this record are released under CC BY 4.0. Citation: cite this record (all versions: 10.5281/zenodo.24443560) and the original source of every collection you use, as listed in CITATIONS.md with their DOIs.
title: EARC data bundle: public tabular, molecular, materials and protein collections with sources, licences and citations

summary: (PT) Este artigo, primeiro de uma trilogia dedicada ao prolongamento do Itinerário Complementar 6 (IC6) e ao futuro da Região Metropolitana de Coimbra (RMC), discute a relação entre a melhoria das acessibilidades e a construção de um projeto de desenvolvimento territorial à escala regional. Partindo da urgência de concluir a ligação rodoviária no eixo Tábua–Oliveira do Hospital–Seia, o texto defende que a concretização da infraestrutura não deve depender da definição prévia de uma estratégia regional, mas que ambas as questões devem ser discutidas no presente. O IC6 permitirá reduzir obstáculos à mobilidade quotidiana, facilitar o acesso a serviços e diminuir custos para famílias e empresas, respondendo a necessidades de territórios onde já existem atividades, relações e oportunidades que importa reforçar. O artigo questiona, contudo, a ideia de que a melhoria das acessibilidades, por si só, assegura o desenvolvimento territorial ou contraria a perda de população. Defende que a consolidação da Região Metropolitana de Coimbra depende da capacidade de transformar a proximidade física em relações de trabalho, formação, cooperação e acesso a serviços, valorizando os diferentes centros urbanos e os lugares que estruturam a região. A reflexão propõe, assim, que a reivindicação do IC6 seja acompanhada por uma discussão mais ampla sobre a urbanidade que se pretende construir, entendendo a região metropolitana não apenas como um território de distâncias mais curtas, mas como um sistema de relações e oportunidades partilhadas. Publicado no Diário As Beiras , em 2 de novembro de 2026, p. 20, na rubrica urbanidadeS . (EN) This article, the first in a trilogy devoted to the extension of the IC6 road and the future of the Coimbra Metropolitan Region (RMC), examines the relationship between improved accessibility and the development of a territorial project at the regional scale. Starting from the urgent need to complete the road connection along the Tábua–Oliveira do Hospital–Seia corridor, the article argues that the construction of this infrastructure should not depend on the prior definition of a regional strategy, but that both issues must be addressed in the present. The IC6 will help reduce obstacles to everyday mobility, improve access to services and lower costs for households and businesses, responding to the needs of territories where activities, relationships and opportunities already exist. The article nevertheless challenges the assumption that improved accessibility alone can ensure territorial development or reverse population decline. It argues that consolidating the Coimbra Metropolitan Region depends on the ability to transform physical proximity into opportunities for employment, education, cooperation and access to services, while strengthening the different urban centres and settlements that structure the region. The discussion therefore proposes that the demand for the IC6 should be accompanied by a broader debate on the kind of urbanity to be developed, understanding the metropolitan region not merely as a territory of shorter distances, but as a system of interconnected places, relationships and shared opportunities. Originally published in Diário As Beiras , 2 November 2026, p. 20, in the urbanidadeS column.
title: IC6: um itinerário para consolidar uma região metropolitana?

summary: Effective Worlds: Objects, Laws, and Changes of Description belongs to the Emergence Calculus series. This free electronic edition is released under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), as a PDF with page numbers matching the print edition and as a reflowable EPUB. What makes a description a useful theory, and what survives when we change it? Six Birds Theory organizes this work around six primitive roles: descent, representability, route mismatch, staging, packaging and audit. Here they help test whether a coarser description still supports a law, compare what different descriptions retain, and check what supports a chosen world. The book opens with a description that cannot predict and a law gained by forgetting, at the cost of a question the description can no longer answer. Readers build states from the questions they must answer, classify descriptions as equivalent, refining, coarsening or incomparable, and separate repairing a description from changing the question. Later units ask what admitted operations require of a state, carry a public theory across representations, choose descriptions that support a joint operation, and show why a readout does not determine a reconstruction. A unit on averaging builds exact ensembles in which evolving and then averaging differs from averaging and then evolving, the structural question physicists call backreaction, without modeling general relativity or cosmology. Readers then construct the best prediction a description allows for a declared target and loss, and carry checked error bounds through changing descriptions. The final unit chooses and defends an effective world for a stated purpose. Scientific conditions, available operations, access assumptions and competing interpretations stay explicit, so each comparison shows what it relies on. For scientists, engineers and philosophers interested in scientific modeling, coarse graining, effective theories, prediction and the philosophy of science. Prose, monochrome figures, worked examples and answered checks carry a complete route; optional mathematics adds precision. The book builds on the introductory Emergence Calculus course; no other specialist volume is required. More about the series: www.emergencecalculus.com
title: Effective Worlds: Objects, Laws, and Changes of Description

summary: STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW ERA / FAMILY 30 / F146-F150 TRUSTWORTHY PERSONALIZED AROMA AI FIVE FLAGSHIP PROSPECTIVE NONCLINICAL RESEARCH ESSENCE / 2026-11-23 FAMILY SCIENTIFIC DNA / A TRUSTWORTHY MODEL IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY AN AUTHORIZED ACTOR. The five contracts concern subgroup calibration disparity, identified counterfactual predictions, hard safety-gated multiobjective optimization, intervention-tested explanation fidelity, and independent replication of automated research. Each contract retains a different empirical witness, source population, denominator, strong baseline, uncertainty, named adversary and independent stop. The forty-two reproducible three-dimensional maps are deterministic synthetic numerical hypotheses, not observations of people or deployed devices. No clinical efficacy, human safety or quantum advantage is claimed. Human exposure and use of sensitive data require entirely separate authorization. F146 / Dataset Bias in AI Aroma Response Models at the Limit. Scientific mechanism: observational data provenance, missing-not-at-random response labels, subgroup base rates, time-dependent exposure confounding and groupwise probability calibration. Unit-resolved endpoint: Response model subgroup calibration gap [%]. Strong comparator: nested-tuned logistic regression, stratified constant-risk forecasts and calibrated group-blind baseline on identical participant-disjoint splits. Concealed challenge: sealed site-level demographic-proxy reversal, subgroup prevalence shift and missing-not-at-random response deletion. Independent witness: independent subgroup-stratified blind holdout with verified group denominators and confidence intervals. Stop: unauthorized use of sensitive subgroup information, group with too few observations to support inference, calibration gap exceeding preregistered tolerance or irreparable test-set leakage. F147 / Counterfactual Simulations of Personalized Aroma Exposure at the Limit. Scientific mechanism: potential-outcome identification assumptions, exposure propensity overlap, time-varying confounding, uncertainty intervals and distinction between intervention and passive observation. Unit-resolved endpoint: Counterfactual outcome prediction error [%]. Strong comparator: pre-registered inverse-propensity weighted, doubly robust and transparent parametric counterfactual baselines using matched observations and exposure constraints. Concealed challenge: hidden unmeasured confounder reversal, vanishing propensity overlap and placebo-like outcome shift. Independent witness: independent synthetic ground-truth causal simulator with reserved mechanisms or ethically approved prospective validation later. Stop: violation of positivity, no independent intervention reference, model uncertainty past declared bound or any simulated recommendation that would initiate unapproved exposure. F148 / Multiobjective Optimization of Aroma Perception and Physiological Response at the Limit. Scientific mechanism: Pareto dominance, bounded preference uncertainty, physiological-signal proxy reliability, dose envelope, hard safety constraints and incompatible objective scales. Unit-resolved endpoint: Normalized safety–preference Pareto utility [1]. Strong comparator: safety-first deterministic rules, weighted-sum classical optimization, expert conservative policy and random Pareto-feasible proposals at matched budgets. Concealed challenge: adversarial preference reversal, hidden biomarker artifact and hard-limit conflict where reward improves but authorization is withdrawn. Independent witness: independent feasibility auditor and blinded simulated Pareto-front evaluator including rejected and abstained candidates. Stop: any hard dose, ingredient or human-authorization limit violated; uncertainty hides a clinically relevant adverse response; nonconsented monitoring. F149 / Explainability and Safety Boundaries in Aroma Recommendation at the Limit. Scientific mechanism: local feature intervention consistency, proxy

THIRTY CANDIDATE EQUATIONS / DIMENSIONS / RIVAL EXPLANATIONS F146 RELATION 1 / Maximum subgroup calibration gap. Candidate equation: G=100*max_g abs(mean(p|g)-mean(y|g)). Units: Predicted probability and observed event rate dimensionless; G measured in percentage points. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Subgroup imbalance versus response missingness calibration ridge. Refutation: Groups with near-zero denominator render rates unstable. F146 RELATION 2 / Groupwise expected calibration error. Candidate equation: ECE=sum_g (N_g/N)*abs(pbar_g-ybar_g). Units: All fractions dimensionless; ECE dimensionless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Weighted composition surface and minority masking. Refutation: Population weighting hides rare group failure. F146 RELATION 3 / Missingness conditional risk. Candidate equation: R_miss=P(M=1|Y=1)-P(M=1|Y=0). Units: Probabilities dimensionless; result difference in 1. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Missing-not-at-random selection cliff. Refutation: Cannot compute from observed data without sensitivity assumptions. F146 RELATION 4 / Subgroup effective sample size. Candidate equation: N_eff=(sum_i w_i)^2/sum_i w_i^2. Units: Weight sums dimensionless; effective size in observations. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Imbalance and reweighting stability basin. Refutation: Extreme weights lower statistical support. F146 RELATION 5 / Empirical group rate interval. Candidate equation: SE_g=sqrt(p_g*(1-p_g)/N_g). Units: Event probability unitless; standard error dimensionless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Small subgroup confidence width spike. Refutation: Normal approximation invalid for small samples. F146 RELATION 6 / External calibration transfer contrast. Candidate equation: DeltaG=G_new_site-G_training_site. Units: Both gaps in percentage points; DeltaG percentage points. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Site-shift increase in calibration disparity. Refutation: A hidden label ontology change impersonates site effect. F147 RELATION 1 / Absolute counterfactual prediction error. Candidate equation: E_cf=100/N*sum_i abs(yhat_i(a)-yref_i(a)). Units: Predictions and synthetic reference outcomes normalized fractions; E_cf percent. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Positivity versus confounder error basin. Refutation: Human counterfactual is never jointly observed. F147 RELATION 2 / Inverse propensity stabilized weight. Candidate equation: w_i=P(A=a)/max(e_i(a),eps). Units: Propensity and probability denominator dimensionless; w dimensionless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Overlap-limited weight amplification cliff. Refutation: Violating positivity makes estimator untrustworthy. F147 RELATION 3 / Average causal contrast candidate. Candidate equation: ATE=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]. Units: Both potential outcomes in same predefined response unit; ATE same unit. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Hidden confounder response reversal saddle. Refutation: No identification absent exchangeability and consistency. F147 RELATION 4 / Doubly robust estimating relation. Candidate equation: mu_hat=N^-1*sum[m(X)+(I(A=a)/e(X))*(Y-m(X))]. Units: m and Y share response units; ratio dimensionless; mu_hat response units. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Propensity misspecification and model failure frontier. Refutation: Both nuisance estimators may be wrong under positivity loss. F147 RELATION 5 / Counterfactual interval coverage. Candidate equation: C=100/N*sum_i I[L_i<=Ycf_i<=U_i]. Units: L,Ycf,U normalized response; C percent. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Coverage failure under hidden confounding. Refutation: Wider intervals can trivially raise coverage. F147 RELATION 6 / Sensitivity perturbation envelope. Candidate equation: E_max=max_delta E_cf(delta). Units: Unmeasured confounder delta dimensionless; E_max percent. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Sensitivity ridge across confounder uncertainty. Refutation: Chosen delta range may exclude true bias. F148 RELATION 1 / Safety gated Pareto utility. Candidate equation: U=I_feasible*sum_k w_k*u_k. Units: Weights sum to one; all u normalized 0 to 1; U dimensionless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Preference weight and proxy uncertainty frontier. Refutation: Multiplication must not allow infeasible points to score. F148 RELATION 2 / Pareto dominance predicate. Candidate equation: D(a,b)=I[all_k u_k(a)>=u_k(b) and any strict]. Units: Normalized utility coordinates dimensionless; indicator binary. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Dominance plateau and ties. Refutation: A missing safety coordinate invalidates comparison. F148 RELATION 3 / Physical exposure limit. Candidate equation: E_total=sum_t c_t*dt. Units: c concentration mg/m3 and dt hour; E_total mg*h/m3. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Cumulative dose constraint wall. Refutation: Temporal aggregation may hide transient peaks. F148 RELATION 4 / Proxy calibration discrepancy. Candidate equation: Delta_proxy=abs(r_proxy-r_reference). Units: Both proxy signals dimensionless normalized rate; Delta unitless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Signal error versus optimization weight valley. Refutation: Biomarker does not establish human benefit. F148 RELATION 5 / Abstention proportion. Candidate equation: A=100*N_abstain/N_considered. Units: Both quantities counts; A percent. summary: STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW ERA / FAMILY 30 / F146-F150 TRUSTWORTHY PERSONALIZED AROMA AI FIVE FLAGSHIP PROSPECTIVE NONCLINICAL RESEARCH ESSENCE / 2026-11-23 FAMILY SCIENTIFIC DNA / A TRUSTWORTHY MODEL IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY AN AUTHORIZED ACTOR. The five contracts concern subgroup calibration disparity, identified counterfactual predictions, hard safety-gated multiobjective optimization, intervention-tested explanation fidelity, and independent replication of automated research. Each contract retains a different empirical witness, source population, denominator, strong baseline, uncertainty, named adversary and independent stop. The forty-two reproducible three-dimensional maps are deterministic synthetic numerical hypotheses, not observations of people or deployed devices. No clinical efficacy, human safety or quantum advantage is claimed. Human exposure and use of sensitive data require entirely separate authorization. F146 / Dataset Bias in AI Aroma Response Models at the Limit. Scientific mechanism: observational data provenance, missing-not-at-random response labels, subgroup base rates, time-dependent exposure confounding and groupwise probability calibration. Unit-resolved endpoint: Response model subgroup calibration gap [%]. Strong comparator: nested-tuned logistic regression, stratified constant-risk forecasts and calibrated group-blind baseline on identical participant-disjoint splits. Concealed challenge: sealed site-level demographic-proxy reversal, subgroup prevalence shift and missing-not-at-random response deletion. Independent witness: independent subgroup-stratified blind holdout with verified group denominators and confidence intervals. Stop: unauthorized use of sensitive subgroup information, group with too few observations to support inference, calibration gap exceeding preregistered tolerance or irreparable test-set leakage. F147 / Counterfactual Simulations of Personalized Aroma Exposure at the Limit. Scientific mechanism: potential-outcome identification assumptions, exposure propensity overlap, time-varying confounding, uncertainty intervals and distinction between intervention and passive observation. Unit-resolved endpoint: Counterfactual outcome prediction error [%]. Strong comparator: pre-registered inverse-propensity weighted, doubly robust and transparent parametric counterfactual baselines using matched observations and exposure constraints. Concealed challenge: hidden unmeasured confounder reversal, vanishing propensity overlap and placebo-like outcome shift. Independent witness: independent synthetic ground-truth causal simulator with reserved mechanisms or ethically approved prospective validation later. Stop: violation of positivity, no independent intervention reference, model uncertainty past declared bound or any simulated recommendation that would initiate unapproved exposure. F148 / Multiobjective Optimization of Aroma Perception and Physiological Response at the Limit. Scientific mechanism: Pareto dominance, bounded preference uncertainty, physiological-signal proxy reliability, dose envelope, hard safety constraints and incompatible objective scales. Unit-resolved endpoint: Normalized safety–preference Pareto utility [1]. Strong comparator: safety-first deterministic rules, weighted-sum classical optimization, expert conservative policy and random Pareto-feasible proposals at matched budgets. Concealed challenge: adversarial preference reversal, hidden biomarker artifact and hard-limit conflict where reward improves but authorization is withdrawn. Independent witness: independent feasibility auditor and blinded simulated Pareto-front evaluator including rejected and abstained candidates. Stop: any hard dose, ingredient or human-authorization limit violated; uncertainty hides a clinically relevant adverse response; nonconsented monitoring. F149 / Explainability and Safety Boundaries in Aroma Recommendation at the Limit. Scientific mechanism: local feature intervention consistency, proxy

Candidate equation: R_miss=P(M=1|Y=1)-P(M=1|Y=0). Units: Probabilities dimensionless; result difference in 1. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Missing-not-at-random selection cliff. Refutation: Cannot compute from observed data without sensitivity assumptions. F146 RELATION 4 / Subgroup effective sample size. Candidate equation: N_eff=(sum_i w_i)^2/sum_i w_i^2. Units: Weight sums dimensionless; effective size in observations. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Imbalance and reweighting stability basin. Refutation: Extreme weights lower statistical support. F146 RELATION 5 / Empirical group rate interval. Candidate equation: SE_g=sqrt(p_g*(1-p_g)/N_g). Units: Event probability unitless; standard error dimensionless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Small subgroup confidence width spike. Refutation: Normal approximation invalid for small samples. F146 RELATION 6 / External calibration transfer contrast. Candidate equation: DeltaG=G_new_site-G_training_site. Units: Both gaps in percentage points; DeltaG percentage points. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Site-shift increase in calibration disparity. Refutation: A hidden label ontology change impersonates site effect. F147 RELATION 1 / Absolute counterfactual prediction error. Candidate equation: E_cf=100/N*sum_i abs(yhat_i(a)-yref_i(a)). Units: Predictions and synthetic reference outcomes normalized fractions; E_cf percent. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Positivity versus confounder error basin. Refutation: Human counterfactual is never jointly observed. F147 RELATION 2 / Inverse propensity stabilized weight. Candidate equation: w_i=P(A=a)/max(e_i(a),eps). Units: Propensity and probability denominator dimensionless; w dimensionless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Overlap-limited weight amplification cliff. Refutation: Violating positivity makes estimator untrustworthy. F147 RELATION 3 / Average causal contrast candidate. Candidate equation: ATE=E[Y(1)-Y(0)]. Units: Both potential outcomes in same predefined response unit; ATE same unit. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Hidden confounder response reversal saddle. Refutation: No identification absent exchangeability and consistency. F147 RELATION 4 / Doubly robust estimating relation. Candidate equation: mu_hat=N^-1*sum[m(X)+(I(A=a)/e(X))*(Y-m(X))]. Units: m and Y share response units; ratio dimensionless; mu_hat response units. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Propensity misspecification and model failure frontier. Refutation: Both nuisance estimators may be wrong under positivity loss. F147 RELATION 5 / Counterfactual interval coverage. Candidate equation: C=100/N*sum_i I[L_i<=Ycf_i<=U_i]. Units: L,Ycf,U normalized response; C percent. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Coverage failure under hidden confounding. Refutation: Wider intervals can trivially raise coverage. F147 RELATION 6 / Sensitivity perturbation envelope. Candidate equation: E_max=max_delta E_cf(delta). Units: Unmeasured confounder delta dimensionless; E_max percent. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Sensitivity ridge across confounder uncertainty. Refutation: Chosen delta range may exclude true bias. F148 RELATION 1 / Safety gated Pareto utility. Candidate equation: U=I_feasible*sum_k w_k*u_k. Units: Weights sum to one; all u normalized 0 to 1; U dimensionless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Preference weight and proxy uncertainty frontier. Refutation: Multiplication must not allow infeasible points to score. F148 RELATION 2 / Pareto dominance predicate. Candidate equation: D(a,b)=I[all_k u_k(a)>=u_k(b) and any strict]. Units: Normalized utility coordinates dimensionless; indicator binary. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Dominance plateau and ties. Refutation: A missing safety coordinate invalidates comparison. F148 RELATION 3 / Physical exposure limit. Candidate equation: E_total=sum_t c_t*dt. Units: c concentration mg/m3 and dt hour; E_total mg*h/m3. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Cumulative dose constraint wall. Refutation: Temporal aggregation may hide transient peaks. F148 RELATION 4 / Proxy calibration discrepancy. Candidate equation: Delta_proxy=abs(r_proxy-r_reference). Units: Both proxy signals dimensionless normalized rate; Delta unitless. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Signal error versus optimization weight valley. Refutation: Biomarker does not establish human benefit. F148 RELATION 5 / Abstention proportion. Candidate equation: A=100*N_abstain/N_considered. Units: Both quantities counts; A percent. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Uncertainty and constraint abstention contour. Refutation: Omitting rejected proposals falsifies yield. F148 RELATION 6 / Human veto conjunction. Candidate equation: P_action=P_safety*P_consent*P_device. Units: All permissions binary and product binary. Reconstructible 3D interpretation: Hard veto feasibility intersection. summary: STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW ERA / FAMILY 28 / F136-F140 HYBRID QUANTUM-CLASSICAL AROMA COMPUTING RESEARCH ESSENCE / PROSPECTIVE NONCLINICAL FALSIFIABLE REPRODUCIBLE / 2026-11-23 FAMILY SCIENTIFIC DNA This family investigates hybrid quantum/classical algorithms without assuming superiority. F136 separates true conformer search quality and incomplete reference minima. F137 demands a consistent VQE Hamiltonian, active space, electron spin and shot budget before calculating errors. F138 requires blind externally authenticated aroma spectra, instrument holdouts, honest class imbalance and a capable classical kernel classifier. F139 converts quantum and conventional computational overhead into a declared equivalent core-hour ledger. F140 treats advantage as a paired end-to-end time difference only after both algorithms reach an equal target error and their unselected failed runs are counted. The five main endpoints have different units and do not combine into one score. Forty-two deliberately synthetic 25-by-25 surfaces propose experimental questions rather than actual device runs. A classical success must remain visible; no human aromatherapy or experimental quantum advantage is claimed. FLAGSHIP F136 / Hybrid Quantum–Classical Conformational Searches for Aroma Molecules at the Limit Physical object matched-cost conformer exploration of identified terpene rotamers and stereoisomers. Candidate mechanism rotational energy barriers, low-lying conformer coverage, molecular identity, force-field screening, correlated-energy re-ranking and search-time selection bias. Primary Conformer search minimum energy gap [kJ/mol]. Strong comparator best tuned basin hopping, molecular mechanics, genetic search and classical DFT re-ranking at equal wall time, CPU/GPU budget and accuracy. Concealed challenge concealed torsional barrier swap, withheld stereoisomer and shuffled initial conformer seed. Independent test independent conformer ledger with optimized geometries, vibrational stationarity, energy corrections and blind runtime meters. Rival incomplete conformer reference, favorable initialization, force-field bias, isotope or stereo mismatch, hidden queue latency and data selection. Binding stop stereochemical identity not verified, reference minimum unconverged, hidden initialization leakage or cost parity not met. The target remains an independent proposed method, not an observed success. FLAGSHIP F137 / Variational Quantum Algorithms for Terpene Electronic Energies at the Limit Physical object noisy VQE surrogate validation against reproducible molecular electronic energies. Candidate mechanism second-quantized Hamiltonians, basis truncation, ansatz expressivity, optimizer variance, shot noise, measurement mitigation and reference correlation. Primary VQE energy error [kJ/mol]. Strong comparator Hartree–Fock, exact diagonalization of matched active spaces, selected CI, classical tensor networks and CC reference when applicable. Concealed challenge blind circuit depth growth, gate noise shift and withheld molecule spin state. Independent test independently constructed Hamiltonian, active-space ledger, calibrated quantum-simulator results and classical exact active-space witness. Rival active-space change, noise-mitigation selection, optimizer restarts, computational precision mismatch, unrealistic error-free reference or basis-set truncation. Binding stop unregistered active space or spin, unreported shot counts, mitigation data leakage or classical energy comparator omitted. The target remains an independent proposed method, not an observed success. FLAGSHIP F138 / Quantum Kernels for Aroma Spectral Classification at the Limit Physical object quantum-kernel spectra classifiers on blinded chemical and instrument splits. Candidate mechanism spectral preprocessing, feature maps and kernel alignment, rare isomer separation, class imbalance, batch confounds, label ontology and held-out calibration. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

Predicted geometric signature: Duplicate basin at low sampling entropy. Rival: Canonicalization mismatch can falsely increase molecular diversity.. F131 / RELATION 3: Novel scaffold share. Formula N=100*N_novel_scaffolds/N_valid. Dimensional condition: Novel scaffold count divided by valid generated count, percent. Predicted geometric signature: Scaffold novelty ridge at constrained validity. Rival: Training corpus incompleteness may imitate novelty.. F131 / RELATION 4: Penalized graph objective. Formula J=log(p_graph)-lambda*P_invalid. Dimensional condition: Log probability and penalty dimensionless, lambda dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Feasible manifold under valence penalties. Rival: Reward hacking can improve J while molecular chemistry degrades.. F131 / RELATION 5: Shannon graph diversity. Formula H=-sum_i p_i ln(p_i). Dimensional condition: p_i relative graph frequencies; entropy nats. Predicted geometric signature: Diversity ridge subject to sampling noise. Rival: A high-entropy distribution can be mostly chemically invalid.. F131 / RELATION 6: Held-out validity difference. Formula DeltaV=V_model-V_classical. Dimensional condition: Both V in percent; DeltaV percentage points. Predicted geometric signature: External scaffold frontier can invert an internal advantage. Rival: A strong classic fragment generator may beat the proposed model.. F132 / RELATION 1: Blind attribute correlation. Formula r=cov(yhat,y)/(sd(yhat)*sd(y)). Dimensional condition: Standard deviation and covariance matched scale; r dimensionless from -1 to 1. Predicted geometric signature: Correlation saddle under rater reliability and scaffold shift. Rival: Repeated ratings or leaked descriptors can inflate correlation.. F132 / RELATION 2: Correlation Fisher transform. Formula z=0.5*ln((1+r)/(1-r)). Dimensional condition: r dimensionless -1<r<1; z dimensionless. Predicted geometric signature: Exploding endpoints near perfect correlation. Rival: High z is unstable for small or dependent test sets.. F132 / RELATION 3: Attribute MAE. Formula MAE=(1/N)*sum|yhat_i-y_i|. Dimensional condition: Predictions and ratings in same registered rating-scale units. Predicted geometric signature: Error valley across label calibration. Rival: A changed rater scale can fabricate gains.. F132 / RELATION 4: Hierarchical rater variance. Formula u_total2=u_molecule2+u_rater2+u_lab2. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 27 · F131-F135 GENERATIVE COMPUTATIONAL DESIGN OF AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH ESSENCE · PROSPECTIVE / NONCLINICAL / FALSIFIABLE / REPRODUCIBLE FAMILY RESEARCH CONTRACT This family studies five complementary but scientifically distinct aspects of computational design for plant-derived odorants. The central claim is not that a machine can create a beneficial scent. It is a prospectively falsifiable proposal that molecular graph candidates, predicted odour descriptors, volatility-constrained Pareto sets, oxidation-stability models and abstract synthesis-route plausibility can be compared fairly against competent classical baselines. Each flagship uses its own denominator, measurement unit, external witness, negative-case ledger and stopping authority. Computational syntax does not establish real molecular identity; a predicted odour attribute does not verify a human perception; a feasible Pareto set is not a safety certificate; a stable simulation is not an aging experiment; and a synthetic route diagram is not a synthesized compound. The response surfaces throughout the 819-page PDF are synthetic 25-by-25 numerical illustrations intended to illuminate hypothetical shape, sensitivity and non-identifiability. They are not model outputs obtained from new molecular-generation runs. Future groups should preregister sample inclusion, chemical identity, strong nulls, risk exclusions and uncertainty before examining results. Classical models should be allowed to win. FLAGSHIP F131 · Generative Design of Candidate Aroma Molecular Structures at the Limit Scientific object: chemical-graph generation under valence, stereochemistry, scaffold holdout and provenance constraints. Physical basis: SMILES parsing, valence and aromaticity sanitization, canonical graph uniqueness, stereoisomer assignment, charge conservation and training scaffold leakage. Primary endpoint: Chemical validity of generated molecules [%]. Comparator: expert-curated terpene analogues, fragment recombination and a tuned classical SMILES generator at the same proposal budget. Strong rival: memorized scaffolds, duplicate canonical graphs, invalid stereochemistry, biased molecular-size filtering or generator reward hacking. Withheld intervention: sealed scaffold-family holdout with stereochemical and charge-state swaps. Independent observation: independent canonicalization and chemistry-rule audit plus blinded scaffold-novelty registry. Binding stop: unknown graph source, invalid atom valence, missing generator denominator, undisclosed training overlap or unreviewed hazardous candidate. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F132 · Bias in Predicting Molecular Odour Properties at the Limit Scientific object: blind structure-to-odour attribute prediction with bias diagnostics across molecular families. Physical basis: olfactory descriptor ontology, multi-label rater uncertainty, scaffold domain shift, molecular representation and panel expectation leakage. Primary endpoint: Blind odour attribute correlation [1]. Comparator: scaffold-held-out random forest, descriptor-based regression and a pre-registered principal-odour-map baseline. Strong rival: semantic descriptor leakage, inconsistent rating scales, panel bias, aromatic-family imbalance or post-hoc attribute selection. Withheld intervention: concealed descriptor renaming, scaffold exclusion and panel-rater disagreement stress test. Independent observation: ethically obtained independent blinded attribute-rating archive with chemistry identity, interrater statistics and external family splits. Binding stop: no ethically sourced sensory reference, uncorrected label leakage, insufficient external families or unstable denominator variance. This evidence contract does not transfer its interpretation to unrelated flagships or human therapeutic claims. FLAGSHIP F133 ·

summary: This replication package accompanies the study of Norgespris, Norway's voluntary fixed-price electricity scheme. The paper compares electricity meters that entered the scheme early with meters classified as non-adopters in three southern Norwegian bidding zones (NO1, NO2 and NO5) from October 2023 to April 2026. It examines who stood to gain from fixed-price protection, how the cohorts responded to daily electricity prices before and after adoption, and how their relative consumption changed. The archive includes aggregate hourly consumption and meter counts from Elhub, ERA5 temperature data obtained through Open-Meteo, and the Python and R code used to generate the tables, figures and numerical results in the paper and its supplement. The README gives the software versions, the command for running the analysis, and a guide to the files behind each exhibit. The included retrieval script obtains the hourly electricity prices from Hva koster strømmen and checks all 2,829 supplier responses against their archived SHA-256 digests.
title: Who Gives Up the Price Signal? Selection, Price Responsiveness and Demand under Norway's Voluntary Fixed Electricity Price

title: An Open Letter to the Academic, Formal Verification, and Frontier AI Communities

summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. summary: STARLI · WHITE RAINBOW ERA · FAMILY 26 / F126-F130 QUANTUM AROMA SIMULATION AND EXPERIMENTAL BENCHMARKS · FIVE THOUSAND WORD RESEARCH ESSENCE Prospective / Nonclinical / Falsifiable / Reproducible / All numerical 3D surfaces are synthetic RESEARCH POSITION This scientific working edition specifies separate tests for nanomaterial adsorption-energy calculations, quantum molecular-simulation benchmarks against strong classical methods, blind botanical-isomer spectral identification, solvent/interface free-energy transfer, and uncertainty calibration against experimental aroma analysis. The five outcomes use incompatible denominators: energy mean absolute error in kilojoules per mole, isomer identification accuracy in percent, and externally observed uncertainty coverage in percent. Surface geometries, molecular identities, gas-phase and condensed-phase reference states, classical compute cost, isomer standards, and prediction interval widths cannot be silently exchanged. The forty-two plotted meshes are deterministic synthetic illustrations rather than actual quantum calculations or experiments. Nothing in these figures establishes a materials improvement, neurological effect, human benefit or special quantum healing property. Research inheritance depends on explicit null comparisons, falsifiers, negative cases, working code and externally held evidence. FIVE INDEPENDENT FLAGSHIP CONTRACTS F126 · Calculation of Aroma Adsorption Energies on Nanomaterials at the Limit Research object: adsorption-energy predictions for traceable botanical volatiles on characterized nanomaterial surfaces. Primary endpoint: Adsorption energy MAE [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: surface-site heterogeneity, adsorbate orientation, surface coverage, dispersion, substrate relaxation, basis-set superposition error and solvent competition. Strong classical comparator: matched-geometry periodic DFT or established dispersion-corrected classical reference with independently measured desorption if available. Independent scientific witness: independent adsorption reference table with surface identity, adsorption site, coverage, energy conventions and uncertainty. Concealed adversarial perturbation: blind swap of adsorption-site geometry, surface hydroxylation and reference molecule orientation. A rival interpretation is coverage-dependent aggregation, omitted surface hydroxylation, ghost-basis correction or a shifted adsorption reference rather than true improvement. Stop if unknown surface chemistry, missing adsorption reference state, energy sign inconsistency, uncontrolled basis or incomplete mass accounting. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F127 · Quantum-Computing Benchmarks for Aroma Molecular Simulation at the Limit Research object: equal-budget quantum-circuit and classical molecule-simulation benchmarking. Primary endpoint: Equal-resource quantum simulation error [kJ/mol]. Principal physical uncertainty: active-space selection, fermion-to-qubit mapping, variational ansatz expressivity, measurement shots, circuit depth, gate noise, error mitigation and total wall-time cost. Strong classical comparator: strong classical electronic-structure baseline and noiseless quantum simulator at the same molecule and explicit wall-time, energy and precision budget. Independent scientific witness: independent reference energy and auditable device/simulator circuit, shot, calibration, compiler and runtime ledger. Concealed adversarial perturbation: withheld spin/active-space perturbation combined with a noisy-shot and calibration-day reversal. A rival interpretation is reference leakage, noise mitigation bias, inconsistent active space, cherry-picked molecule or ignored overhead. Stop if absence of matched classical resource ledger, unreproducible measurement statistics, unstable optimizer or unreported hardware calibration. This is a prospective design rather than a verified result. F128 · Sp

Candidate: Var(Ehat)=sum_j c_j^2*(1-<Pj>^2)/Nj. Units and assumptions: c_j energy; Pj dimensionless ±1; Nj counts; variance energy squared. Units and assumptions: Both wavenumbers cm^-1; residual cm^-1. Three-dimensional interpretation: Instrument calibration shift contour. Refutation: A shifted peak is not a different isomer. F128 · FORMULA 5: Spectral resolving power. Candidate: Rspec=nu/deltaNu. Units and assumptions: Both nu and deltaNu cm^-1; dimensionless. Three-dimensional interpretation: Resolution cliff with overlapping peaks. Refutation: Physical coelution may remain even at excellent spectral resolution. summary: STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW ERA / FAMILY 25 / F121-F125 QUANTUM CHEMISTRY OF BOTANICAL AROMA MOLECULES RESEARCH WORKING EDITION V1.0 / PROSPECTIVE, NONCLINICAL, FALSIFIABLE, NUMERICALLY REPRODUCIBLE SCIENTIFIC IDENTITY AND NONCLAIM BOUNDARY Family 25 invites future molecular researchers to test five distinct hypotheses: electronic-structure reference accuracy, stereochemically resolved conformer ranking, conditional ligand and olfactory receptor interaction energies, oxidation transition-state errors, and wavelength-dependent photochemical degradation rates. Each question has a different kind of observable. F121, F123 and F124 require energy-error units in kJ/mol; F122 requires dimensionless Kendall rank agreement; F125 uses h^-1 for a first-order kinetic coefficient. Shared molecular metadata cannot make these numerical quantities interchangeable. Forty-two synthetic three-dimensional meshes visualize possibilities, not results computed for an actual terpene. No new quantum chemistry benchmark was performed on real molecule-specific input decks; no receptor experiment, inhalation study, skin assay or clinical efficacy study was conducted. The proposed methods need independent references, uncertainty accounting, matched computational budgets and preregistered reasons to stop. A high-level classical method may outperform every newer architecture and remains a scientifically useful answer. FIVE INDIVIDUAL FLAGSHIP RESEARCH CONTRACTS F121 / Quantum-Chemical Simulation of Aroma Electronic Structure at the Limit The proposed physical object is electronic-structure prediction of authenticated botanical odorant molecules, with emphasis on electron correlation, density functional approximation, basis-set incompleteness, spin state, reference geometry, stereochemistry, pseudopotential choice and convergence diagnostics. Primary decision: Electronic structure energy MAE [kJ/mol]. The minimum reproducible prototype needs digitally identified terpene molecular graphs, stereochemical identifiers, reproducible geometries and frozen quantum chemistry input files. Compare to same-geometry high-level classical quantum chemistry, where feasible DLPNO-CCSD(T) or carefully converged reference calculations under a registered resource budget. An independent observer must evaluate independently generated matched-geometry high-level electronic-energy tables with computational settings, provenance and uncertainty. Blinded adversarial intervention: blinded stereoisomer-label permutation with a concealed basis-set and geometry swap. Potentially stronger rival: conformer omission, changed reference geometry or inconsistent electronic reference state rather than an improved Hamiltonian approximation. Hard stop: missing independent energy reference, uncontrolled charge or spin, nonconvergent SCF or undisclosed multi-reference character. This is a research-design contract, not a newly verified gain. Successor interpretation: model, molecular identity, reference and reported uncertainty travel together. No favorable synthetic numerical residual should be substituted for a molecule-specific converged quantum calculation. In F121, the strongest classical analysis may win. Preserve all unsuccessful inputs, problematic spin or photochemical states and withheld counterexamples. A research gate is an invitation to reject the model when evidence requires it. F122 / Conformational Energy Landscapes of Botanical Terpenes at the Limit The proposed physical object is ranking of torsional conformers in complex botanical terpene stereoisomers, with emphasis on torsional potential energy, conformer search coverage, Boltzmann populations, thermal barriers, stereo- and enantiomer assignment, correlated energy errors and duplicated minima. Primary decision: Conformer rank agreement (Kendall tau) [ratio]. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions. THE SIX-STAGE CHAPTER DEVELOPMENT In the first passage the investigator identifies physical origin, material identity and the inherited scientific dispute. The second passage proposes a specific physical mechanism and a mathematical geometry with separate units on each axis. The third passage audits calibration, independent measurements and all denominators. The fourth introduces an adversarial counterfactual designed to preserve a plausible visible outcome while changing the cause. The fifth tests the strongest equal-resource comparator, including blinded disturbances and uncertainty intervals. The sixth leaves an open source inheritance with a hard stopping rule and a future research question. The progression must change the question at each step; simply altering the names of variables would not constitute scientific development. TWO HUNDRED RESEARCH GATES The gates follow forty specific challenges for each of five distinct flagship endpoints. Every gate has a material or informational origin, an extreme counterfactual revealing how a false interpretation might survive and a future plan with an independent witness. Each gate includes a concept structure and an adversarial-break structure. Their diagrams explain competing roles; they do not prove that the proposed mechanisms work. The gate remains open when an outside investigator discovers a new, better explanation and can reproduce the experiment without asking the originator for private knowledge. THIRTY-THREE PHOENIX PROTOTYPES Each Phoenix object proposes a physical or digital minimum that could be independently built: a chemical identity card, sensor calibration fixture, adversarial controller, locked sensor model, offline reconstruction package or simulated archive migration. A prototype is an answer embryo, not a certified product. Its design is useful only if it identifies an independent observation that could make the present answer fail, and if the human operator retains the right to stop the test. ONE-HUNDRED-YEAR ARCHIVAL TEST The century-scale horizon is modeled, not observed. It contains threats such as changing formats, missing dependencies, lost institutional custody, inaccessible computing services and silent changes to research methods. The preferred experiment uses adversarial simulated migrations and independent replay across distinct custody pathways. A successor should be able to identify the original chemical evidence, recreate model grids, verify denominators and revoke inherited control privileges. A beautiful future image without these rights is insufficient. FINAL SCIENTIFIC INSCRIPTION The future is not an extension of a beautiful prediction. It is an invitation to test the parts of today's knowledge that might be wrong. The White Rainbow Era seeks a defensible warmth: open knowledge, human authority, bounded instruments, adequate reference comparisons and the inheritance of questions.
