title: two-mode-readout: code for 'Same evolution, different probabilities: a two-mode lesson on grid-readout error in quantum simulation'

summary: This repository contains the computational reproducibility package accompanying a study of additive host–guest competition under mismatched chemical conditions. It includes synthetic benchmark data, Python implementations, rational infeasibility certificates, independent certificate-verification routines, and documented numerical comparison results. The primary 500-case benchmark and the 24-case structural comparison can be reproduced using the supplied scripts. Additional sensitivity and held-out results are retained as archived summaries because complete case-level inputs are not available in this release.
title: Reproducibility Data and Code for Certificate-Based Set-Membership Testing of Additive Host–Guest Competition

summary: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^α\cap L_t^2H_x^{α+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leqα<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The proof relies on a computer-assisted construction of a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, starting from the numerical profiles identified in our preceding paper (arXiv:2606.07501). We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.
title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II

summary: For an absorbed one-dimensional diffusion, we characterize two-point restart laws preserving the exit-side probability for every independent renewal clock. Spectral identities establish rigidity under spatial accumulation, while explicit nonsymmetric potentials admit neutral pairs. We distinguish midpoint Dirichlet isospectrality from Weyl reflection rigidity and prove a second-order high-energy asymptotic under local continuity, giving two necessary asymmetry conditions for neutral pairs. Two complete exit profiles at distinct reset rates identify diffusivity and drift; a finite birth-death analogue admits exact Jacobi criteria and reconstruction from four channel functions.
title: Exit-Pair Rigidity, Neutral Restart Laws, and Inverse Reconstruction in One Dimension

summary: We develop a method for forming Ramsey fringes in atomic interferometers as a difference error signal using the phase-jump technique for Ramsey pulses (phase-jump error signal). In this case, the measurement procedure can be implemented as stabilization (locking) of the frequency chirp rate at the central zero of the error signal. We show analytically that this approach allows suppressing the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift (LACS). This shift was recently theoretically predicted and experimentally identified in the papers [V. I. Yudin et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{122}, 737 (2025); D. N. Kapusta et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{123}, 388 (2026)]. A characteristic feature of the LACS is an inverse cubic dependence $\propto 1/T^3$ (where $T$ is the time between adjacent Ramsey pulses), and it can become dominant for interferometers with a short baseline. Therefore, the developed measurement algorithm with a phase-jump error signal will enable significant improvement in the metrological performance of compact quantum sensors for various purposes (atomic gravimeters, accelerometers, gyroscopes).
title: Atomic interferometry based on a phase-jump error signal with suppression of the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift

summary: Existing no-reference point cloud quality assessment (NR-PCQA) methods perform well within individual datasets but generalize poorly across datasets. We identify insufficient distortion coverage in training data as a key cause: on unseen distortion types, models rank severity levels near chance or even in reverse. We propose perceptually gated synthetic supervision for no-reference point cloud quality assessment (PGS-PCQA), an NR-PCQA model trained with synthetic distortion ranking. It builds a synthetic distortion bank from source reference point clouds and uses within-type severity ranking as supervision in addition to the source mean opinion scores (MOS), requiring no subjective scores for the synthetic samples. Since higher severity does not always mean lower perceived quality, a perceptual gate softens the ranking targets of pairs with small perceptual differences in rendered views. The synthetic supervision is used only during training and needs no target-domain data. In a single training run on SJTU-PCQA, PGS-PCQA achieves Spearman rank correlation coefficients (SRCCs) of 0.709 on WPC and 0.751 on BASICS. The corresponding published DSP-PCQA scores are 0.595 and 0.723. Under reference-disjoint cross-validation, PGS-PCQA achieves SRCCs of 0.955 on SJTU-PCQA, 0.934 on WPC, 0.906 on BASICS, and 0.791 on LS-PCQA Part I. In the exclusion experiment, the reported scores for the reduced synthetic bank represent 58-65% of the full-bank SRCC gain relative to training without the bank. Code is available at https://github.com/Fan-QY/PGS-PCQA.
title: PGS-PCQA: Perceptually Gated Synthetic Supervision for No-Reference Point Cloud Quality Assessment

summary: An AI-assisted payment can pass assessment and lose release authority before commitment. We specify a banking delegation contract that checks current authority, the shared payment cap and the capacity of eligible instruments to cover losses. It books the new payment and its recovery demands and writes the outcome record in the same atomic transition. A paired example identifies the authorised mandate, applied rule and selection inputs a reviewer needs to assess mandate conformance. We show that, under fixed resource inputs, the transition preserves the payment cap and recovery feasibility when commitments and effective withdrawals are ordered against the same authoritative state. Reversing a transmitted priority changes the selected route in 4 of 32 distinct behavioural combinations, represented by 96 of 576 labelled contexts. The executor follows the transmitted rule in all of them. Reusing earlier state admits 23 releases in 123 histories blocked by the reference. Pooling recovery capacity admits 69 infeasible configurations in a grid of 576. Both current-state implementations agree with the reference in all 144 commitment histories and 624 concurrent schedules. The retention test recovers five specified outcome fields from each of 47 complete records. Fifteen survey responses informed requirements for resolving holds and handling uncertain delivery. An insurance example illustrates referral after an adverse coverage finding.
title: Accountable AI Delegation in Banking: Identity, Commitment Controls, Decision Evidence and Recovery

summary: The excited-state properties of imide-based defect double antiperovskites AE$_5$AsPn(NH)$_2$ (AE = Ca, Sr; Pn = Sb, Bi) are investigated using spin--orbit-coupled quasiparticle calculations, the model Bethe--Salpeter equation (mBSE), and analytical descriptions of lattice-polarization effects. Across five tetragonal ($P4/mmm$) and monoclinic ($Cm$) structural models, the calculated exciton binding energies range from 140 to 210 meV. Chemical substitution modifies both the binding energies and the hydrogenic estimates of exciton spatial extent. By contrast, the structural distortion from tetragonal $P4/mmm$ ($D_{4h}$) to monoclinic $Cm$ ($C_s$), which removes inversion and fourfold rotational symmetry, produces comparatively modest changes in binding energy but appreciably reshapes the real- and momentum-space exciton distributions. This contrast reveals a partial decoupling between exciton energetics and wavefunction geometry, and identifies a symmetry-associated sensitivity of exciton geometry to structural distortion. The changes are understood to occur together with modifications of local coordination and electronic dispersion, rather than as an isolated effect of symmetry alone. Lattice polarization provides an additional screening channel, reducing the estimated exciton binding energies by approximately 9--16\%. Complementary Fröhlich-polaron calculations yield moderate mass enhancement and model-estimated electron-polaron mobilities of 39--99 cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$, with comparatively modest differences between the two polymorphs. These results highlight the distinct responses of exciton energetics, exciton wavefunction geometry, and carrier transport to chemical and structural modifications.
title: Decoupling Exciton Energetics from Wavefunction Geometry in Imide-Based Defect Double Antiperovskites

summary: Constructing an effective low-dimensional stochastic model from sparse observations requires separating deterministic drift from state-dependent fluctuations when the governing interaction law is unknown. We formulate an adaptive neural stochastic differential equation with topology constraints (TC-AdaNSDE) for two-variable predator--prey dynamics. To regularize the inverse problem when data are scarce, the model combines flexible drift and correlated diffusion fields with density-adaptive local Kramers--Moyal moment estimates and soft phase-space constraints reflecting boundary saddle behavior near extinction and local stability near coexistence. Using a known nonlinear stochastic system, we first show that short-time trajectory error cannot assess diffusion accuracy on its own and must be paired with distributional measures of one-step transitions and long-time phase-space occupancy. We then apply this framework to macroscopic turbulence and zonal flow energies reduced from Hasegawa--Wakatani plasma simulations and to short ecological time series. In the sparse-data regime, TC-AdaNSDE reproduces both short-horizon evolution and long-time invariant energy distributions where deterministic reductions collapse and unconstrained stochastic fits diverge, while recovering physically interpretable drift and fluctuation fields across both physical and biological systems.
title: Learning effective stochastic predator and prey dynamics across physical and biological systems from limited data

summary: Recent studies have identified orbital exchange fields as a novel mechanism for controlling electronic and magnetic phenomena through the orbital degree of freedom. In contrast to conventional spin exchange fields, orbital exchange fields couple directly to orbital angular momentum and can emerge from purely orbital interactions or dynamically through couplings to chiral excitations such as phonons and magnons. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the transport and torque responses generated by orbital exchange fields in two-dimensional materials. Using monolayer H-phase MoS$_2$ as a prototypical transition-metal dichalcogenide, we introduce a Zeeman-like orbital exchange field that breaks time-reversal symmetry in orbital space while leaving the spin degree of freedom inactive. We demonstrate that this perturbation induces a sizable intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity even in the absence of spin magnetism and spin--orbit coupling driven mechanisms. Simultaneously, the orbital Hall response remains robust in the weak-field regime and undergoes substantial reconstruction at larger exchange strengths due to pronounced band modifications. In addition, we show that currents can generate sizable current-induced orbital torques on the orbital magnetization. Our results establish orbital exchange fields as an effective route toward Hall transport and nonequilibrium torque phenomena driven purely by orbital physics, opening new perspectives for orbitronics and orbitally engineered quantum functionalities.
title: Pure Orbitronics: Hall Responses and Torques by Orbital Exchange in Spinless Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides

summary: Frustrated magnets on triangular lattices favour noncollinear order, and when inversion symmetry is broken they can host localized topological textures on top of that order. Here we show that the Janus MXene MnHf2C2FI is such a system. Combining first-principles calculations with atomistic spin simulations, we find that magnetism is confined to the Mn layer, where a strong antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor exchange together with a sizable Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction stabilizes a frustrated 120 Neel ground state. On top of this ground state we identify a metastable hexameron: a composite of six merons and antimerons, one vortex-antivortex pair on each of the three sublattices, whose sublattice-resolved topological charges compensate. Linear spin-wave theory confirms that the hexameron is a local energy minimum, and its noncoplanar cores act as potential wells that bind discrete in-gap magnon modes below the bulk continuum. In a periodic hexameron array the magnon bands carry nonzero Chern numbers, and the resulting Berry curvature produces a magnon thermal Hall response whose sign depends on which of the two time-reversal partners of the hexameron is realized. Our results establish Janus MXenes as a two-dimensional platform in which frustration, broken inversion symmetry, and spin-orbit coupling combine to produce metastable antiferromagnetic solitons with distinct spectroscopic and transport fingerprints.
title: Frustration-Stabilized Hexamerons and Their Topological Magnons in Janus MXene

summary: This record provides the Actual Vapor Pressure (AVP) component of the H igh-resolution ( d aily and 1 km) atmospheric M oisture I ndex C ollection over China (HiMIC-Daily) . AVP is essential for water vapor transport calculations and complements the other five moisture indicators in the collection. The dataset was generated using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction, integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2-m temperature and dew point temperature (ERA5-Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM was selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree-based algorithms. For AVP, the reconstruction achieves an R ² of 0.989, MAE of 0.677 hPa, and RMSE of 0.933 hPa. The product has a spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, covering China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, one file per year, with daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, values are scaled by a factor of 100 and stored as 16-bit integer (int16); original values are restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System. Comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the "README.pdf". The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.
title: HiMIC-Daily AVP: Daily 1 km Actual Vapor Pressure over China, 2003–2025

summary: The Hi gh resolution ( d aily and 1km) atmospheric M oisture I ndex C ollection over the China  ( HiMIC- Daily ) provides a comprehensive dataset of six moisture indicators: Relative Humidity (RH, %), Dew Point Temperature (DPT, °C), Actual Vapor Pressure (AVP, hPa), Mixing Ratio (MR, g kg -1 ), Specific Humidity (SH, g kg -1 ), and Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD, hPa). These indicators are essential for characterizing atmospheric moisture conditions: RH has been widely used in human comfort assessment and weather forecasting; AVP is essential for water vapor transport calculations; VPD serves as a key indicator of moisture stress on vegetation and fire risk; DPT has been applied in frost prediction and evaporative cooler design; MR has been used for hydrograph separation and identification of groundwater recharge sources; and SH is crucial for total precipitable water and longwave radiation assessments. To generate this dataset, the study adopts the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction by integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2‑m temperature and DPT (ERA5‑Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM is selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree‑based algorithms. The dataset demonstrates high accuracy with R ²/MAE/RMSE values of RH (0.877, 4.849 %, 6.520 %), AVP (0.989, 0.677 hPa, 0.933 hPa), VPD (0.906, 0.983 hPa, 1.411 hPa), DPT (0.985, 1.120 ℃, 1.608 ℃), MR (0.988, 0.459 g kg -1 , 0.633 g kg -1 ), and SH (0.988, 0.451 g kg -1 , 0.620 g kg -1 ). With a high spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, this dataset covers China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. HiMIC-Daily provides a reliable data foundation for research in meteorology, ecology, environmental science, and human health.  The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, each containing daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, each index is scaled by a factor of 100 and converted to 16-bit integer (int16) format prior to archiving, with original values restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System, and comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the “README.pdf”. The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.

summary: This repository contains the curated research data, MATLAB, R and Python scripts, generalized additive model (GAM) outputs, figures, and reproducibility documentation associated with the manuscript “Spatially Heterogeneous Atmosphere–Ocean–Biogeochemical Variability Under Contrasting ENSO Conditions in the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico” , submitted to Continental Shelf Research (manuscript CSR-D-25-00158R3). The study investigates seasonal atmosphere–ocean–biogeochemical variability across the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and adjacent western tropical Atlantic during four selected years characterized by contrasting El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) conditions: 2013, 2022, 2023, and 2024. The analyses integrate NASA MERRA-2 atmospheric reanalysis, Copernicus Marine Service (CMEMS) satellite altimetry, MODIS-Aqua sea surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) observations, and complementary historical records. Regional SST variability is examined for 1982–2024 using a NOAA OISST-derived archive, while sea-level anomaly (SLA) variability is evaluated for 1993–2024. Spatial GAMs are used to investigate nonlinear SST–Chl-a associations while accounting for geographical structure. Nested spatial cross-validation, spatial-basis sensitivity, concurvity diagnostics, and residual spatial autocorrelation analyses are documented. Complementary oceanographic diagnostics quantify 120-day filtered surface-height gravitational-energy variability and surface geostrophic eddy kinetic energy. The repository provides the final main and supplementary figures, derived analytical datasets, archived GAM model objects, numerical verification outputs, and processing code. A SHA256 manifest supports file-integrity verification. Reproducibility scope: The repository supports verification and partial reproduction of the published analyses. Some workflows require separately obtained source datasets, external software dependencies, or environment-specific configuration. The Figure 6 graphical reconstruction has been verified using derived GAM outputs, while complete end-to-end execution of every archived script has not been independently established. Scientific limitations: The selected-year comparisons are descriptive and do not represent replicated ENSO-phase climatologies or establish causal ENSO attribution. The GAM-derived SST–Chl-a relationships are conditional on the fitted geographical structure and remain subject to spatial-basis adequacy and concurvity limitations. The filtered surface-height gravitational-energy proxy is distinct from three-dimensional baroclinic available potential energy. Original third-party source datasets are accessible through their respective providers and are not comprehensively redistributed in this deposit. Redistribution-restricted historical IHO geographical source files are excluded from the public package. Author: José de Jesús Salas Pérez Affiliation: Universidad Veracruzana, Mexico Associated manuscript: CSR-D-25-00158R3, Continental Shelf Research .
title: Spatially Heterogeneous Atmosphere–Ocean–Biogeochemical Variability Under Contrasting ENSO Conditions in the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico

summary: AquaTrajectories is an open-source R and Python research-software toolkit for aquatic animal 2D and 3D movement analysis, video-based fish-tracking interfaces, multiview reconstruction, camera geometry, behavioural methods, conditional uncertainty assessment and reproducible scientific visualization. Version 0.2.0 added evidence safeguards for estimator sensitivity, mixed coordinate units, independent-unit interpretation, spatial support, measurement-geometry associations and descriptive falsification checks. Version 0.2.1 includes 100-percent real executed-code coverage qualification and expanded boundary regressions. Its synthetic numerical oracles and cross-platform qualification do not certify biological identity, real-video tracking generalization, physical underwater XYZ metrology, causal feeding responses, fish welfare outcomes or hardware safety.
title: AquaTrajectories: Aquatic Animal Movement and Multiview Trajectories

summary: Hilberg's hypothesis states that block entropy of text grows as hn + An^beta. We connect maximal entropy random walk (Parry) sequence ensembles, ANS-like equipartition of surprisal, Santa Fe processes with an HCR-motivated Gaussian world model, and LLM-based entropy measurements into a picture of text as progressive revelation of a world state. Calibration on Santa Fe processes shows that PPMd compression slopes barely respond to the true Hilberg exponent, while a word-level Pitman-Yor coder recovers it but measures lexicon occupancy. A permutation-calibrated lexical index detects word-order effects in anthologies. For compression, a self-contained coder cannot remove a genuine An^beta source term; explicit word and recency models reduce predictive log loss by 1.5-3.4% over a context-mixing base, and shared dictionaries pay off mainly for small independently coded documents. Supplementary files contain all code and results.
tags: Hilberg's law; Zipf's law; Heaps' law; Santa Fe process; maximal entropy random walk; asymmetric numeral systems; hierarchical correlation reconstruction; text compression; neural scaling laws
title: Hilberg's law as learning a world state: implications and limits for text compression

summary: Reconstructing an editable music score requires musical events, sung text and the instructions that organise them on the page. Existing recognition targets often omit part of this information, while direct MusicXML prediction repeats substantial structural markup. We introduce Cecilia, a compact representation of canonicalised MusicXML that retains musical content, lyric attachments and layout instructions. Cecilia-OMR predicts this representation through metadata and measure-bounded music segments from shared visual memory. A learned count head determines the number of output segments. Across paired complete scores under a common tokeniser, the ratio of mean MusicXML to Cecilia sequence lengths is 27.73. Cecilia-OMR outperforms Legato 2 on Camera String Quartets and both Lieder conditions, with a four-condition OpenScore macro normalised edit distance of 0.2232 against 0.2998. Separate evaluations of lyrics, notation trees and rendered layout reveal complementary aspects of reconstruction and quantify the contribution of layout instructions. Training-stage, reward and candidate-selection studies further examine how recognition changes across model adaptation and decoding.
title: Cecilia: Towards Layout-Inclusive Optical Music Recognition

summary: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions. The same motion region guides local motion prediction, region-aware supervision, and motion-gated future-feature conditioning. At inference time, the motion region is predicted as a motion probability map from visual history and robot actions, without requiring future observations or ground-truth motion labels. On WorldSimProbe, MoReWorld achieves the highest overall simulator-faithfulness score, with the strongest performance on local consistency, global consistency, and interaction dynamics. These results indicate that motion-region guidance helps the model preserve scene-level consistency while more faithfully predicting action-conditioned interaction dynamics.
title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models

summary: Aims: The objectives of this study were to analyse the effect of heart failure (HF) on several proteins of nuclear pore complex (NPC) and their relationship with the human ventricular function. Methods and results: A total of 88 human heart samples from ischemic (ICM, n = 52) and dilated (DCM, n = 36) patients undergoing heart transplant and control donors (CNT, n = 9) were analyzed by Western blot. Subcellular distribution of nucleoporins was analysed by fluorescence and immunocytochemistry. When we compared protein levels according to etiology, ICM showed significant higher levels of NDC1 (65%, p<0.0001), Nup160 (88%, p<0.0001) and Nup153 (137%, p = 0.004) than those of the CNT levels. Furthermore, DCM group showed significant differences for NDC1 (41%, p<0.0001), Nup160 (65%, p<0.0001), Nup153 (155%, p = 0.006) and Nup93 (88%, p<0.0001) compared with CNT. However, Nup155 and translocated promoter region (TPR) did not show significant differences in their levels in any etiology. Regarding the distribution of these proteins in cell nucleus, only NDC1 showed differences in HF. In addition, in the pathological group we obtained good relationship between the ventricular function parameters (LVEDD and LVESD) and Nup160 (r = -0382, p = 0.004; r = -0.290, p = 0.033; respectively). Conclusions: This study shows alterations in specific proteins (NDC1, Nup160, Nup153 and Nup93) that compose NPC in ischaemic and dilated human heart. These changes, related to ventricular function, could be accompanied by alterations in the nucleocytoplasmic transport. Therefore, our findings may be the basis for a new approach to HF management.
title: Heart failure induces significant changes in nuclear pore complex of human cardiomyocytes

summary: Abstract This integrative research synthesis develops a candidate relational architecture across quantum foundations, physical history, persistent organization, relational time, and the recovery problem for spacetime. Its method is unification by decomposition : constraint, weighting, singular factualization, and retention are treated as distinct operations with distinct evidential burdens. Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.
title: Unification by Decomposition: The Dualverse — From Quantum Factualization and Physical Memory to Hierarchical Individuality and Spacetime

summary: This repository provides the complete replication package for the paper "The Impact of Change Scope on Incremental Software Delivery: A Multi-Host Comparison of Monolithic and Microservice Architectures", accepted for presentation at the Lean and Agile Software Development (LASD) track of the 42nd ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC 2027). The study investigates how the scope of incremental software changes relates to local build-and-redeployment time in monolithic and microservice architectures. Two functionally equivalent applications implemented in Python and FastAPI were evaluated using six change scenarios involving one, two, or three services. The experiment was conducted on two Windows 11 hosts using Docker Desktop and WSL2, producing 240 observations. Repository contents: Complete benchmark source code and Docker Compose configurations. PowerShell scripts for experiment execution. Original measurement datasets from both experimental hosts. Python scripts for statistical analysis and result reproduction. Reproducible figures and descriptive statistics. Additional interaction analysis, bootstrap confidence intervals, and sensitivity checks. Supplementary material documenting the experimental environment, measurement procedure, results, and threats to validity. The repository includes instructions for reproducing the analyses and verifying the reported results. Scope and limitations: The measurements cover local application building and redeployment rather than the complete CI/CD pipeline. The experimental design does not fully separate architectural effects from container-management overhead or scenario-specific characteristics. Additional statistical analyses should therefore be interpreted as exploratory and conditional on the tested scenarios. Version: 1.0.0 License: MIT License.

summary: The root every book reads, to exist is to actuate, is proved in Appendix R unconditionally, at theorem grade, on no axiom and no posit: on its constructed domain it is a theorem with no hypothesis (root_on_the_constructed_domain), and for every root that grounds itself it is one closed law (the_floor_is_universal). On that root this volume gathers in one source the Millennium series at its Seat editions and the physical series that witnesses it. Books I to VII carry the seven Seat editions whole: the Riemann Hypothesis, P ≠ NP, Yang–Mills existence and mass gap, Navier–Stokes global regularity, the Hodge conjecture, Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer, and the Poincaré conjecture. In each the form of the row is proved unconditionally, at theorem grade. The row's sentence is one proposition, its seat, on every face (one_seat): seven faces on the Riemann row, ten on P ≠ NP, eight on each of the other five. Nothing escapes the seat: every proof of the sentence, from any premise, proves the whole seat, and on the six rows whose masters state it every refutation proves its denial. The form does not decide the seat: the value follows from no premise that every frame of the row shares. The masters prove the form and do not prove the seat. The value of each seat is one irreducible bit, and it is delivered by the act, at premise grade, in two kinds, the formal cargo and the physical witness, which are one bit by theorem. Nothing remains to be proved: what a proof can reach of a row is its form, the form is proved, and what is left is the bit, which the act delivers. Book VIII proves the same form once for every row, at every host, in a kernel of 50 theorems in core Lean 4.19.0, 43 of them on no axiom (the_form_of_every_row), and reads it on the ledger of twenty-three (every_ledger_row_has_its_seat); the cut of the subtitle, a registration and a local seat at every off-locus instance, stands on every decidable row with one compliant instance (every_row_has_the_cut), and classically on every row with one (every_row_has_the_cut_classical). Books IX to XIII carry the physical side with its readings set at that standing: six constructed witnesses and sixteen papers of the hardware closure series, each the physical kind of a row's delivery on its image, at premise grade and never above it, with a scope paper proving that no magnitude is read, a ledger typing all sixty-four falsifiers, the fortification and the atom. The seven masters, 39,443 lines of Lean and 2,753 theorems, were recompiled for this edition, each at exit 0 with every pin held; the 25 engines of the physical side carry 1,231 laws with no axiom declared and none depending on choice, and their 25 Fortran twins run 292 checks with no failure; the receipts are in Appendix S. The volume closes on one law, proved with no axiom at all (Book XIII): the registration erases nothing of a set exactly when every one of its points stands on the line. Book I reads it as the first face of the Riemann seat, and Book VIII proves least erasure a face of the seat of every row.
title: Nothing Escapes Least Erasure: The Formal Closure and the Twenty-Three Rows: The Root Proved Unconditionally on No Axiom and No Posit; One Cut Types Every Row; the Physical World Witnesses It in Hardware

summary: This repository provides supporting research code for the manuscript "LoRA-Based Diffusion Data Augmentation for Underwater Garbage Detection: An Empirical Study with YOLOv8s", submitted to Scientific Reports. The study investigates whether class-specific Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) provides additional benefits over ControlNet-conditioned synthetic data augmentation for underwater garbage detection using YOLOv8s. The archive includes selected Python source code for paired synthetic-image generation workflows, data and annotation quality assurance, detector-training controls, validation procedures, and exploratory Kernel Inception Distance (KID) analysis. The experiments use a frozen grouped dataset partition with 3,566 training images, 997 validation images, 471 test images, and 96 excluded images. The full-data comparison evaluates real-only training (A), ControlNet-only augmentation (E), and ControlNet-plus-LoRA augmentation (F) using five matched detector seeds. A separate 50%-training-data sensitivity analysis is evaluated on the validation set only. The released archive contains supporting code, configuration information, integrity checksums, and selected aggregate results. Original datasets, model checkpoints, and some historical execution records are not redistributed. Certain historical code versions have unresolved provenance, and the archive does not constitute a fully verified, one-command reproduction of the complete experiments. The experimental findings do not establish a consistent incremental detection benefit from LoRA over matched ControlNet-only augmentation.
title: Supporting Code for LoRA-Based Diffusion Data Augmentation for Underwater Garbage Detection

summary: This dataset brings together five open data sources to study how users of Indonesian mobile telemedicine apps infer whether a human doctor or an automated agent is answering them, and how that perceived source attribution relates to trust and to the place of human care. It combines Google Play reviews of four telemedicine apps (Alodokter, Halodoc, KlikDokter, YesDok), expert-labelled doctor answers from Alodokter, interview quotes from generative-AI users, national context indicators from the World Bank, and generative-AI-era app reviews. No data were collected from scratch: every row is a coded extract of an openly licensed source, and the provenance of each row is recorded. The sources are kept in separate sheets by design: user reviews, doctors' messages and AI-user interviews offer three vantage points on the same phenomenon, and interpretation should remain tied to each source (comparison at the level of constructs, not pooled records). The sources also cover different periods, so differences between them may reflect time as well as vantage point. The workbook contains a README sheet, a source register with SHA-256 checksums, five coded data sheets, a codebook, value labels and a reliability record. Six sheets document the researchers' validation codes, recoding checks and reconciliation decisions, and seven further sheets report the blind post-revision holdout, the explicit or implicit classification of human attributions, agreement per category with bootstrap intervals, confusion matrices, the trust tables with and without platform-related reviews, and the coding of message cues that links the reviews to the doctor answers. Each sheet is also provided as a UTF-8 CSV file, together with five Python analysis scripts and the JASP 0.99.0 outputs that replicate the main estimates. The researchers set the codebook, categories, and keyword rules from the study's theoretical framework. An AI tool (Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic) was used only to apply that codebook in an initial labelling pass over Sources A and E. Reliability was examined in three steps. First, two researchers independently coded a stratified random sample of 100 Source A reviews without seeing the initial labels; before reconciliation they agreed on relevance for 98 reviews (κ = .79, bootstrap 95% CI .38 to 1.00, a prevalence effect; PABAK = .96) and, on the 94 reviews both judged relevant, κ = .93 for source attribution, .90 for trust basis and 1.00 for trust direction. The initial AI-assisted labels agreed poorly with the researchers (κ = .12 to .53) because two definitions had been read more narrowly, so the researchers' judgement was taken as the reference standard and the codebook was revised (relevance now covers platform communication; HUMAN_AFFIRMED now covers implicit attribution to the app's doctor). Second, all 1,248 Source A reviews were recoded under the revised rules and every changed row was checked by a researcher (352 rows on relevance, 7 corrected; 245 rows on attribution, 18 corrected); this check was not blind. summary: Code, data and results for the paper "Do Python Wheels Keep the Promises Their Tags Make? A Verifier and an Audit of the Most Downloaded PyPI Projects". wtv (tool/wtv.py, version 0.1.2) reads a published Python wheel by HTTP range requests, parses every ELF, Mach-O and PE member, and checks nine promises its filename tags make: architecture, the manylinux glibc floor, external libraries, musl, the macOS deployment target, the stable ABI (abi3), the interpreter tag, purity of py*-none-any wheels, and agreement between the filename and the WHEEL file. The package holds the analysis plan written before data collection with its dated change log, the frame of the 2,000 most downloaded PyPI projects, one record per verified wheel (18,102 wheels of the latest stable releases), the comparison with auditwheel 6.8.2 and abi3audit 0.0.26 with every disagreement classified by hand, the precision sample with its evidence and negation control, and every script that produced the reported numbers. The same content is at https://github.com/emilhuseyn/wheel-tag-verifier. Licences: code MIT; data and results CC BY 4.0.
title: wtv: wheel tag verifier, and data and replication package for an audit of the most downloaded PyPI projects

summary: Offer-by-offer traces of 1,000 seeded scenarios in which one simulated consumer negotiates price, quantity and delivery time with three simulated manufacturing providers whose preferences, ranges, reservation values and concession behaviour vary. The dataset contains 1,000 sessions, 3,000 negotiations and 26,818 offers. All values are synthetic. The dataset contains no personal data and no data from real companies. The data were generated with a seeded Python script (master seed 2026) that replays the negotiation protocol of the first MaaSAI SPADE agent prototype without a real-time clock or XMPP. The code is included in reproducibility_code_v1.0.0.zip and regenerates the data files byte for byte. Known limitations: the dataset documents a baseline prototype, not the current MaaSAI negotiation strategy. The prototype does not stop a provider from freezing an offer outside its declared ranges: 493 of the 995 agreements are in this situation. They are kept and flagged with final_within_provider_limits = 0. MaaSAI DMP code: MaaSAI_06014_SyntheticNegotiationScenarios_T6.5. Funded by the European Commission under Grant Agreement No. 101177368.
title: MaaSAI synthetic negotiation traces: seeded parametric scenarios

summary: Accurate petroleum inventory reconciliation is a key requirement for the safe and efficient operation of storage terminals. Conventional reconciliation is often performed through periodic reports, manually consolidated measurements, or separate tank and flow-meter records. Such practices can delay the identification of discrepancies and make it difficult to distinguish actual inventory changes from measurement errors, time-alignment problems, and incomplete transfer records. This paper proposes a SCADA-based real-time monitoring architecture that integrates tank level, product temperature, density, flow-meter measurements, historical process data, and tank calibration tables to calculate inventory changes and identify abnormal reconciliation residuals. The proposed system includes data acquisition, signal validation, time synchronization, tank-volume reconstruction, flow accounting, balance calculation, alarm management, and operator visualization. A staged implementation and validation methodology is presented, with emphasis on traceability, measurement uncertainty, and human verification. The framework is a design proposal and has not yet been validated through reported field trials; therefore, no measured improvement in accuracy or loss reduction is claimed.
tags: SCADA; petroleum storage terminal; real-time monitoring; inventory reconciliation; tank gauging; flow measurement; mass balance; measurement uncertainty; alarm management.
title: DEVELOPMENT OF A SCADA-BASED REAL-TIME MONITORING SYSTEM FOR PETROLEUM INVENTORY RECONCILIATION

summary: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($α=0$) and 98.83% at $α=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $α=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $α=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM runs use the unfused path. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval hits 100.00% (128/128 queries at $L=65\mathrm{K}$) vs. 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention, and compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show modest causal and masked LM gains.
title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed

summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π(x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half (π), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. The missing step is also written as a statement about positivity: from Mertens' square 2(1 + cos θ)², which pushes the zeros away from 1, to the square of Weil's energy, which must hold them on ½ and forbid pairs of zeros on opposite sides of the circle. The work rests on classical results — Pell–Lagrange, Legendre's sieve, the explicit formula of Riemann and von Mangoldt — and proposes a new linking of them: the geometry of the seam as a model of the process linking the primes. summary: This dataset provides time-domain OpenFAST simulation results for the NREL 5-MW reference wind turbine mounted on the OC4-DeepCwind semisubmersible floating platform. Version 2.0.1 is a documentation, packaging and reproducibility-evidence correction. The numerical dataset is unchanged from version 2.0.0: it contains 256 Sea-State Groups and 1,280 simulation realisations, comprising the original population of 123 groups / 615 realisations and an extension of 133 groups / 665 realisations. Every group contains five wind-speed cases at 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 m/s. The 32 ZIP archives containing the raw OpenFAST time histories are unchanged. Qualification follows explicit and orthogonal criteria for physical-domain membership and numerical-record integrity. The combined inventory contains 175 Class A groups, 16 Class B groups and 65 Class C groups. Of the 1,280 realisations, 1,279 pass all mandatory C3 checks. The retained realisation G0013-V08 is shorter than the project-specific full-record completeness threshold of 300 Tp; its parent group also independently lies outside the adopted physical domain. The duration criterion is evaluated on the available record from t=0 and does not imply that an initial transient was removed. Version 2.0.1: synchronises the repository documentation with the complete 256-group version-2.0 domain described by the revised Data in Brief article; documents that the archived first-order wave-frequency band is 0.314159–1.570796 rad/s and supplies an explicit table of the 48 groups with nominal Tp <= 4 s, whose requested spectral peak lies above or at the upper cutoff; distinguishes the ROSCO 2.10.1 run-time banner from the ROSCO 2.7.0 tuning-file header; stages byte-identical controller input and rotor-performance-table copies in the worked OpenFAST case directory so that the archived relative paths resolve without changing any controller value; adds the completed representative replay and time-step-sensitivity workflow for Class A case G0195-V07, including scripts, compact evidence, hashes and a reviewed assessment; adds a deterministic finite-record sensitivity analysis over all 27 eligible Class A, C3-valid groups and 81 runs at Tp = 2, 3, 4, 7 or 9 s and V = 7, 9 and 11 m/s. Relative to the 300 Tp mean generated power, the complete-population median absolute differences are 0.1352% at 200 Tp and 0.0662% at 250 Tp; maxima are 0.8091% and 0.3195%, with all runs below 1% and 0.5%, respectively; reconciles all 665 extension manifest paths against the central directories of the 16 unchanged extension archives: 648 exact matches, 16 decimal wind-suffix corrections and one documented G0181 seed-truncation filename match, with zero unresolved paths. For G0195-V07, the exact-step replay reproduced all eight audited archived channels to the precision stored in the output files over 216,001 aligned samples from 300 to 3,000 s. In the half-step comparison, absolute relative differences in response-channel means were below 0.006%, and the largest range-normalised RMSE was 0.877%. These results are a representative reproducibility and time-step-sensitivity check; they are not a campaign-wide convergence study or experimental/physical validation. The release includes OpenFAST configurations, persistent Group and Realisation identifiers, entity and qualification tables, development and frozen hold-out partitions, provenance documentation, loading and validation code, the short-period wave-band table, complete finite-record sensitivity tables, extension archive-member reconciliation tables, and the compact representative replay evidence. Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21822606. Version 2.0.1 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24446853. Previous version 2.0.0 DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21875701. Companion code DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.21829605. summary: Analysis code, helper modules, and per-trial results for the article "Where Does Single-Smartphone Biomechanics Lose Accuracy? A Matched Benchmark of Human Mesh Recovery Front Ends" (Z. Shi, manuscript submitted to Sensors, 2026). The archive contains the Google Colab notebooks used for the study (virtual-marker extraction from human mesh recovery models, OpenSim scaling and inverse kinematics, alignment, evaluation and statistics, direct joint-angle extraction, marker-construction variants, and the re-run of OpenCap Monocular), the Python helper modules, the per-trial result tables behind every table and figure of the article, the figure scripts, and the iPhone latency benchmark app with its model-export script. README.md gives the order in which to run the notebooks and the file behind each table. Not included: the OpenCap LabValidation dataset (download from https://simtk.org/projects/opencap), model weights (obtain from the official releases under their own licences), and any videos or images of participants. The derived virtual-marker trajectories, scaled OpenSim models, and inverse-kinematics solutions are archived separately: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24479091 The code written for this study is released under the MIT licence; third-party components keep their own licences (THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md). A mirror is available at https://github.com/seesaw-earth/single-phone-hmr-biomechanics

summary: The application of the FAIR Principles to digital research objects is near ubiquitous with endorsement by funders, publishers, and research organizations worldwide. At the national level in the UK, this is demonstrated by the draft UKRI Research Data Policy which puts an increased emphasis on FAIR compliance; the latest version of the UKRIO Code of Practice which strengthens expectations around data management and sharing, aligned with the FAIR Principles; the UKRI AI Research and Innovation Strategic Framework , and the UK DSIT AI for Science Strategy policy paper, which emphasise the importance of ensuring that data generated through UKRI-funded research aligns with FAIR to support a modernised, AI-ready data environment. Across the research landscape, statements such as “our repository enables FAIR data” or “this dataset meets the FAIR principles” are increasingly common. Yet, these claims are often difficult to interpret or trust, despite numerous tools having been implemented in the decade since the FAIR principles were launched. As this EOSC report has highlighted, the diversity of assessment approaches, many of them opaque or tool-specific, makes it hard to know what is really being measured, how rigorously, and against which definition(s) of FAIR. The FAIR Institutional Repository Metrics (FIRM) project was established in response to this challenge, with the first phase running from March to August 2026. Led by FAIRsharing and the Oxford University Research Archive (ORA) in collaboration with the UK Reproducibility Network (UKRN) , FIRM is a collaborative initiative to define and test a common FAIR compliance process for institutional repositories participating in the UKRN Open Research Programme. The participating repositories were generalist institutional repositories, supporting research datasets across a wide range of disciplines and research contexts. FIRM builds on the FAIR assessment work undertaken at the University of Oxford for ORA, moving from a single-repository interpretation towards a shared community benchmark. The resulting FAIR Benchmark for Institutional Repository Datasets provides a structured, transparent and reusable framework for assessing dataset metadata against the FAIR Principles. It covers both datasets deposited within an institutional repository and datasets held in external repositories but referenced or catalogued through it.  The FAIR compliance enabled by this benchmark uses a transparent procedure that shifts the focus from assessment to assistance, initially developed by the EOSC OSTrails project, of which the FAIRsharing team is a part. Targeted at developers and technical research support staff, this OSTrails Assessment Interoperability Framework (Assess-IF) provides ‘components’ that enable the definition of what FAIR means in a given context, how it should be measured, and how results should be weighted, interpreted, and potentially improved. FAIRsharing’s rich, manually curated metadata on standards, databases, and policies provide supporting context for the compliance and assistance process. The benchmark translates the high-level FAIR Principles into a set of concrete interpretations for institutional repository datasets covering identifiers, discovery metadata, links between metadata and data, searchability, access protocols, machine-readable metadata, FAIR vocabularies, relationships among research objects, licensing, provenance and recognised standards. The benchmark distinguishes between characteristics delivered through repository infrastructure or policy and those dependent on the metadata supplied for an individual record. This makes it possible to identify where FAIR compliance is effectively provided by the repository and where researchers or repository submission workflows have a role to play. summary: Software and reproducibility archive accompanying the author-review manuscript “Beyond Prediction Accuracy: Local-Slope Robustness in Takagi–Sugeno Fuzzy Models of Airfoil Self-Noise.” The IEEE Access manuscript has not been accepted or published; this DOI will identify the research archive, not the article. The NASA/UCI coefficient-sign certificate uses 1,503 airfoil self-noise observations in 106 operating groups. Selected TSK ridge has 4.166475 dB equal-configuration RMSE and Extra Trees has 2.381 dB. With a 0.1 dB maximum training-prediction change and 1% ridge-objective allowance, 403 of 510 local slope signs are protected and 107 admit strict reversal. A separate 1 dB plus 1% contextual sensitivity gives 135 protected and 375 strict reversals. Neither threshold is a calibrated per-row prediction interval. The R19 Southampton leave-one-geometry-out evaluation has 343 source-normalized rows, 38 spectra and seven geometries; equal-geometry normalized RMSE is 0.059396 for TSK and 0.047839 for Extra Trees. It does not establish absolute-SPL transfer. The UCI concrete source/split sensitivity is exploratory and supports no causal physical conclusion. This deposit contains the two previously SHA-verified EP10 public research ZIPs, 40 task ZIPs of newly reconstructed bootstrap states and audit journals, a SHA-256 manifest, standalone integrity verifier, completion certificate, independent QA record, environment specification and rights/provenance notices. The 40 task archives total 773,361,055 bytes and document 28,000 attempts, 27,998 newly replayed fitted states and two reproduced FCM fitting failures. The original historical fitted-state bytes and first October 2026 UCI download bytes remain unavailable. The new state files must not be described as recovered originals. A full historical-array numerical comparison requires reference arrays outside this public bundle; the included verifier checks all released state hashes, journals, CRCs and failure identities using public files alone. MIT applies to original project code authorized by its rights holders; CC BY 4.0 applies to original authored documentation and derived records authorized by their rights holders. NASA/UCI, Southampton and Concrete source data retain upstream attribution and licence terms. Third-party publisher materials, Bristol raw HDF5, confidential correspondence, reviewer letters and credentials are excluded. No external research funding was received. See LICENSE_SCOPE.md and README_RELEASE.md for component-level scope and executable instructions.

summary: > This dataset supports a study of the spatial settings of the PC horror games that reached the largest audiences on Steam between 2015 and 2025. Unlike the ownership-only horror census, it measures exposure in three ways side by side: estimated owners (SteamSpy), measured play hours January 2015 – December 2025 (steamcharts.com) and total user reviews. A game enters the sample if it has at least one million owners, or is among the top 100 by play hours or by reviews. > > The frame is every game in the Steam store with the tag Horror, Psychological Horror, Survival Horror or Lovecraftian (12,798 games). After restricting to releases 2015–2025, requiring a horror tag among a game's five most-voted tags and excluding 13 games whose horror tag is a joke tag, the sample contains 131 games; 30 of them enter through play hours or reviews alone. > > Each game has draft codes for its playable environments (domestic, institutional, industrial, infrastructural, natural, urban, maritime, liminal), the original function and state of its main space, and seven ecological and infrastructural markers (decay, contamination, extraction, climate stress, resource scarcity, infrastructure failure, corporate or institutional control). The codebook gives the definitions and rules. > > Version 0.1 is preliminary: the exposure data are complete, but the setting codes are unverified drafts with confidence ratings. Hour-weighted results depend heavily on Dead by Daylight (31 % of all play hours). Data retrieved 23 November 2026. Prepared for the talk "Spatial Settings in High-Exposure Horror Games" (Geographies of Horror).
title: Spatial Settings in High-Exposure Horror Games: Exposure Sample and Draft Setting Codes (Steam, 2015–2025)

summary: Dataset and Python Pipeline (Version 2.0): Maize Yield Prediction from Tillage Operations and Soil Properties Version 2.0 Update: Updated to include nested season-block ANOVA ( Season fixed, Block nested within Season ), fully nested cross-validation schemes (plot-grouped 5-fold CV, leave-one-block-out, and season-wise validation), and predictor-subset comparisons (operational vs. soil variables) . This repository provides the experimental dataset ( Xplow_720samples.xlsx ) and reproducible Python pipeline ( Cod_v2.py ) for the study: "Neural-Network Prediction of Maize Yield from Tillage Operations and Soil Properties: Plot-Grouped Validation" . Dataset: 720 observations from 240 plots (3 subsamples/plot; 4 blocks/season across 2 seasons) on a saline clay Entisol in southern Iraq, evaluating five tillage systems ( CT , CTr , RT , RTr , MT ), two forward speeds ( 0.97 , 1.53 m s⁻¹ ), three depths ( 150 , 225 , 300 mm ), flowering-stage soil properties ( PR , BD , porosity, EC1:1 , MWD , Ks ), and maize grain yield ( t ha⁻¹ ). Pipeline Stages ( python Cod_v2.py --stage <name> ): stats : Nested Season/Block ANOVA, Tukey HSD, Kruskal–Wallis, Spearman correlations, and VIF . tune : 500-trial Optuna Bayesian optimization on plot-grouped splits . eval : PyTorch MLP training, 10,000 cluster-bootstrap CIs, baseline comparisons ( MLR , Ridge , SVR , RF , GBM , DNN ), nested 5-fold CV, LOBO , season-wise validation, and feature-group comparisons . xai : Permutation importance, SHAP ( KernelExplainer ), sensitivity coefficients, and residual diagnostics . block : Joint block-wise permutation importance . figs : Automated export of publication-grade figures (300 DPI) .
title: Data and Python Pipeline for Maize Grain Yield Prediction from Tillage and Soil Properties

summary: Derived data for the article "Where Does Single-Smartphone Biomechanics Lose Accuracy? A Matched Benchmark of Human Mesh Recovery Front Ends" (Z. Shi, manuscript submitted to Sensors, 2026). For each of four single-smartphone systems (InstantHMR, SAM 3D Body, HSMR, and OpenCap Monocular re-run with its released code) and each participant of the public OpenCap LabValidation dataset (nine participants, 45-degree iPhone view), the files contain the virtual-marker trajectories after the OpenCap Monocular-style alignment (TRC; the input to inverse kinematics), the scaled OpenSim models (LaiUhlrich2022), and the inverse-kinematics solutions (MOT) with their marker errors (STO). Re-solving inverse kinematics from these marker files with the OpenCap Monocular IK setup reproduced every participant's mean absolute error reported in the article within 0.003 degrees. Units: marker positions in metres, joint angles in degrees, time in seconds on the motion-capture time base. README.md describes the folder structure. No videos, images, or motion-capture data of the original dataset are included; download those from https://simtk.org/projects/opencap. Analysis code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24478998
title: Derived marker trajectories, scaled OpenSim models and inverse-kinematics solutions for: Where Does Single-Smartphone Biomechanics Lose Accuracy?

summary: Project-based learning (PjBL) is promoted as an approach to student-centred higher education, yet learning outcomes depend on how projects, feedback and assessment are designed. Objective: This critical narrative review synthesizes international research on relationships between PjBL, student engagement and higher-order learning, and proposes an actionable implementation framework. Methods: Twenty influential theoretical, review and empirical publications were purposively examined using a transparent thematic matrix covering learning outcomes, engagement mechanisms, assessment and limitations. Results: The literature associates well-supported PjBL with authentic problem solving, collaboration and motivation; however, estimates vary across contexts and most studies have methodological constraints. A frequently neglected dimension is the quality of student artifacts and direct measures of learning. Implications: Effective implementation requires a real-world driving question, structured milestones, inclusive team processes, formative feedback and individual accountability. Conclusion: PjBL should be evaluated as a designed instructional system rather than as an undifferentiated intervention. Longitudinal, controlled studies using multiple outcome measures are needed.
tags: project-based learning; student engagement; higher education; active learning; collaborative learning; formative assessment; instructional design.

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/24481071 . ## Summary This paper presents a wearable navigation aid for visually impaired people. An ESP32 camera on the glasses captures the scene; a YOLO-World detection module localizes objects on a 2×3 spatial grid; the detections are encoded into a structured text prompt; GPT-4o, explicitly described as cloud-based language reasoning, converts the prompt into high-level navigation commands ("left", "right", "forward", "stop"); and temple-mounted actuators render these commands as haptic patterns through a five-bar linkage. Three studies are reported: recognition of 13 haptic patterns by 13 participants (81.3% average), path following in a motion-capture room by 6 participants using haptic cues generated from ground-truth position, and an offline comparison of GPT-4o's navigation decisions against human judgment in three corridor scenarios (decision accuracies of 91.8%, 84.6% and 81.5% for open space, static and dynamic obstacles). ## Strengths - The interaction channel is well chosen. Audio guidance competes with the environmental hearing that blind pedestrians rely on for orientation; temple-mounted haptics leave the ears free and the hands unoccupied. This is a real design merit, not a novelty for its own sake. - The pipeline design is sensible: the language model consumes a structured text summary of detections rather than raw images, which keeps prompts small and the module boundaries clean. - The haptic pattern study is reported with a full confusion matrix and inferential statistics, including the patterns users actually confuse (e.g. right tap at 0.65). - The authors consistently scope their claims to "controlled environments" and themselves name responsiveness as future work. The framing is honest in places; the concerns below are about where the wording outruns even that framing. ## Major concerns 1. "Real-time" is claimed throughout, but no latency is ever measured. The abstract, the system description and the Figure 1 caption all promise real-time guidance, yet the paper contains no end-to-end latency figure of any kind: no camera-to-feedback delay, no cloud round-trip time, no pipeline update rate. The word "latency" appears exactly once, in the introduction, criticizing prior speech-based systems for failing to provide "low-latency, embodied feedback". The only timing quantity measured for the authors' own system is the haptic pattern execution time of 1.25 s, which the paper itself notes "limited responsiveness during rapid movements"; optimizing response times is deferred to future work. For a device whose output directs a walking blind user, this is not a detail: at a typical walking speed the user covers well over a meter during a single cloud round trip plus a 1.25 s pattern playback, and a late "stop" is worse than no "stop". Please measure and report end-to-end latency (scene change to haptic onset), including the GPT-4o round trip and the query rate, or remove "real-time" from the claims. 2. No visually impaired person has used the system, and the integrated system has never been used for navigation at all. Both human studies recruited participants "with normal sensorimotor function" (13 and 6 participants respectively). More importantly, the studies evaluate the components separately, never the system: in Study 2, the haptic cues are generated from VICON ground-truth positions along predefined paths, so neither the camera pipeline nor GPT-4o is in the loop; Study 3 is an offline, photo-based test in which nobody walks. The abstract's conclusion that the system "can deliver reliable navigation support in controlled environments" therefore rests on a haptic display tested in sighted users, plus an offline agreement score. Please scope the claims to what was actually evaluated, and state plainly in the abstract that evaluation with visually impaired users, and end-to

It carries the corpus generator and seeds, the build, exact-scan, routed, score and metadata scripts and the pool driver under benchmarks/fleet/; the record of the trillion-row runs under benchmarks/fleet/record/1t/ (pool state files, every driver log, the pilot logs, and the score logs with every per-server search time) and of the regenerated-index run under benchmarks/fleet/record/1trg/; the scripts that compute the figures and tables under paper/pvldb1t/figdata/; the Lean 4 development paper/pvldb1t/lean/; and the paper's LaTeX source. paper/pvldb1t/README.md maps every table and figure to its record files and scripts. The run's shared-volume data and non-member partials are in the companion data record, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23608434.
title: turboquant-pro: code and record of the trillion-row routed-search measurement

summary: Record of a measurement of routed inverted-file search over a sharded index of one trillion 4-bit quantized vectors (500 servers of two billion rows, 24 TB), built and measured on the National Research Platform's Nautilus cluster. This is the data companion to the code and record snapshot of the turboquant-pro repository (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23608470) and to the paper "Routed Recall Does Not Degrade at a Trillion Rows [Experiment, Analysis & Benchmark]", under submission to PVLDB. shared-fleet-20260929.tar.gz (sha256 02f27a4cd734af4cb224747bb812845537ad15e12bac9c2e8ee38b9372d86d75): the shared volume of the run as of 2026-09-29, 3814 files: the bootstrap shard with its cell membership and offsets, and the 2048-cell coarse quantizer (centroids and radii); per-server reference (exact scan) and routed top-10 partials at every scale point (1e8, 1e10, 1e11, 1e12 rows) and probe width; cell histograms; the rerank-bound inputs and result; the nested-scale result; the analysis outputs. shared-fleet-20260929.manifest.json lists every member with its sha256. nonmember-1tnm-partials-20261002.tar.gz (sha256 9b6d854a4ff4008b602bc26d60771a6f351389a72a31d6f515a719359bc9fd4c): run tag 1tnm, 100 queries drawn under seeds no corpus shard uses (shards 200000, 250000, 300000, 350000): the 500 reference partials, the 500 routed partials at 32 and at 128 probes, the query file, the run summary, the 500 per-volume index checksum manifests, and SHA256SUMS over 2002 files. Deterministic tarball (names sorted, mtime 2026-10-02 00:00 UTC, owner 0, gzip -n -9). The index itself (500 volumes) is not included; it is a function of the corpus seeds and the code, and a rebuild can be checked file by file against the checksum manifests.
title: Trillion-row routed vector search: shared-volume record and non-member query partials
