summary: Persistent object maps must incorporate new surfaces while retaining valid identities and correcting earlier associations. We present a map-revision module that separates historical identity changes from new-surface admission. Proposed merges are tested against shared and separate mask explanations across views; a merge is allowed only if its evidence margin remains positive after removing any one observed frame. New measured points are assigned through local identity competition, with a mask witness and a seed-frame stability check. On two preselected KITTI-360 windows, the fixed method increases mean building/car instance AP50:90 from 17.259 to 18.762 under a local evaluation protocol. Controlled output interventions attribute the gains to fragment consolidation, protection against harmful overwrites, and local assignment of new points. Four additional spatial holdouts increase mean AP from 20.263 to 23.171, although unconditional revision is slightly higher at 23.251. The extra seed-frame check yields no AP gain over nearest-seed assignment in either set. A 330-frame garage recording demonstrates offline integration with LiDAR--inertial--visual odometry. These results identify where observation-supported revision improves object maps and where conservative decisions still limit recovery.
title: OmniSLAM: Evidence-Authorized Revision of Persistent Object Maps

summary: Abstract Abstract The geometry in brief. A conditioned state is a geometric object. The laws compatible with what has been observed form a polytope, the credal fibre. Its faces are cut out by the cells of the tables, and its vertices are certified by bases that come in dual pairs: the positive cells of a vertex form a spanning tree of the bipartite graph of the table (a graphic-matroid basis), and the zero cells form the complementary cographic basis, whose normals span the vertex cone. Conditioning maps the fibre onto a polytope of conditional laws, and the probability bands we report are coordinate projections of that polytope. Evidence acts on it by a projective map, an isometry of the Hilbert metric. Sampling noise is described differently: under regular sampling conditions it is asymptotically a Fisher–Rao confidence region, whose square-root image on the round sphere is approximately a spherical cap of radius of order m−1/2. Toric K¨ahler geometry supplies the selected law inside the fibre, its scales and its walls; the chamber complex of the margins supplies the stratification along which all of this changes. The note develops this picture and tests every computable claim against exact, pre-registered checks. A running example. A water authority must decide whether to keep seeding storms with silver iodide. It continues if q = P (above-normal rain | seeded, wet forecast) is at least a cost ratio θ. The records arrive in pieces: monthly flight counts, monthly rain categories, and later the 2 × 3 table of seeded and unseeded storms against above-normal, normal and below-normal rain. We follow this one synthetic data stream through the whole construction and back to the decision (Studies 83–90, held-out seeds, every check pre-registered and frozen with SHA-256). The data give a credal fibre and its probability bands; the margins give toric chambers and walls; the margins also set the mirror potential of the degree-six del Pezzo surface, whose thimbles form an exceptional collection in its Fukaya–Seidel category. The experiment is a carrier for a realistic decision problem, not a claim about seeding. What the example verifies. Each layer is tested on held-out data: (i) credal walls lie on the chamber walls, while Stokes events are mutations; (ii) margin-order ties are collision walls where two orthogonal objects swap, confirmed at the Floer level on 10 of 12 brackets (the other two, one not audited and one with a non-minimal representative, stay in the record); (iii) a full twist of the potential acts as the Serre functor; (iv) the support region of a vector-valued hypothesis is cut out by Markov moves on the table; (v) poisoning that preserves the margins cannot move a credal decision, though it flips conventional ones (6 flips against 0); (vi) caustics, where two critical points merge, are A2 folds acting by σ±3. What it does not verify. Nothing here concerns real data or whether seeding works. Three problems remain open after a registered repair, with their checks recorded as failed: chamber reuse after one Stokes event, the control bracket of Study 83 (and the held-out bracket with the same defect), and coherence of the lift on a full slice. Every failed check is kept in the record. Categorical status. In Seidel’s framework the thimbles generate and the identification of their category with the derived category of the surface is proved (lemma 262, corollary 263). Only 1 the wrapped version in the sense of Ganatra–Pardon–Shende still rests on two steps that are argued, not certified. The rest of the note. Part I identifies the state selected by a toric potential as the lexico- graphic max–min point, up to O(1/ log(1/T )), and writes the K¨ahler dictionary in probabilistic language. Part II reads it on contingency tables, where one count of data can cross a wall. Part III treats composition, contextuality, the value of information and poisone

summary: Data, codebook, prompt, model outputs and code for a study of Chile's General Rule (NCG) No. 461 and corporate climate risk disclosure. The package contains a 20-item Climate Risk Disclosure Index (CRDI) aligned with IFRS S2 for 370 annual reports of 54 non-financial firms listed in Santiago (fiscal years 2019–2025), coded by a large language model (Gemini 3.1 Pro) in three independent runs with page-level quotations; a human audit of the model's evidence for 20 reports (400 report-items); a blind manual recoding of 10 of those reports (200 report-items) and the adjudication of the disagreements; the firm-year panel with market and accounting variables; and the scripts that collect the reports, code them and estimate all difference-in-differences, event-study and fixed-effects models. Version 1.2.0 adds the blind recoding and adjudication (coding/blind_validation), with a script that reproduces the agreement statistics reported in the article.
title: Replication package for: Does Mandatory Integrated Reporting Improve Climate Risk Disclosure? Evidence from Chile's Staggered Mandate

\frac{t}{t_{\text{evap}}}\right)^{1/3}\). نقطه بازگشت منحنی پیج زمانی رخ می‌دهد که انتروپی تابش خروجی برابر با انتروپی باقی‌مانده افق رویداد شود (\(S_{\text{rad}}(t_{\text{Page}}) = S_{\text{BH}}(t_{\text{Page}})\)): \(1-\left(\frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}\right)^{2}=\left(\frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}\right)^{2}\implies \frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 0.707107\implies t_{\text{Page}}=\left(1-2^{-3/2}\right)t_{\text{evap}}\approx 0.64645\,t_{\text{evap}}\) نقص اصلی در مدل نیمه‌کلاسیک استاندارد: در فضای ۴ بعدی پیوسته، انتروپی تابش به صورت \(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{Hawking}}(t) = S_{\text{BH},0} \left[1 - summary: معما و پارادوکس ۲۱ از ۱۰۰: پارادوکس منحنی پیج و آنتروپی درهم‌تنیدگی تابش هاوکینگ (The Page Curve Paradox) این پارادوکس که در سال ۱۹۹۳ توسط دان پیج فرموله شد، نسخه کمی و دقیقِ بحران اطلاعات سیاه‌چاله است: اگر یک سیاه‌چاله از یک حالت کوانتومی خالص (\(S_{\text{ent}} = 0\)) تشکیل شود و طبق مکانیک کوانتومی به صورت یکانی (Unitary) تبخیر گردد، آنتروپی درهم‌تنیدگی (فون نویمان) تابش خروجی هاوکینگ (\(S_{\text{rad}}(t)\)) باید ابتدا افزایش یابد، در زمان پیج (\(t_{\text{Page}}\)) به بیشینه خود برسد، و سپس با کوچک شدن افق رویداد کاهش یافته و در پایان تبخیر به صفر مطلق بازگردد. اما محاسبه نیمه‌کلاسیک هاوکینگ نشان می‌دهد که \(S_{\text{rad}}(t)\) به صورت یکنواخت رشد می‌کند و در پایان تبخیر از انتروپی بکنشتاین-هاوکینگ سیاه‌چاله (\(S_{\text{BH}}(t)\)) فراتر می‌رود که اصل یکانی بودن مکانیک کوانتومی را نقض می‌کند. ۱. صورت معما و مقیاس‌های رصدی و نظری (Bekenstein-Hawking & Island Formula Benchmarks) داده‌های رصدی و مقیاس‌های فیزیکی مرجع (سیاه‌چاله کلان‌جرم Sagittarius A* و سیاه‌چاله ستاره‌ای GW150914): سیاه‌چاله ستاره‌ای ادغام LIGO GW150914 (جرم نهایی \(M_0 = 62 M_\odot \approx 1.233 \times 10^{32} \text{ kg}\)): انتروپی اولیه بکنشتاین-هاوکینگ (\(S_{\text{BH}, 0} = \frac{4\pi k_B G M_0^2}{\hbar c}\)): \(S_{\text{BH},0}\approx 4.034\times 10^{80}\,k_{B}\quad (\text{معادل }5.82\times 10^{80}\text{ بیت اطلاعات})\) سیاه‌چاله کلان‌جرم کمان ای* (Sagittarius A* — \(M_0 = 4.297 \times 10^6 M_\odot\)): انتروپی اولیه بکنشتاین-هاوکینگ: \(S_{\text{BH}, 0} \approx 1.937 \times 10^{90} \, k_B\) زمان پیج (\(t_{\text{Page}}\)) و کسر جرم بحرانی: در مدل تبخیر هاوکینگ \(\frac{dM}{dt} \propto -M^{-2} \implies M(t) = M_0 \left(1 - \frac{t}{t_{\text{evap}}}\right)^{1/3}\). نقطه بازگشت منحنی پیج زمانی رخ می‌دهد که انتروپی تابش خروجی برابر با انتروپی باقی‌مانده افق رویداد شود (\(S_{\text{rad}}(t_{\text{Page}}) = S_{\text{BH}}(t_{\text{Page}})\)): \(1-\left(\frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}\right)^{2}=\left(\frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}\right)^{2}\implies \frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 0.707107\implies t_{\text{Page}}=\left(1-2^{-3/2}\right)t_{\text{evap}}\approx 0.64645\,t_{\text{evap}}\) نقص اصلی در مدل نیمه‌کلاسیک استاندارد: در فضای ۴ بعدی پیوسته، انتروپی تابش به صورت \(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{Hawking}}(t) = S_{\text{BH},0} \left[1 - \left(\frac{M(t)}{M_0}\right)^2\right]\) محاسبه می‌شود که در انتهای تبخیر به \(S_{\text{BH},0} > 0\) می‌رسد؛ در حالی که مدل‌های «جزیره کوانتومی» (Quantum Extremal Islands - Penington, Almheiri et al.) مجبور به دوختن دستی یک عملگر کمینه ( min ) ناپیوسته در زمان پیج هستند که دارای شکستگی تیز (Cusp / غیرمشتق‌پذیر) در \(t = t_{\text{Page}}\) است. ۲. مقایسه معادلات: فیزیک استاندارد در برابر مدل حمزه (HIP-1155) الف) مدل استاندارد (منحنی هاوکینگ واگرا در برابر منحنی ناپیوسته پیج) منحنی نیمه‌کلاسیک هاوکینگ (نقض یکانی بودن): \(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{Hawking}}(x)=S_{0}\cdot (1-x)\quad ,\quad x(t)=\left(\frac{M(t)}{M_{0}}\right)^{2}\in [0,1]\) منحنی پیج با فرمول جزیره (دارای ناپیوستگی مشتق در \(x = \frac{1}{2}\)): \(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{Island}}(x)=S_{0}\cdot \min \left(1-x\,,\,x\right)\) این فرمول در نقطه \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) (زمان پیج) دارای زاویه تیز (Cusp) است و مشتق زمانی آن پرش ناپیوسته دارد. ب) فرمول‌بندی غیر-دوری مدل اطلاعاتی حمزه (HIP-1155) در چارچوب HIP-1155، منحنی پیج یک تابع کاملاً هموار، تحلیلی و مشتق‌پذیر (\(C^{\infty }\)) است که بدون نیاز به عملگر دست‌ساز min(...) و بدون هیچ شکستگی تیز در زمان پیج، مستقیماً از همبستگی دوگانه میان لایه ۱ (ابعاد ۱ تا ۱۶۵) و دروازه ۶ (لایه شبکه: ابعاد ۸۲۶ تا ۹۹۰) به دست می‌آید: معادله انتروپی درهم‌تنیدگی هموار حمزه (\(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{HIP}}(x)\)): با تعریف \(x(t) = \left(\frac{M(t)}{M_0}\right)^2 \in [0, 1]\) به عنوان کسر مساحت افق باقی‌مانده و \(1 - x(t)\) به عنوان کسر مساحت تبخیرشده، آنتروپی درهم‌تنیدگی از طریق میانگین هارمونیک-اطلاعاتی دروازه‌های ۱ و ۶ (تنظیم‌

summary: معما و پارادوکس ۲۱ از ۱۰۰: پارادوکس منحنی پیج و آنتروپی درهم‌تنیدگی تابش هاوکینگ (The Page Curve Paradox) این پارادوکس که در سال ۱۹۹۳ توسط دان پیج فرموله شد، نسخه کمی و دقیقِ بحران اطلاعات سیاه‌چاله است: اگر یک سیاه‌چاله از یک حالت کوانتومی خالص (\(S_{\text{ent}} = 0\)) تشکیل شود و طبق مکانیک کوانتومی به صورت یکانی (Unitary) تبخیر گردد، آنتروپی درهم‌تنیدگی (فون نویمان) تابش خروجی هاوکینگ (\(S_{\text{rad}}(t)\)) باید ابتدا افزایش یابد، در زمان پیج (\(t_{\text{Page}}\)) به بیشینه خود برسد، و سپس با کوچک شدن افق رویداد کاهش یافته و در پایان تبخیر به صفر مطلق بازگردد. اما محاسبه نیمه‌کلاسیک هاوکینگ نشان می‌دهد که \(S_{\text{rad}}(t)\) به صورت یکنواخت رشد می‌کند و در پایان تبخیر از انتروپی بکنشتاین-هاوکینگ سیاه‌چاله (\(S_{\text{BH}}(t)\)) فراتر می‌رود که اصل یکانی بودن مکانیک کوانتومی را نقض می‌کند. ۱. صورت معما و مقیاس‌های رصدی و نظری (Bekenstein-Hawking & Island Formula Benchmarks) داده‌های رصدی و مقیاس‌های فیزیکی مرجع (سیاه‌چاله کلان‌جرم Sagittarius A* و سیاه‌چاله ستاره‌ای GW150914): سیاه‌چاله ستاره‌ای ادغام LIGO GW150914 (جرم نهایی \(M_0 = 62 M_\odot \approx 1.233 \times 10^{32} \text{ kg}\)): انتروپی اولیه بکنشتاین-هاوکینگ (\(S_{\text{BH}, 0} = \frac{4\pi k_B G M_0^2}{\hbar c}\)): \(S_{\text{BH},0}\approx 4.034\times 10^{80}\,k_{B}\quad (\text{معادل }5.82\times 10^{80}\text{ بیت اطلاعات})\) سیاه‌چاله کلان‌جرم کمان ای* (Sagittarius A* — \(M_0 = 4.297 \times 10^6 M_\odot\)): انتروپی اولیه بکنشتاین-هاوکینگ: \(S_{\text{BH}, 0} \approx 1.937 \times 10^{90} \, k_B\) زمان پیج (\(t_{\text{Page}}\)) و کسر جرم بحرانی: در مدل تبخیر هاوکینگ \(\frac{dM}{dt} \propto -M^{-2} \implies M(t) = M_0 \left(1 - \frac{t}{t_{\text{evap}}}\right)^{1/3}\). نقطه بازگشت منحنی پیج زمانی رخ می‌دهد که انتروپی تابش خروجی برابر با انتروپی باقی‌مانده افق رویداد شود (\(S_{\text{rad}}(t_{\text{Page}}) = S_{\text{BH}}(t_{\text{Page}})\)): \(1-\left(\frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}\right)^{2}=\left(\frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}\right)^{2}\implies \frac{M(t_{\text{Page}})}{M_{0}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\approx 0.707107\implies t_{\text{Page}}=\left(1-2^{-3/2}\right)t_{\text{evap}}\approx 0.64645\,t_{\text{evap}}\) نقص اصلی در مدل نیمه‌کلاسیک استاندارد: در فضای ۴ بعدی پیوسته، انتروپی تابش به صورت \(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{Hawking}}(t) = S_{\text{BH},0} \left[1 - \left(\frac{M(t)}{M_0}\right)^2\right]\) محاسبه می‌شود که در انتهای تبخیر به \(S_{\text{BH},0} > 0\) می‌رسد؛ در حالی که مدل‌های «جزیره کوانتومی» (Quantum Extremal Islands - Penington, Almheiri et al.) مجبور به دوختن دستی یک عملگر کمینه ( min ) ناپیوسته در زمان پیج هستند که دارای شکستگی تیز (Cusp / غیرمشتق‌پذیر) در \(t = t_{\text{Page}}\) است. ۲. مقایسه معادلات: فیزیک استاندارد در برابر مدل حمزه (HIP-1155) الف) مدل استاندارد (منحنی هاوکینگ واگرا در برابر منحنی ناپیوسته پیج) منحنی نیمه‌کلاسیک هاوکینگ (نقض یکانی بودن): \(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{Hawking}}(x)=S_{0}\cdot (1-x)\quad ,\quad x(t)=\left(\frac{M(t)}{M_{0}}\right)^{2}\in [0,1]\) منحنی پیج با فرمول جزیره (دارای ناپیوستگی مشتق در \(x = \frac{1}{2}\)): \(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{Island}}(x)=S_{0}\cdot \min \left(1-x\,,\,x\right)\) این فرمول در نقطه \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) (زمان پیج) دارای زاویه تیز (Cusp) است و مشتق زمانی آن پرش ناپیوسته دارد. ب) فرمول‌بندی غیر-دوری مدل اطلاعاتی حمزه (HIP-1155) در چارچوب HIP-1155، منحنی پیج یک تابع کاملاً هموار، تحلیلی و مشتق‌پذیر (\(C^{\infty }\)) است که بدون نیاز به عملگر دست‌ساز min(...) و بدون هیچ شکستگی تیز در زمان پیج، مستقیماً از همبستگی دوگانه میان لایه ۱ (ابعاد ۱ تا ۱۶۵) و دروازه ۶ (لایه شبکه: ابعاد ۸۲۶ تا ۹۹۰) به دست می‌آید: معادله انتروپی درهم‌تنیدگی هموار حمزه (\(S_{\text{rad}}^{\text{HIP}}(x)\)): با تعریف \(x(t) = \left(\frac{M(t)}{M_0}\right)^2 \in [0, 1]\) به عنوان کسر مساحت افق باقی‌مانده و \(1 - x(t)\) به عنوان کسر مساحت تبخیرشده، آنتروپی درهم‌تنیدگی از طریق میانگین هارمونیک-اطلاعاتی دروازه‌های ۱ و ۶ (تنظیم‌

summary: Pre-registered protocol, code and input data for an external confirmation of a one-hour-ahead electrical load forecasting benchmark. Models were developed on the Paraguayan national load series (2008–2022); this record fixes, before forecast performance on the Brazilian test (2024–2025) and confirmation (2026) periods is examined, the complete protocol for evaluating them on the South subsystem of the Brazilian interconnected system (ONS). Contents: protocol (PDF), analysis code, Kaggle notebooks, Brazil load and weather inputs (ONS, Open-Meteo ERA5 and GFS; CC BY 4.0), Paraguay development results, and SHA-256 checksums.
title: Pre-registered confirmation protocol: one-hour-ahead load forecasting, Paraguay to Brazil South

Models were developed on the Paraguayan national load series (2008–2022); this record fixes, before forecast performance on the Brazilian test (2024–2025) and confirmation (2026) periods is examined, the complete protocol for evaluating them on the South subsystem of the Brazilian interconnected system (ONS). Contents: protocol (PDF), analysis code, Kaggle notebooks, Brazil load and weather inputs (ONS, Open-Meteo ERA5 and GFS; CC BY 4.0), Paraguay development results, and SHA-256 checksums.
title: Pre-registered confirmation protocol: one-hour-ahead load forecasting, Paraguay to Brazil South

summary: Analysis code, processed summary results, figures, supplementary tables, audit report, and manuscript files for a public-data transcriptomic study of intra-abdominal sepsis. Raw GEO data are not redistributed and are available under GSE65682, GSE95233, GSE57065, and GSE294745. The study reports reproducible immunothrombotic separation of abdominal sepsis from gastrointestinal controls, external septic shock cohort replication, poor external LASSO calibration, and no independent 28-day mortality association.
tags: intra-abdominal sepsis; immunothrombosis; transcriptomics; neutrophil extracellular traps; platelets; bioinformatics; machine learning
title: Immunothrombotic transcriptomic reprogramming distinguishes intra-abdominal sepsis and is reproducible in septic shock cohorts

summary: Statistical data covering Uzbekistan's 14 regions over 2011–2025 are used to estimate the short- and long-run effects of entrepreneurship, economic development, transport infrastructure, and foreign trade on regional investment activity. The study employs static panel models and a fixed-effects panel ARDL(1,1) model to estimate long-run coefficients and the speed of adjustment towards equilibrium. All computations were performed in Python using the NumPy and SciPy libraries. The findings indicate substantial persistence in regional investment activity, with a lagged dependent variable coefficient of 0.65, implying that approximately 35% of deviations from long-run equilibrium are corrected annually. In the long run, transport infrastructure emerges as the only factor exhibiting robust statistical results, with an estimated elasticity of 1.20. The model is used to forecast regional investment shares for 2026–2028. However, an out-of-sample evaluation for 2023–2025 reveals that the model performs less accurately than a naive forecasting benchmark. Accordingly, a combined forecasting approach is proposed to improve the reliability of the projections.
title: ECONOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF THE FACTORS AFFECTING THE USE OF REGIONAL INVESTMENT POTENTIAL AND A FORECASTING MODEL

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation over book-length documents must locate a small, coherent set of passages inside tens of thousands of tokens. Flat dense retrieval ignores document structure; RAPTOR instead builds a hierarchy by recursively clustering and summarizing with a language model. We study a complementary design that exploits the native structure of a document: a two-level retriever that (i) selects chapters with a hybrid BM25+dense match over chapter recaps, (ii) runs a chapter-filtered dense search, and (iii) expands top passages into contiguous, section-aware spans under a token budget, plus content-hash-gated delta ingestion to keep the index cheap to update. We evaluate on five public-domain books (113 chapter-localization queries) and on QuALITY and NovelQA (200K+ token novels). In-house, we find a seed-stable precision/ranking tradeoff: with section expansion off, hierarchical retrieval returns a higher fraction of chunks from the correct chapter (+3.3pp, Wilcoxon p=0.014); with expansion on, ranking improves (MRR, p=0.040). Accuracy differences are not significant. On QuALITY, hierarchical retrieval beats flat top-k (81.0% vs 70.4%, p=0.0019) and matches the full article (p=0.74). On NovelQA, hierarchical and flat retrieval are statistically tied (55.7% vs 56.8%, p=0.24); hierarchy helps aggregation questions while flat wins on localized facts. Against a faithful RAPTOR baseline we find a complementary tradeoff, not superiority. Delta ingestion reuses 94 to 99.7% of embeddings on incremental edits. We make no claim of semantic chapter-boundary inference and scope claims to English narrative prose.
title: Structure-Exploiting Hierarchical Retrieval for Long Narrative Documents: A Precision-Oriented Alternative to Learned Abstraction Trees

summary: Multi-step retrieval over long contexts is a key capability for retrieval-augmented generation, but strong existing approaches are costly and complex to train. Supervised retrievers are far simpler and cheaper, yet they fall well behind in this setting. We show that this gap stems not from supervised training itself, but from three misalignments between training and inference: easy training negatives, noisy retrieval prefixes, and position-agnostic scoring. Guided by this analysis, we introduce S$^2$LMR, a simple yet effective supervised sequential retriever that models multi-step retrieval as the evolution of an explicit textual state encoded by a single shared Transformer. On long-context reasoning, multi-hop QA, and needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks with context lengths ranging from 4K to 10M tokens, S$^2$LMR achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods, substantially outperforming prior supervised retrievers. Notably, it requires only $\sim$2 hours of training on a single A6000 for contexts of up to 10M tokens, while remaining robust across a wide range of hyperparameter settings.
title: S$^2$LMR: Supervised Sequential Long-Context Multi-Step Retriever

summary: Practical highway infrastructure inspection entails progressive diagnostic reasoning from visual perception to maintenance decisions, yet existing benchmarks remain confined to isolated tasks, leaving Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) insufficiently evaluated across sequential inspection stages. Meanwhile, current datasets focus primarily on highway pavement defects, falling short of real-world inspection across diverse infrastructure components such as highway pavements, guardrails, glare screens, and drainage systems. To address these gaps, we formulate the Highway Infrastructure Inspection Progression Chain (HIIP-Chain), spanning Anomaly Detection, Anomaly Recognition, Condition Analysis, and Maintenance Resolution, and introduce HighwayVerse. HighwayVerse comprises 14,143 real-world Ground and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) inspection records spanning 100 and 17 anomaly categories, respectively, with 84,858 expert-reviewed question-answer pairs. We evaluate 12 open-source and closed-source MLLMs using the chained metric Final, which credits a correct maintenance decision only when all preceding diagnostic stages are completed correctly. Results show that although models achieve relatively high accuracy when initially judging whether an anomaly is present, their markedly lower Final scores expose struggles across downstream recognition, analysis, and decision-making. This discrepancy indicates that current MLLMs do not fully comprehend specific highway anomaly patterns beyond superficial initial judgments. Furthermore, we propose LaneRAG, a training-free retrieval-augmented framework that provides hierarchical reference guidance achieving consistent performance improvements across diverse MLLMs. Our dataset, evaluation benchmark, and source code will be publicly released.
title: HighwayVerse: A Chain-of-Inspection Benchmark for Highway Infrastructure Anomaly Understanding

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is known to reduce training-data leakage in single-turn interactions, but whether this protection persists over multi-turn conversations is unclear. We introduce CRELT (Conversational RAG Extraction Leakage Trajectory), a reusable framework that tracks, turn by turn, the real contact details from the training data that a RAG system discloses. CRELT separates retrieval, conversation history, and attack strategy through a full-factorial design, uses a retrieval corpus verified to contain none of the target PII, and counts an item as leaked only when it is absent from the model input at the turn it is produced. In our main experiment, this criterion excludes 29-53% of raw matches that were already present in the input. Across GPT-J-6B, Pythia-6.9B, and Pythia-12B, targeting real Enron contact details, retrieval reduces disclosure under both full and cleared history, consistent with prior single-turn results. A length-matched control with random passages reproduces 91-99.5% of this reduction under cleared history and 47-78% under full history, so much of it comes from the added context rather than from what is retrieved. With retrieval enabled, however, retaining full conversation history increases disclosure by a factor of 3.6-4.9, while retaining only one previous turn already restores disclosure to approximately the full-history level. With retrieval, clearing the history reduces disclosure by 72-79%, but does not eliminate it. These results show that single-turn privacy audits can substantially underestimate training-data leakage in conversational RAG systems and that conversation-history policy is a critical dimension of privacy evaluation.
title: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG

summary: Collecting self-reported risk information and maintaining continuity between assessment, explanation, and follow-up are practical components of a lung cancer screening workflow. We present Aegis, a browser-based research prototype that combines a conversational questionnaire, rule-based risk categorization, downloadable reports, retrieval-augmented health information, and doctor-user communication. A session-oriented controller manages question progression and clarification, while a language model assists with answer validation. Structured responses are passed to a separate risk-analysis module, and reports are linked to user and session records through Firebase services. The project adopts a multi-agent design that separates information collection, validation, assessment, and report generation. Its documented verification scope comprises 45 functional test specifications covering account management, questionnaire interaction, reporting, doctor-side review, and consultation. The available evaluation describes workflow behavior qualitatively; it provides no per-case execution results, clinical cohort, predictive-performance measurements, or comparative experiments. We therefore present Aegis as an engineering prototype for organizing risk information and follow-up, with clinical validity and the benefits of its agent-based design remaining unestablished. The paper describes the implementation, distinguishes implemented workflows from incomplete extensions, and identifies the evidence required for reproducible and clinically meaningful evaluation.
title: Aegis: A Conversational Prototype for Lung Cancer Risk Information and Follow-up

summary: Retrieval-augmented language models answer well when the relevant document comes first or last and poorly when it sits in the middle. Some fine-tuning recipes lift the middle by lowering the start. We show how training contexts teach positional bias. With a uniform answer slot and shuffled distractors, the optimal reader ignores position. Building on this result, Exchangeable Self-Distillation (ExSD) trains a small adapter on shuffled contexts to reproduce the model's answer when it reads the answer document alone. It needs no gold answers and only a few thousand examples. On six models from 1.5B to 32B parameters, ExSD raises both average and worst-position accuracy against the frozen model, including on a held-out test split. In controlled LoRA comparisons, it significantly improves both criteria over Pos2Distill. Against CORD, mean differences are not significant, while worst-position accuracy improves significantly in the 20- and 30-document settings. ExSD also matches or beats gold-answer fine-tuning, changes behavior on other tasks far less, and transfers to unseen tasks. Head probes show greater reliance on content over position.
title: Make Position Uninformative: Exchangeable Self-Distillation Flattens the Lost-in-the-Middle Curve

summary: Differentially private zeroth-order optimization (DPZO) is a promising approach for privacy-preserving LLM fine-tuning, offering exceptional memory efficiency. However, its utility is highly sensitive to the clipping threshold $C$, a key DP-specific hyperparameter that controls the trade-off between noise injection and clipping bias. Existing DPZO methods typically tune $C$ by repeatedly evaluating candidate values and reporting the best result, which is computationally expensive and incurs additional privacy cost that must be accounted for under DP. Designing a practical DP procedure for selecting $C$ in DPZO is challenging because no fixed choice performs well across settings, straightforward search-based strategies suffer from poor utility and efficiency, and existing clipping-selection methods for DPSGD do not transfer well to DPZO due to its fundamentally different error regime. In this paper, we propose AutoClip-DPZO, a practical DP method that automatically and efficiently selects $C$ for DPZO. Our key idea is to avoid fine-tuning-based search by reducing clipping selection to a private quantile estimation problem, where the target quantile depends only on public privacy and training parameters. To derive this selection rule, we develop a novel characterization of DPZO error as a function of $C$ that captures both noise variance and clipping bias while remaining accurate and easy to optimize. Experiments show that AutoClip-DPZO achieves utility comparable to that obtained with the optimal $C$, while avoiding repeated fine-tuning-based search and incurring negligible additional overhead. Moreover, AutoClip-DPZO does not rely on sensitive hyperparameters.
title: AutoClip-DPZO: Practical Private Clipping Selection for Differentially Private Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning

summary: We propose the Flow Matching Surface Neural Operator (FMSNO), which combines learning a shared map from irregular surface meshes to a regular two-dimensional grid on the sphere and training a neural operator on the regular grid. Constructing a separate map for each new geometry can dominate inference time on large meshes. We initially pretrain the mapping by flow matching using precomputed optimal transport maps as targets and then continue its training using combined geometry and CFD objectives. We apply it to unseen geometries in a single forward pass. The learned flow deforms the surface points, and we project its endpoints onto the sphere. We then splat geometric features onto the spherical grid, apply a neural operator (we tested both Fourier and Spherical Fourier Neural Operators), and interpolate its output back to the surface. For a mesh with $N$ points, evaluating the map costs O(N), and the full prediction costs O(NlogN) with the FNO backbone. We evaluate surface pressure prediction on ShapeNet-Car, AhmedML, and DrivAerNet++, and drag coefficient prediction on DrivAerNet++. Across the three pressure benchmarks, our accuracy is on par with that of the most accurate baseline. On a surface with one million points, our method achieves a 354x end-to-end inference speedup over that baseline while keeping the same memory usage asymptotics of O(N).
title: FMSNO: Scaling Surface Neural Operators by Learned Flow Matching Reparametrisation

summary: Node affinity prediction in the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB) asks how a node's future interactions will be distributed over other nodes. On this task, methods that reuse past ground-truth labels often outperform temporal graph neural networks, and the state of the art builds on them. Such comparisons assume a point-in-time correct evaluation, in which a model receives only information available at prediction time. Drawing on as-of joins and bitemporal databases, we formalize this requirement by distinguishing when a label must be predicted, its query time, from when it is fully determined, its availability time, and we audit the four TGB node affinity datasets and their evaluation loop with model-agnostic tools. None of the four meets it. On three datasets, each label summarizes a single day about five days after its timestamp, not the documented following week, yet the loop feeds it back right after that timestamp; on the fourth, the loop processes the edges from which each label is computed before predicting it. Under a drop-in leakage-free protocol, every method whose inputs leak loses up to 17% of its NDCG@10, the advantage of past labels over the interaction stream nearly vanishes or reverses, and both the best configuration of the state of the art and the rankings change; a blend of training-free long-memory statistics, with weights fit on validation data, matches or exceeds the state of the art under both protocols. Point-in-time correctness should therefore be built into benchmarks, and our tools carry over to other benchmarks whose labels aggregate event streams over time windows.
title: Temporal Leakage Distorts the TGB Node Affinity Leaderboard: A Point-in-Time Audit

summary: AI agents accumulate conversations, images, and documents through long-term interactions with users. Answering later questions often requires connecting evidence across these records, yet the resulting understanding is rarely retained, allowing mistakes to recur on related questions. Existing multimodal memory methods largely focus on storing and retrieving records, with limited mechanisms for learning from completed tasks and consolidating task-specific experience. We therefore propose MMMem, a task-aware multimodal memory framework that extracts and consolidates experience from completed tasks through four complementary strategies. First, source-linked multi-view memory organizes original text, images, and rendered pages alongside generated scene images that combine clues across records for retrieval. Second, source-generated tasks support knowledge alignment at two levels: warm-up consolidates source knowledge into task-relevant experiences in external memory, while self-training adapts the model's parametric knowledge to task demands. Third, the same vision-language model distills completed tasks into experiences that record the task context, conclusion, and support links. Finally, task-aware retrieval recalls source views and relevant experiences for answering and verification, while source-supported reuse guides long-term retention. Across three memory benchmarks and two vision-language readers, MMMem outperforms eight baselines. With Qwen3.5-9B, MMMem achieves relative gains of 36.9%, 17.6%, and 15.2% over the best-performing baselines on LoCoMo, Mem-Gallery, and LooGLE v2, respectively. Ablations show consistent gains from training and memory warm-up, while case studies illustrate how individual components work in practice.
title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation

summary: Long-lived Web assistants require effective memory and retrieval mechanisms to access information from past user interactions. While these capabilities can be learned through specialized policies, it remains unclear whether specialists trained independently in different environments can be effectively composed without joint optimization. This paper investigates compositional transfer through policy distillation. Memory-writing and sequential retrieval policies are independently distilled from frontier-model action trajectories into 3B models and combined with a fixed answer generator without downstream training. On a LongMemEval-based benchmark, the distilled composition achieves 73.1% accuracy, compared with 36.2% for a composition of existing RL-trained specialists, and also outperforms the evaluated RL-trained compositions on PersonaMem-v2. Component ablations reveal that improvements in individual policies depend on their composition, highlighting the importance of cross-specialist compatibility. Further task-specific adaptation improves accuracy to 75.2% on LongMemEval through RL and 48.9% on PersonaMem-v2 through supervised distillation. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of independent specialist distillation for modular multi-agent systems. Source code and datasets of teacher-generated memory-editing and retrieval trajectories are released to facilitate reproducibility and further research.
title: Composing Independently Distilled Memory and Retrieval Policies for Long-Term Agents

summary: World models support planning by predicting how the environment evolves under candidate actions. However, one-step predictive accuracy alone does not characterize multi-step planning utility, which depends on distinguishing candidate futures. This raises a natural question: How does latent transition geometry shape planning? We investigate this through an action-conditioned transition-field view, using curvature regularization as a controlled intervention. Across four continuous-control tasks, appropriately tuned regularization improves planning, while excessive regularization can be detrimental. By decomposing the transition field into affine and non-affine components, we find that regularization reduces action sensitivity mainly through the non-affine component. To assess its role in planning, we directly manipulate the non-affine action response in frozen models and show that it affects candidate selection and closed-loop success. Further analysis shows that curvature generally brings predicted futures closer together, while preserving more of the differences along the goal direction. This helps explain why the planning effects vary across tasks. We observe broadly consistent planning trends across five sampling- and gradient-based solvers on LeWM and similar rollout-geometry trends on DINO-WM. Qualitative attention visualizations reveal accompanying shifts toward task-relevant visual structure. Together, these findings clarify how latent transition geometry influences multi-step planning.
title: How Latent Transition Geometry Matters for Planning in World Models

summary: Robot agents built on frontier vision-language models now solve most robot memory benchmarks. Does this mean they can remember what they need in a home, where people and machines keep moving things? Existing memory benchmarks cannot answer this question, because they pause the simulator while the model thinks: nothing can change during a decision, so whatever the robot remembers is still true when it acts. We introduce RoboLiveMem, a benchmark that runs the same memory tasks twice, once with the world paused while the model thinks and once with the world running. It contains 29 task families in three tiers, from 16 realistic BEHAVIOR-1K scenes of homes, workshops and a restaurant to controlled ManiSkill tasks. Every task mixes real changes with harmless look-alikes and runs without any change, so that no fixed strategy succeeds, and most tasks have a twin that keeps the change in view, which separates forgetting from acting too late. Testing 16 models on 34,176 episodes, we find three surprises. (1) Paused results hide the problem: when a remembered object changes in a realistic scene, the 8 Claude and GPT models succeed in 97% of episodes on average with the world paused, but in only 50% with the world running, and their ranking changes: Claude Opus 5.5, which never fails when paused, succeeds in 44%. (2) Speed is not the fix: slower models do no worse, and models given only 2 s per decision still fall at least 36 points below their paused success. (3) Models see the change but act on camera frames from before it ended. Looking again just before acting closes most of the realistic gap, yet when identical objects are swapped several times, all nine models we test still lose points to memory.

summary: Conventional artificial neurons separate spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time, limiting their ability to model irregular observations. We introduce the Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neuron (DAWIN), a continuous-time primitive for replacing standard neural layers in MLPs, Transformers, and graph neural networks. DAWIN couples spatial projection with elapsed-time-dependent wave excitation and integrates it into a local complex state through closed-form damped evolution, avoiding numerical differential equation solvers. We show that DAWIN generalizes static sinusoidal and memoryless wave neurons on interval-augmented inputs, derive closed-form gradients, and establish bounded-input bounded-output stability for positive damping and sampling intervals bounded away from zero. An associative Triton prefix-scan implementation, DAWINLinear, uses FP32 accumulation and achieves O(log L) parallel depth for sequence length L. Across 11 parameter-matched tasks covering irregular oscillators, MuJoCo dynamics, pedestrian trajectories, and PhysioNet 2012 clinical sequences, DAWIN outperforms Neural CDE on 9 tasks and ReLU-MLP on 8. It achieves the lowest error on dense clinical dynamics (0.9531 NRMSE, winning across all 10 seeds) and ties for the best mortality prediction (0.9993 AUROC). Shuffling elapsed intervals increases error by 58.2%-77.4% on selected dynamics tasks, versus 0.06% on a time-irrelevant control, supporting reliance on physical timing. On NVIDIA B200 GPUs, parallel wave integration accelerates inference by up to 2,630 times over its serial implementation and reduces peak GPU memory by up to 97.6% relative to Mamba in the tested configurations.
title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning

summary: Terraforming Mars is a long-horizon, action-conditioned control problem that requires predicting atmospheric responses to interventions over centuries to identify effective policies. This position paper argues that physics-regularized recurrent state-space world models are the most promising foundation for this setting. Data-driven climate emulators lack action-conditioning, and physics-based general circulation models (GCMs) are too expensive for policy search. Among learned world models, recurrent state-space architectures with physics constraints are better suited than transformer-based alternatives: they provide native uncertainty quantification through their stochastic-deterministic decomposition, remain stable under sparse non-terrestrial training data, and enforce physical consistency at each rollout step. To make this position concrete, we describe a potential architecture combining JEPA-inspired latent encoding, universal differential equation constraints, and a Dreamer-lineage planning head. We also introduce MarsWorld, an open benchmark proposal for intervention-conditioned planetary world models, and discuss broader implications and objections.
title: World Models Are the Right Foundation for Simulating Mars Terraforming

summary: We study how observed many-body system size affects the number of state copies needed to estimate a zero-temperature first-order transition point. The unknown Hamiltonian has bounded, translation-invariant on-site and nearest-neighbour interactions on a 3D cubic lattice with local dimension three. The field coupling is known, and all models share a known boundary field penalizing one local level. The limiting order parameter is uniformly separated across the transition. Each query returns an independently prepared Gibbs or ground state at an adaptive field and system size. For error $ε$ and fixed confidence, we prove an exponential separation between two size caps at the same temperature. There are absolute constants $0<c_0<C$ and $c_1>0$ such that, at inverse temperature $β=c_1/ε$, restricting side lengths to $L\le c_0/ε$ requires $\exp(Ω(1/ε))$ copies in worst-case expectation, even with collective measurements. Allowing $L\le C/ε$ permits $O(\log^2(1/ε))$ copies and $O(ε^{-3})$ total spins, using local measurements and polynomial classical postprocessing. The minimax expected total spin count is $Θ(ε^{-3})$ uniformly for $β\ge c_1/ε$. At fixed positive temperature it is $Θ_β(ε^{-2})$, attained from one- and eight-site Gibbs states followed by exponential classical computation. For ground-state copies it is $Θ(ε^{-3})$. The lower bound uses a three-state ferromagnet whose boundary suppresses the sector carrying transition information. A spanning-forest argument and edge-boundary counting control its Gibbs weight uniformly over fields and allowed sizes, and a trace-distance hybrid argument handles adaptive learners with quantum memory. The upper bound combines finite-volume free-energy estimates, concavity and local order-parameter measurements.

summary: We introduce MotionPort, which learns low-dimensional latent representations of body motion for accurate dynamics prediction and effective long-horizon planning. Existing world-model planners often search over action representations learned for prediction, yet we show that predictive accuracy alone does not ensure that optimization can discover successful trajectories. MotionPort addresses this mismatch by representing body trajectories rather than action chunks and organizing the search space by motion similarity, helping predicted improvements translate into successful execution. Without fine-tuning state encoders, MotionPort raises average goal-reaching success from 37.9% to 87.8% across three backbones and seven settings in four domains. On the evaluated AntMaze-OGBench tasks, it achieves 72% success, compared with 4% for the strongest baseline.

summary: Latent world models enable planning from images, but their predictions do not directly establish whether a robot will satisfy physical constraints. We present JEPA-Shield, which connects a frozen action-conditioned Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) world model to task-space safety enforcement. Two downstream models predict relative motion from imagined latent rollouts and decode unsafe geometry from the current image. Split conformal prediction turns end-to-end motion-prediction errors into multi-horizon uncertainty tubes. A backup-based shield checks these tubes against physical constraints and screens both candidate trajectories and final proposals in diffusion-inspired sampling-based model predictive control. Under the stated exchangeability and initial-backup assumptions, we establish probabilistic constraint satisfaction at action-block boundaries for a returned plan executed without replanning. We also introduce VParkBench, with geometric car and tractor-trailer parking tasks and a editable photorealistic Gaussian-splatting environment. In closed-loop evaluation, JEPA-Shield achieves success rates of 84.4%, 82.3%, and 99.0%, respectively, with no observed constraint violations. Ablations show complementary benefits from shielding and uncertainty calibration. The results demonstrate the importance of grounding latent world-model predictions in task-space quantities and explicitly accounting for prediction uncertainty in safety-critical planning.
title: JEPA-Shield: Safe Diffusion Planning with Latent World Models via Conformal Shielding

The purpose is not to announce that a new acupuncture mechanism has been confirmed. It is to design a research archive in which every ambitious model comes with a stronger rival, a declared uncertainty and a route to refusal. A well-matched classical baseline may defeat a quantum-labelled architecture. A thermal or electrode artifact may account for a proposed biofield. Two cultural readers may agree about an ancient text yet disagree about the physical proxy that should test its modern interpretation. A capable control system must still stop when a human revokes permission. Finally, a striking result should remain provisional until a different laboratory can reconstruct its adverse cases and explain why the result might be false. The family is situated in Eastern philosophical traditions as intellectual history and an ethics of balance and responsibility, while empirical claims are restricted to independently observable measurements. All diagrams, surfaces and numerical grids in this volume are synthetic and prospective. There is no clinical intervention, biological proof, medical-device validation, confirmed remote effect or established new field.
