summary: This artifact accompanies the poster paper "Evaluating Multi-Agent Incident Response: Baseline Design, Efficiency, and Policy Compliance" by Ebelechukwu Nwafor and Habeeb Olufowobi, accepted at the ACM/SIGAPP Symposium on Applied Computing (SAC '27). The paper asks whether a multi-agent LLM workflow for incident response is more efficient than a single agent, and shows that the answer depends on how the single-agent baseline is built. It evaluates MAN-IDS, a four-role LLM workflow, against single-agent baselines and a deterministic rule in three controlled studies on a Docker test network with Redis and PostgreSQL access scenarios. Contents - The MAN-IDS system and the evaluation harness (runners, scoring, decision protocol). - All prompts, model versions, and settings used in the studies. - The protocol for each study, written before any model calls were made. - Complete run records with full traces for 1,152 scheduled investigations across 64 campaigns:   - Study 1: explicit response policy, Claude Sonnet 5, 384 runs.   - Study 2: detector gating and routing repair, Claude Sonnet 5, 512 runs.   - Study 3: replication with Qwen3-8B on fresh campaigns, 256 runs. - Analysis scripts and their saved outputs, including the stage-timing, format-versus-decision, and comparable-quality re-analyses reported in the paper. - The trace analysis that motivated the routing repair, with the run records of the earlier evaluation it reads. - Detector experiment outputs (splits, predictions, reports) derived from CICIDS2017 and CSE-CIC-IDS2018. - The test-network setup (Docker Compose files, topology, schemas). Reproducing the results No model calls or API keys are needed. Running "python3 reproduce_analyses.py" re-runs the three study analyses from the saved run records and reports whether each result matches the shipped file byte for byte. The README lists the required Python packages and the remaining commands. Notes - Response actions were never executed. All tools are controlled and non-executing. - The public datasets are not redistributed. Only derived splits, predictions, and reports are included. - Run traces contain the absolute file paths of the machines that produced them. - Re-running the model studies would require an Anthropic API key (Studies 1 and 2) or a GPU serving Qwen3-8B (Study 3), plus Docker. License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
title: Artifact for "Evaluating Multi-Agent Incident Response: Baseline Design, Efficiency, and Policy Compliance" (ACM SAC 2027)

summary: This record contains the code, the processed input data and the results of every run of a benchmark study on the day-ahead and rolling-horizon scheduling of building energy systems with photovoltaics (PV), photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) collectors, a battery, a heat pump and a thermal storage tank.   The study compares three quantum-inspired metaheuristics (quantum-inspired evolutionary algorithm, quantum-behaved particle swarm optimisation, simulated quantum annealing) with their classical counterparts (genetic algorithm, particle swarm optimisation, simulated annealing), with general-purpose optimisers (differential evolution, L-SHADE, sep-CMA-ES, jSO, Gaussian QPSO, real-coded QEA, coordinate pattern search) and with mixed-integer linear programming (an exact MILP for the linear instances, a naive linearisation, a piecewise-linear MILP and its three-band and scenario-based forms). All optimisers receive the same number of objective-function evaluations and are tuned with one protocol.   Experiments - 21 synthetic day-ahead instances with 24 to 864 decision variables, 30 runs per algorithm and instance, evaluation budgets of 5,000, 20,000 and 100,000 - 1,311 data-driven day-ahead instances in three climates (typical-meteorological-year weather, measured electrical loads) - component ablations, budgets proportional to the number of variables, settings tuned at 864 variables - warm starts from the schedule of the piecewise-linear MILP - one year of rolling-horizon operation with 19 controllers, with and without a weekly demand charge, and three shorter variants (perfect forecasts, a second forecast-error model, random initialisation at every step)   Contents (143 files, 44 MB compressed) - qio_ies/: simulator of the energy system (numba), optimisers, MILP models, rolling-horizon operation - scripts/: one script per experiment, the statistical analysis, and the scripts that write the tables and figures - data/: processed measured load series - results/: output of every run (CSV, NPZ, JSON), reference costs and analysis tables - README.md: layout, commands and requirements   Reproduction The analysis tables and the tables and figures of the accompanying article can be regenerated from the stored run results with the analysis, table and figure scripts listed in README.md. The experiments themselves can be repeated with the run scripts. Metaheuristic runs are deterministic for a given seed. Extract the archive with the file times preserved.   Requirements Python 3.11 with numpy, scipy (HiGHS), numba, pandas, joblib, matplotlib and pvlib. The results were produced with Python 3.11.9, numpy 2.4.6, scipy 1.17.1, numba 0.66.0, pandas 3.0.3, matplotlib 3.11.0, joblib 1.5.3 and pvlib 0.15.2.   Data sources The weather records are the typical-meteorological-year files distributed with pvlib. The measured loads are derived from the UCI data set ElectricityLoadDiagrams20112014 (https://doi.org/10.24432/C58C86).
title: Benchmark of quantum-inspired and classical metaheuristics and piecewise-linear MILP for PV–battery–heat-pump–thermal-storage scheduling: code, data and results

summary: Language models fuse reports in retrieval, multi-agent consensus and agent memory, where treating shared-source reports as independent can double count evidence. A common remedy is an instruction to count each source once. Its value depends on the receiver's raw baseline. Pricing it needs an exact reference. We build the graded-dependence exact reference: binary worlds with single-report reliability 0.65 and four dependence levels, whose disclosed parameters give every world an exact posterior and every rule a target risk. The paired gain protocol scores raw and instructed answers of four configurations on 2,976 worlds. Agreement and gain separate in both directions. At $δ$ = 0, claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6.1-sol agreed with the rule within 0.001 in 744 of 744, and the instruction raised their posterior mismatch by 0.044; gpt-6-luna agreed in 165 of 744 and gained 0.0140 (95% interval 0.0064 to 0.0219); claude-haiku-5-5's gain moved from -0.0295 ($δ$ = 0) to +0.0302 ($δ$ = 1) (descriptive). The prespecified first-child endpoint contrast, gain at $δ$ = 1 minus $δ$ = 0, was 0.0342 (0.0303 to 0.0382). In the preregistered tests, the raw source-weight contrast was positive (0.259, 95% interval 0.182 to 0.337; Holm rejected zero) and the grouping endpoint difference was not detected (0.0004, -0.0023 to 0.0031). This interval excludes differences larger than 0.0031 in magnitude and lies within the registered precision bound of $\pm$0.0046. The reference prices the rule before any model call. The paired gain, estimable as a Brier difference on labelled deployment items, decides adoption per receiver and prompt condition.
title: Double counting in LLM evidence fusion: exact posteriors separate rule compliance from posterior gain

summary: Unplanned 30-day intensive care unit (ICU) readmission is a critical benchmark for evaluating healthcare quality. Most predictive models assume readmission risk depends solely on a patient's individual pathophysiological state, ignoring hospital operational context and resource capacity. In practice, discharge decisions are dynamic trade-offs between patient stability and bed turnover pressures. To address this gap, we develop an Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) for ICU discharge risk assessment. The system combines multi-agent collaborative extraction with self-evolving retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to eliminate template noise from progress notes, while constructing departmental workload indicators alongside admission flow features, continuous vital signs, and sparse medical codes (ICD/DRG). Addressing severe class imbalance (about 10.5% readmissions) and alarm fatigue, we implement data normalization, class reweighting, and decision-threshold calibration. In 20 independent runs across 20,000 ICU stays from MIMIC-III, empirical findings demonstrate that: vital signs alone have limited predictive capacity under real-world class imbalance (PR-AUC of 0.1387 +/- 0.0086); directly concatenating raw text embeddings degrades decision tree performance (XGBoost and LightGBM PR-AUC drop to 0.3893 and 0.4030); whereas an end-to-end multimodal fine-tuning architecture (Transformer E2E FineTune) utilizing layer-wise parameter freezing and differential learning rates reverses text negative transfer, achieving the highest AUROC of 0.8288 +/- 0.0110, PR-AUC of 0.4373 +/- 0.0310, and F1-Score of 0.4757 +/- 0.0196. Operational indicators supply independent risk signals, laying an engineering foundation for high-utility clinical decision support tools.
title: Operation-aware Multimodal Clinical Decision Support System for ICU Discharge Risk Assessment

summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a standard approach to enhance the reliability of large language model (LLM) outputs by retrieving documents relevant to a query and supplying them in the LLM prompt. Today's RAG systems collect, index, and serve these documents from centralized stores. In practice, however, documents are owned by organizations, devices, and individuals who cannot or will not surrender custody of them to a central party, e.g., because of privacy, copyright or regulatory compliance. Existing modern decentralized retrieval techniques either reintroduce a coordinating authority, or rely on a global data structure that requires continuous network-wide coordination (e.g., DHTs). We present ZeroRAG, a decentralized routing layer for document retrieval in RAG that performs semantic query routing across an overlay of peers with- out global data structures or centralized orchestration. Documents remain with the peers that own them, and each peer keeps only lightweight local state: a bounded set of neighbor advertisements and a cache of recently routed queries. Using these, ZeroRAG steers each query through a best-first walk that progressively rewires the overlay toward semantically relevant neighbors, so recall improves over time as the network self-organizes. We evaluate ZeroRAG using three real-world workloads and two decentralized baselines. We find that ZeroRAG outperforms baselines in terms of recall and required network messages, approaches the recall and LLM answer accuracy of a centralized document store, self-heals after catastrophic peer failures, and scales to 100 000 peers.
title: ZeroRAG: Adaptive Semantic Peer Routing for Decentralized Retrieval-Augmented Generation

summary: Deep parallel cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (CMARL)} trains multiple agents that all act at every time step to optimize a common objective. Like single-agent RL, CMARL can produce unsafe behaviors that violate implicit safety requirements not captured by the reward, and these behaviors are hard to explain. However, testing CMARL policies for safety has received less attention than the safety testing of single-agent RL policies. In this paper, we propose DisQ, a test case selection method that identifies failure-revealing states in value-based CMARL by exploiting a signal specific to trained Q-learning agents. The signal is the Q-value gap, an explainable metric that flags a state when the agents' estimates of the achievable return diverge by more than a calibrated threshold. DisQ selects such states for execution and skips those without a gap. Our experiments in four CMARL benchmark environments show that, in most of the evaluated configurations, DisQ improves failure detection over single-agent RL testing methods applied to CMARL, namely random testing and search-based testing with genetic algorithms. Our main contributions are the Q-value gap, an indicator of potential miscoordination computable from a single state without executing the system, and DisQ, a test case selection method that adapts existing single-agent testing methods to CMARL.
title: Testing for Coordination Failures in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

summary: High expertise and cost barriers exclude small and medium-sized enterprises from discrete-event simulation (DES). We introduce GenAI4SimPy, a multi-agent framework powered by Qwen 3.6 (27B), an open-weight large language model, that automates end-to-end DES generation from manufacturing event logs to executable SimPy models through tool-augmented reasoning and human-in-the-loop validation. Evaluated on three execution blocks from a public smart factory dataset, the framework achieved a mean absolute percentage error of 7.9\% and coverage of failure rate for all three blocks and of throughput for two of three. A fidelity paradox was observed: accurate process-level parameters did not ensure system-level behavioral fidelity, with flow-time and throughput errors driven by misinterpreted observation-window truncation and absent system-level calibration. These results demonstrate that local open-weight models can perform DES generation at accuracy comparable to cloud-based alternatives, while identifying parameter extraction as necessary but insufficient for behavioral validity. Source code and results are available at https://github.com/RaikoPipe/genai4simpy
title: From Manufacturing Event Logs to Simulation: Enabling SMEs with Agentic AI for SimPy Simulation Generation

summary: Upper-mid-band spectrum offers bandwidth opportunities for the integrated networks of ground vehicles, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), and low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to support 6G wide-area vehicle-to-everything (V2X) connectivity. However, V2X services' latency and reliability are sensitive to the mid-band selection due to frequency-dependent propagation and rain attenuation. This paper investigates environment-aware spectrum agility over candidate frequency range 3 (FR3) bands within 7.125-24.25 GHz, jointly with end-to-end (E2E) multi-path traffic splitting and transmit power control. Each data packet is partitioned into non-overlapping subflows over direct and UAV-assisted paths, with failed sky-link subflows selectively retransmitted subject to retransmission and freshness constraints. We formulate latency- and reliability-oriented problems, followed by a unified sequential optimization problem incorporating band-switching costs and average quality-of-service (QoS) violation budgets. To coordinate optimization decisions across heterogeneous timescales, we develop an agentic AI-assisted hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning (AA-HMARL) framework. A high-level agentic supervisor integrates recurrent memory, analytical evaluation of candidate bands, and event-triggered replanning to coordinate slow environmental adaptation with fast channel and retransmission dynamics, while distributed ground vehicles and UAV agents optimize data splitting and power using constrained MAPPO. Simulation results demonstrate an adjustable reliability-latency trade-off. Particularly, AA-HMARL reduces the mean E2E completion latency and the mean number of retransmission rounds among successfully delivered updates by 17.8-25.5% and 57.6-61.5%, respectively, and reduces the mean age of information (AoI) by 12.7-14.6% relative to fixed-band MAPPO across two traffic types.
title: Hierarchical Agentic Mid-Band Agility for Reliable Low-Latency Space-Air-Ground Integrated V2X Networks

summary: Every move in a robot team changes the world in which its teammates must act. Coordinated manipulation therefore calls for predicting the team's actions together with the physical future they jointly create. We introduce MAWAM, a multi-agent world-action model that jointly generates each robot's future views and executable action chunks in a single sample. Built from a pretrained single-robot world-action backbone, MAWAM jointly denoises all robots' action and future-view tokens through cross-agent attention, while preserving a separate control interface for each robot. MAWAM achieves the highest success on all three real-robot tasks (laundry-bag collection, bath-towel folding, and umbrella handover), with 67.8% mean success, 18.9 percentage points above MA-VLA trained on the same demonstrations and cameras. In simulation, MAWAM reaches 90.3% mean success on eight tasks with teams of up to four arms. Ablations show that cross-agent attention and team-stage future-video supervision both improve coordinated control: without attention, a four-arm relay falls from 95.0% to 39.0%, and without this supervision, Place Food falls from 78.0% to 47.0%.
title: MAWAM: A Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Coordinated Manipulation

summary: Abstract (it) Il corpus in esame decostruisce il mito dell’applicazione standardizzata della prospettiva albertiana basata su una griglia di quadrati nell’opera di Leonardo da Vinci, proponendo un paradigma metrico-modulare fondato su evidenze geometriche oggettive e falsificabili. Attraverso l’analisi tridimensionale dell’Annunciazione, dell’Adorazione dei Magi e dell’Ultima Cena, emerge una grammatica spaziale in costante evoluzione. Leonardo abbandona la rigida scacchiera per sviluppare un sistema di “righelli inseriti”, evolvendo da una misurazione monodirezionale a un’architettura ritmica e stereometrica. Il metodo d’indagine, basato su tecniche di retroingegneria CAD e sul “banale aristotelico”, dimostra come le proporzioni spaziali (dalla proporzione 3:1:3, passando per il modulo 4:3, il rapporto 1:4 e gli angoli a 36° fino ad arrivare ai ritmi polifonici 1:4:1, 2:1:2 e 1:6:1) siano direttamente ricavabili dall’opera stessa. Riferimento teorico primario del corpus è il Manoscritto A di Leonardo (f. 41r), secondo cui la profondità dello spazio dipinto si costruisce da riduzioni misurabili, prima ancora che da una griglia di quadrati. L’approccio restituisce spazi non solo misurabili, ma architettonicamente rimontabili e strutturati sulle misure umane, rigettando interpretazioni esoteriche o simbologie forzate. Abstract (en) The examined corpus deconstructs the myth of the standardized application of Albertian perspective based on a grid of squares in the works of Leonardo da Vinci, proposing a metric-modular paradigm founded on objective and falsifiable geometric evidence. Through the three-dimensional analysis of the Annunciation, the Adoration of the Magi, and the Last Supper, a constantly evolving spatial grammar emerges. Leonardo abandons the rigid checkerboard to develop a system of “inserted rulers,” evolving from a monodirectional measurement to a rhythmic and stereometric architecture. The investigative method, based on CAD reverse-engineering techniques and the “Aristotelian obvious,” demonstrates how spatial proportions (from the 3:1:3 proportion, passing through the 4:3 module, the 1:4 ratio and the 36° angles, up to the 1:4:1, 2:1:2 and 1:6:1 polyphonic rhythms) can be directly derived from the artwork itself. The primary theoretical reference of the corpus is Leonardo’s Manuscript A (f. 41r), according to which the depth of painted space is constructed from measurable reductions, even before a grid of squares. This approach yields spaces that are not only measurable but architecturally reassemblable and structured on human measurements, rejecting esoteric interpretations or forced symbolism. Abstract esteso (IT) Il corpus Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score propone una rilettura unitaria di tre indagini nate separatamente ma convergenti verso una stessa ipotesi: Leonardo da Vinci non applica in modo meccanico la prospettiva albertiana a maglia quadrata, né se ne discosta episodicamente per errore o licenza, ma sviluppa progressivamente una propria grammatica spaziale metrico-modulare, verificabile a partire dall'immagine stessa. L'oggetto della ricerca non è una lettura iconografica complessiva delle opere, bensì la ricostruzione degli spazi dipinti come dispositivi misurabili, abitabili e rimontabili attraverso procedure geometriche esplicite. Il trittico mette in relazione tre momenti distinti di questa elaborazione: l’ Annunciazione come forma prototipica della “geometria inserita”, l’ Adorazione dei Magi come emersione di una griglia generativa 4:3 connessa al braccio fiorentino, e l’ Ultima Cena come approdo a una vera polifonia stereometrica, governata da un unico modulo capace di coordinare larghezza, altezza e profondità. In questa prospettiva, lo sviluppo dell’opera leonardesca appare co
title: Leonardo's Spatial Grammar: A CAD Reverse-Engineering Analysis Corpus: Leonardo's CAD, Leonardo's Rulers, Leonardo's Score

summary: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^α\cap L_t^2H_x^{α+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leqα<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The proof relies on a computer-assisted construction of a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, starting from the numerical profiles identified in our preceding paper (arXiv:2606.07501). We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.
title: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II

summary: For an absorbed one-dimensional diffusion, we characterize two-point restart laws preserving the exit-side probability for every independent renewal clock. Spectral identities establish rigidity under spatial accumulation, while explicit nonsymmetric potentials admit neutral pairs. We distinguish midpoint Dirichlet isospectrality from Weyl reflection rigidity and prove a second-order high-energy asymptotic under local continuity, giving two necessary asymmetry conditions for neutral pairs. Two complete exit profiles at distinct reset rates identify diffusivity and drift; a finite birth-death analogue admits exact Jacobi criteria and reconstruction from four channel functions.
title: Exit-Pair Rigidity, Neutral Restart Laws, and Inverse Reconstruction in One Dimension

summary: We develop a method for forming Ramsey fringes in atomic interferometers as a difference error signal using the phase-jump technique for Ramsey pulses (phase-jump error signal). In this case, the measurement procedure can be implemented as stabilization (locking) of the frequency chirp rate at the central zero of the error signal. We show analytically that this approach allows suppressing the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift (LACS). This shift was recently theoretically predicted and experimentally identified in the papers [V. I. Yudin et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{122}, 737 (2025); D. N. Kapusta et al., JETP Lett. \textbf{123}, 388 (2026)]. A characteristic feature of the LACS is an inverse cubic dependence $\propto 1/T^3$ (where $T$ is the time between adjacent Ramsey pulses), and it can become dominant for interferometers with a short baseline. Therefore, the developed measurement algorithm with a phase-jump error signal will enable significant improvement in the metrological performance of compact quantum sensors for various purposes (atomic gravimeters, accelerometers, gyroscopes).
title: Atomic interferometry based on a phase-jump error signal with suppression of the lineshape-asymmetry-caused shift

summary: Existing no-reference point cloud quality assessment (NR-PCQA) methods perform well within individual datasets but generalize poorly across datasets. We identify insufficient distortion coverage in training data as a key cause: on unseen distortion types, models rank severity levels near chance or even in reverse. We propose perceptually gated synthetic supervision for no-reference point cloud quality assessment (PGS-PCQA), an NR-PCQA model trained with synthetic distortion ranking. It builds a synthetic distortion bank from source reference point clouds and uses within-type severity ranking as supervision in addition to the source mean opinion scores (MOS), requiring no subjective scores for the synthetic samples. Since higher severity does not always mean lower perceived quality, a perceptual gate softens the ranking targets of pairs with small perceptual differences in rendered views. The synthetic supervision is used only during training and needs no target-domain data. In a single training run on SJTU-PCQA, PGS-PCQA achieves Spearman rank correlation coefficients (SRCCs) of 0.709 on WPC and 0.751 on BASICS. The corresponding published DSP-PCQA scores are 0.595 and 0.723. Under reference-disjoint cross-validation, PGS-PCQA achieves SRCCs of 0.955 on SJTU-PCQA, 0.934 on WPC, 0.906 on BASICS, and 0.791 on LS-PCQA Part I. In the exclusion experiment, the reported scores for the reduced synthetic bank represent 58-65% of the full-bank SRCC gain relative to training without the bank. Code is available at https://github.com/Fan-QY/PGS-PCQA.
title: PGS-PCQA: Perceptually Gated Synthetic Supervision for No-Reference Point Cloud Quality Assessment

summary: An AI-assisted payment can pass assessment and lose release authority before commitment. We specify a banking delegation contract that checks current authority, the shared payment cap and the capacity of eligible instruments to cover losses. It books the new payment and its recovery demands and writes the outcome record in the same atomic transition. A paired example identifies the authorised mandate, applied rule and selection inputs a reviewer needs to assess mandate conformance. We show that, under fixed resource inputs, the transition preserves the payment cap and recovery feasibility when commitments and effective withdrawals are ordered against the same authoritative state. Reversing a transmitted priority changes the selected route in 4 of 32 distinct behavioural combinations, represented by 96 of 576 labelled contexts. The executor follows the transmitted rule in all of them. Reusing earlier state admits 23 releases in 123 histories blocked by the reference. Pooling recovery capacity admits 69 infeasible configurations in a grid of 576. Both current-state implementations agree with the reference in all 144 commitment histories and 624 concurrent schedules. The retention test recovers five specified outcome fields from each of 47 complete records. Fifteen survey responses informed requirements for resolving holds and handling uncertain delivery. An insurance example illustrates referral after an adverse coverage finding.
title: Accountable AI Delegation in Banking: Identity, Commitment Controls, Decision Evidence and Recovery

summary: The excited-state properties of imide-based defect double antiperovskites AE$_5$AsPn(NH)$_2$ (AE = Ca, Sr; Pn = Sb, Bi) are investigated using spin--orbit-coupled quasiparticle calculations, the model Bethe--Salpeter equation (mBSE), and analytical descriptions of lattice-polarization effects. Across five tetragonal ($P4/mmm$) and monoclinic ($Cm$) structural models, the calculated exciton binding energies range from 140 to 210 meV. Chemical substitution modifies both the binding energies and the hydrogenic estimates of exciton spatial extent. By contrast, the structural distortion from tetragonal $P4/mmm$ ($D_{4h}$) to monoclinic $Cm$ ($C_s$), which removes inversion and fourfold rotational symmetry, produces comparatively modest changes in binding energy but appreciably reshapes the real- and momentum-space exciton distributions. This contrast reveals a partial decoupling between exciton energetics and wavefunction geometry, and identifies a symmetry-associated sensitivity of exciton geometry to structural distortion. The changes are understood to occur together with modifications of local coordination and electronic dispersion, rather than as an isolated effect of symmetry alone. Lattice polarization provides an additional screening channel, reducing the estimated exciton binding energies by approximately 9--16\%. Complementary Fröhlich-polaron calculations yield moderate mass enhancement and model-estimated electron-polaron mobilities of 39--99 cm$^2$ V$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$, with comparatively modest differences between the two polymorphs. These results highlight the distinct responses of exciton energetics, exciton wavefunction geometry, and carrier transport to chemical and structural modifications.
title: Decoupling Exciton Energetics from Wavefunction Geometry in Imide-Based Defect Double Antiperovskites

summary: Constructing an effective low-dimensional stochastic model from sparse observations requires separating deterministic drift from state-dependent fluctuations when the governing interaction law is unknown. We formulate an adaptive neural stochastic differential equation with topology constraints (TC-AdaNSDE) for two-variable predator--prey dynamics. To regularize the inverse problem when data are scarce, the model combines flexible drift and correlated diffusion fields with density-adaptive local Kramers--Moyal moment estimates and soft phase-space constraints reflecting boundary saddle behavior near extinction and local stability near coexistence. Using a known nonlinear stochastic system, we first show that short-time trajectory error cannot assess diffusion accuracy on its own and must be paired with distributional measures of one-step transitions and long-time phase-space occupancy. We then apply this framework to macroscopic turbulence and zonal flow energies reduced from Hasegawa--Wakatani plasma simulations and to short ecological time series. In the sparse-data regime, TC-AdaNSDE reproduces both short-horizon evolution and long-time invariant energy distributions where deterministic reductions collapse and unconstrained stochastic fits diverge, while recovering physically interpretable drift and fluctuation fields across both physical and biological systems.
title: Learning effective stochastic predator and prey dynamics across physical and biological systems from limited data

summary: Recent studies have identified orbital exchange fields as a novel mechanism for controlling electronic and magnetic phenomena through the orbital degree of freedom. In contrast to conventional spin exchange fields, orbital exchange fields couple directly to orbital angular momentum and can emerge from purely orbital interactions or dynamically through couplings to chiral excitations such as phonons and magnons. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the transport and torque responses generated by orbital exchange fields in two-dimensional materials. Using monolayer H-phase MoS$_2$ as a prototypical transition-metal dichalcogenide, we introduce a Zeeman-like orbital exchange field that breaks time-reversal symmetry in orbital space while leaving the spin degree of freedom inactive. We demonstrate that this perturbation induces a sizable intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity even in the absence of spin magnetism and spin--orbit coupling driven mechanisms. Simultaneously, the orbital Hall response remains robust in the weak-field regime and undergoes substantial reconstruction at larger exchange strengths due to pronounced band modifications. In addition, we show that currents can generate sizable current-induced orbital torques on the orbital magnetization. Our results establish orbital exchange fields as an effective route toward Hall transport and nonequilibrium torque phenomena driven purely by orbital physics, opening new perspectives for orbitronics and orbitally engineered quantum functionalities.
title: Pure Orbitronics: Hall Responses and Torques by Orbital Exchange in Spinless Transition-Metal Dichalcogenides

summary: Frustrated magnets on triangular lattices favour noncollinear order, and when inversion symmetry is broken they can host localized topological textures on top of that order. Here we show that the Janus MXene MnHf2C2FI is such a system. Combining first-principles calculations with atomistic spin simulations, we find that magnetism is confined to the Mn layer, where a strong antiferromagnetic nearest-neighbor exchange together with a sizable Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction stabilizes a frustrated 120 Neel ground state. On top of this ground state we identify a metastable hexameron: a composite of six merons and antimerons, one vortex-antivortex pair on each of the three sublattices, whose sublattice-resolved topological charges compensate. Linear spin-wave theory confirms that the hexameron is a local energy minimum, and its noncoplanar cores act as potential wells that bind discrete in-gap magnon modes below the bulk continuum. In a periodic hexameron array the magnon bands carry nonzero Chern numbers, and the resulting Berry curvature produces a magnon thermal Hall response whose sign depends on which of the two time-reversal partners of the hexameron is realized. Our results establish Janus MXenes as a two-dimensional platform in which frustration, broken inversion symmetry, and spin-orbit coupling combine to produce metastable antiferromagnetic solitons with distinct spectroscopic and transport fingerprints.
title: Frustration-Stabilized Hexamerons and Their Topological Magnons in Janus MXene

summary: This record provides the Actual Vapor Pressure (AVP) component of the H igh-resolution ( d aily and 1 km) atmospheric M oisture I ndex C ollection over China (HiMIC-Daily) . AVP is essential for water vapor transport calculations and complements the other five moisture indicators in the collection. The dataset was generated using the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction, integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2-m temperature and dew point temperature (ERA5-Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM was selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree-based algorithms. For AVP, the reconstruction achieves an R ² of 0.989, MAE of 0.677 hPa, and RMSE of 0.933 hPa. The product has a spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, covering China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, one file per year, with daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, values are scaled by a factor of 100 and stored as 16-bit integer (int16); original values are restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System. Comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the "README.pdf". The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.
title: HiMIC-Daily AVP: Daily 1 km Actual Vapor Pressure over China, 2003–2025

summary: The Hi gh resolution ( d aily and 1km) atmospheric M oisture I ndex C ollection over the China  ( HiMIC- Daily ) provides a comprehensive dataset of six moisture indicators: Relative Humidity (RH, %), Dew Point Temperature (DPT, °C), Actual Vapor Pressure (AVP, hPa), Mixing Ratio (MR, g kg -1 ), Specific Humidity (SH, g kg -1 ), and Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD, hPa). These indicators are essential for characterizing atmospheric moisture conditions: RH has been widely used in human comfort assessment and weather forecasting; AVP is essential for water vapor transport calculations; VPD serves as a key indicator of moisture stress on vegetation and fire risk; DPT has been applied in frost prediction and evaporative cooler design; MR has been used for hydrograph separation and identification of groundwater recharge sources; and SH is crucial for total precipitable water and longwave radiation assessments. To generate this dataset, the study adopts the Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) algorithm for spatial reconstruction by integrating meteorological station observations with multiple high-resolution datasets, including land surface temperature (MOD11A1/MYD11A1), land cover (MCD12Q1), topographic variables (MERIT DEM), column water vapor (MCD19A2), vapor pressure (TerraClimate), 2‑m temperature and DPT (ERA5‑Land), and population density (WorldPop). LightGBM is selected for its higher efficiency and robustness compared to other tree‑based algorithms. The dataset demonstrates high accuracy with R ²/MAE/RMSE values of RH (0.877, 4.849 %, 6.520 %), AVP (0.989, 0.677 hPa, 0.933 hPa), VPD (0.906, 0.983 hPa, 1.411 hPa), DPT (0.985, 1.120 ℃, 1.608 ℃), MR (0.988, 0.459 g kg -1 , 0.633 g kg -1 ), and SH (0.988, 0.451 g kg -1 , 0.620 g kg -1 ). With a high spatial resolution of 1 km × 1 km and a daily temporal resolution, this dataset covers China from January 1, 2003, to December 31, 2025. HiMIC-Daily provides a reliable data foundation for research in meteorology, ecology, environmental science, and human health.  The dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, each containing daily data indexed by the time coordinate. To optimize storage and maintain precision, each index is scaled by a factor of 100 and converted to 16-bit integer (int16) format prior to archiving, with original values restored by dividing the stored data by 100. The dataset is referenced to the World Geodetic System (WGS) 1984 Coordinate System, and comprehensive information on file naming and other specifications is documented in the “README.pdf”. The HiMIC-Daily dataset is organized into annual NetCDF files, with one file per indicator per year. Currently, each moisture indicator is provided through its own dedicated download link: RH (2003–2020) AVP (2003–2020) VPD (2003–2020) DPT (2003–2020) MR (2003–2020) SH (2003–2020) Because the dataset is updated annually, one additional link will be added each year as a new annual file becomes available: 2021 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2022 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2023 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2024 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) 2025 (RH, AVP, VPD, DPT, MR, SH) More data will be added in the future.   If you use the HiMIC-Daily dataset for related scientific research, please cite the corresponding reference: Su, Z., Zhang, H., Wu, S., Zeng, Z., Zhang, T., and Luo, M.: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2020, Earth System Science Data . https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-2026-367, 2026.
title: HiMIC-Daily: A high-resolution (daily and 1 km) multi-indicator atmospheric moisture collection over China, 2003–2025

summary: This repository contains the curated research data, MATLAB, R and Python scripts, generalized additive model (GAM) outputs, figures, and reproducibility documentation associated with the manuscript “Spatially Heterogeneous Atmosphere–Ocean–Biogeochemical Variability Under Contrasting ENSO Conditions in the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico” , submitted to Continental Shelf Research (manuscript CSR-D-25-00158R3). The study investigates seasonal atmosphere–ocean–biogeochemical variability across the Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Mexico, and adjacent western tropical Atlantic during four selected years characterized by contrasting El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) conditions: 2013, 2022, 2023, and 2024. The analyses integrate NASA MERRA-2 atmospheric reanalysis, Copernicus Marine Service (CMEMS) satellite altimetry, MODIS-Aqua sea surface temperature (SST) and chlorophyll-a (Chl-a) observations, and complementary historical records. Regional SST variability is examined for 1982–2024 using a NOAA OISST-derived archive, while sea-level anomaly (SLA) variability is evaluated for 1993–2024. Spatial GAMs are used to investigate nonlinear SST–Chl-a associations while accounting for geographical structure. Nested spatial cross-validation, spatial-basis sensitivity, concurvity diagnostics, and residual spatial autocorrelation analyses are documented. Complementary oceanographic diagnostics quantify 120-day filtered surface-height gravitational-energy variability and surface geostrophic eddy kinetic energy. The repository provides the final main and supplementary figures, derived analytical datasets, archived GAM model objects, numerical verification outputs, and processing code. A SHA256 manifest supports file-integrity verification. Reproducibility scope: The repository supports verification and partial reproduction of the published analyses. Some workflows require separately obtained source datasets, external software dependencies, or environment-specific configuration. The Figure 6 graphical reconstruction has been verified using derived GAM outputs, while complete end-to-end execution of every archived script has not been independently established. Scientific limitations: The selected-year comparisons are descriptive and do not represent replicated ENSO-phase climatologies or establish causal ENSO attribution. The GAM-derived SST–Chl-a relationships are conditional on the fitted geographical structure and remain subject to spatial-basis adequacy and concurvity limitations. The filtered surface-height gravitational-energy proxy is distinct from three-dimensional baroclinic available potential energy. Original third-party source datasets are accessible through their respective providers and are not comprehensively redistributed in this deposit. Redistribution-restricted historical IHO geographical source files are excluded from the public package. Author: José de Jesús Salas Pérez Affiliation: Universidad Veracruzana, Mexico Associated manuscript: CSR-D-25-00158R3, Continental Shelf Research .
title: Spatially Heterogeneous Atmosphere–Ocean–Biogeochemical Variability Under Contrasting ENSO Conditions in the Caribbean Sea and Gulf of Mexico

summary: AquaTrajectories is an open-source R and Python research-software toolkit for aquatic animal 2D and 3D movement analysis, video-based fish-tracking interfaces, multiview reconstruction, camera geometry, behavioural methods, conditional uncertainty assessment and reproducible scientific visualization. Version 0.2.0 added evidence safeguards for estimator sensitivity, mixed coordinate units, independent-unit interpretation, spatial support, measurement-geometry associations and descriptive falsification checks. Version 0.2.1 includes 100-percent real executed-code coverage qualification and expanded boundary regressions. Its synthetic numerical oracles and cross-platform qualification do not certify biological identity, real-video tracking generalization, physical underwater XYZ metrology, causal feeding responses, fish welfare outcomes or hardware safety.
title: AquaTrajectories: Aquatic Animal Movement and Multiview Trajectories

summary: Hilberg's hypothesis states that block entropy of text grows as hn + An^beta. We connect maximal entropy random walk (Parry) sequence ensembles, ANS-like equipartition of surprisal, Santa Fe processes with an HCR-motivated Gaussian world model, and LLM-based entropy measurements into a picture of text as progressive revelation of a world state. Calibration on Santa Fe processes shows that PPMd compression slopes barely respond to the true Hilberg exponent, while a word-level Pitman-Yor coder recovers it but measures lexicon occupancy. A permutation-calibrated lexical index detects word-order effects in anthologies. For compression, a self-contained coder cannot remove a genuine An^beta source term; explicit word and recency models reduce predictive log loss by 1.5-3.4% over a context-mixing base, and shared dictionaries pay off mainly for small independently coded documents. Supplementary files contain all code and results.
tags: Hilberg's law; Zipf's law; Heaps' law; Santa Fe process; maximal entropy random walk; asymmetric numeral systems; hierarchical correlation reconstruction; text compression; neural scaling laws
title: Hilberg's law as learning a world state: implications and limits for text compression

summary: Reconstructing an editable music score requires musical events, sung text and the instructions that organise them on the page. Existing recognition targets often omit part of this information, while direct MusicXML prediction repeats substantial structural markup. We introduce Cecilia, a compact representation of canonicalised MusicXML that retains musical content, lyric attachments and layout instructions. Cecilia-OMR predicts this representation through metadata and measure-bounded music segments from shared visual memory. A learned count head determines the number of output segments. Across paired complete scores under a common tokeniser, the ratio of mean MusicXML to Cecilia sequence lengths is 27.73. Cecilia-OMR outperforms Legato 2 on Camera String Quartets and both Lieder conditions, with a four-condition OpenScore macro normalised edit distance of 0.2232 against 0.2998. Separate evaluations of lyrics, notation trees and rendered layout reveal complementary aspects of reconstruction and quantify the contribution of layout instructions. Training-stage, reward and candidate-selection studies further examine how recognition changes across model adaptation and decoding.
title: Cecilia: Towards Layout-Inclusive Optical Music Recognition

summary: Action-conditioned video world models imagine future observations under candidate robot actions, providing a promising visual tool for robot policy evaluation and interaction simulation. However, existing video world models often optimize global reconstruction errors instead of emphasizing interaction-relevant regions. As a result, they may preserve overall scene appearance but overlook local interaction details, leading to physically implausible outcomes such as hallucinated contact effects and inconsistent robot-object interactions. We introduce MoReWorld, a unified motion-region-guided framework that uses a shared motion region, the part of the environment that moves in response to the robot's actions, to focus dynamics learning and video generation on interaction-relevant regions. The same motion region guides local motion prediction, region-aware supervision, and motion-gated future-feature conditioning. At inference time, the motion region is predicted as a motion probability map from visual history and robot actions, without requiring future observations or ground-truth motion labels. On WorldSimProbe, MoReWorld achieves the highest overall simulator-faithfulness score, with the strongest performance on local consistency, global consistency, and interaction dynamics. These results indicate that motion-region guidance helps the model preserve scene-level consistency while more faithfully predicting action-conditioned interaction dynamics.
title: Learning Interaction Dynamics via Motion-Region Guidance for Robotic Video World Models

summary: Abstract This integrative research synthesis develops a candidate relational architecture across quantum foundations, physical history, persistent organization, relational time, and the recovery problem for spacetime. Its method is unification by decomposition : constraint, weighting, singular factualization, and retention are treated as distinct operations with distinct evidential burdens. Key Analyses & Framework Quantum Foundations & Entanglement: The double slit separates coherent alternatives, receiver-defined effects, Born weighting, and the $n = 1$ record. The Sorkin hierarchy and reconstruction literature delimit what is already formally known and leave open the physical motivation for second-order weighting. Entanglement is analyzed through a missing-loss audit: spatial routing, operational differentiation, and dynamical decoupling do not by themselves demonstrate ontological severance of a nonfactorizable joint state. Ontology & Event-Factualization: Primitive factualization is treated as a technical event-ontology posit, with fundamental agency as a stronger interpretive hypothesis (alongside objective stochasticity, Bohmian completion, Everettian branching, and collapse dynamics as comparison classes). A present-state coherence veto prevents absolute factualization while coherence-bearing degrees of freedom remain causally accessible to future interactions in which their phase relation can again matter. Retained factual consequences provide the bridge to physical history, memory, differential persistence, and increasingly organized agency. Downstream Physics & Empirical Testing: Transition and stabilization are treated as relational roles of one field-energy reality rather than new substances. The synthesis incorporates a fully exposed prospective transition-stabilization kill test in a driven liquid-to-vapor system and preserves planetary, gravitational, and spacetime extensions as explicitly conditional research branches. Methodological Stance: No universal master equation is claimed. The program is a structured ontology, audit, and research architecture whose modules must earn mathematical or empirical closure independently. Philosophical Extensions (Dual-Aspect Hypothesis): A further dual-aspect factualist hypothesis, with a panexperiential extension, distinguishes the publicly accessible objective face of factual processes from a minimally subjective first-person-like aspect associated with irreducible factual resolution. This is presented as a stronger ontological interpretation, not as an experimentally established consequence. It does not identify an elementary subjective aspect with a subject, mind, or consciousness. Complex biological agency is treated as potentially nested and hierarchically integrated, while the combination of elementary subjective loci into a unified subject is left as an explicit unresolved problem.
title: Unification by Decomposition: The Dualverse — From Quantum Factualization and Physical Memory to Hierarchical Individuality and Spacetime

summary: Offer-by-offer traces of 1,000 seeded scenarios in which one simulated consumer negotiates price, quantity and delivery time with three simulated manufacturing providers whose preferences, ranges, reservation values and concession behaviour vary. The dataset contains 1,000 sessions, 3,000 negotiations and 26,818 offers. All values are synthetic. The dataset contains no personal data and no data from real companies. The data were generated with a seeded Python script (master seed 2026) that replays the negotiation protocol of the first MaaSAI SPADE agent prototype without a real-time clock or XMPP. The code is included in reproducibility_code_v1.0.0.zip and regenerates the data files byte for byte. Known limitations: the dataset documents a baseline prototype, not the current MaaSAI negotiation strategy. The prototype does not stop a provider from freezing an offer outside its declared ranges: 493 of the 995 agreements are in this situation. They are kept and flagged with final_within_provider_limits = 0. MaaSAI DMP code: MaaSAI_06014_SyntheticNegotiationScenarios_T6.5. Funded by the European Commission under Grant Agreement No. 101177368.
title: MaaSAI synthetic negotiation traces: seeded parametric scenarios

summary: Accurate petroleum inventory reconciliation is a key requirement for the safe and efficient operation of storage terminals. Conventional reconciliation is often performed through periodic reports, manually consolidated measurements, or separate tank and flow-meter records. Such practices can delay the identification of discrepancies and make it difficult to distinguish actual inventory changes from measurement errors, time-alignment problems, and incomplete transfer records. This paper proposes a SCADA-based real-time monitoring architecture that integrates tank level, product temperature, density, flow-meter measurements, historical process data, and tank calibration tables to calculate inventory changes and identify abnormal reconciliation residuals. The proposed system includes data acquisition, signal validation, time synchronization, tank-volume reconstruction, flow accounting, balance calculation, alarm management, and operator visualization. A staged implementation and validation methodology is presented, with emphasis on traceability, measurement uncertainty, and human verification. The framework is a design proposal and has not yet been validated through reported field trials; therefore, no measured improvement in accuracy or loss reduction is claimed.
tags: SCADA; petroleum storage terminal; real-time monitoring; inventory reconciliation; tank gauging; flow measurement; mass balance; measurement uncertainty; alarm management.
title: DEVELOPMENT OF A SCADA-BASED REAL-TIME MONITORING SYSTEM FOR PETROLEUM INVENTORY RECONCILIATION

summary: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($α=0$) and 98.83% at $α=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $α=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $α=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM runs use the unfused path. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval hits 100.00% (128/128 queries at $L=65\mathrm{K}$) vs. 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention, and compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show modest causal and masked LM gains.
title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed

summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π(x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. summary: This article analyzes the philosophical implications of Alpöge's November 2026 Lean formalization of the Riemann hypothesis, a proof co-developed with AI assistance. While formal verification is established, conceptual understanding remains incomplete. The article introduces "hybrid conceptual authority" to describe how conceptual contribution and justificatory authority diverge in AI-assisted mathematics. Drawing on philosophy of chemistry's model of explanatory autonomy, it proposes a four-dimensional framework verification, reconstruction, attribution, and interpretation for evaluating epistemic practice in proof production.
title: Hybrid Conceptual Authority in AI-Assisted Mathematics

summary: Description This dataset documents the participation of female musicians in European concert life between 1750 and 1800. It records individual performers alongside detailed information on their appearances in public concerts, enabling the reconstruction of collaborative performance networks. By cross-referencing musicians and shared concert events, the dataset captures patterns of co-performance and professional interaction within Europe's musical scene.   Developed as part of a broader doctoral research project on women’s roles in eighteenth-century European music, the dataset integrates biographical data with performance records. The data is structured as an Excel database partitioned into functional sheets, including Nodes, Interactions, and Edges, which are optimized for direct import into Gephi network visualization software. Each node entry includes detailed attribute columns such as names, nationalities, roles, musical competencies (e.g., composer, singer, instrument, teacher), and documented travel corridors.   The database forms the direct foundation for network visualizations, in which musicians and associated entities are represented as nodes and their shared performances are represented as edges. These structured sheets allow for the direct analysis of the density, mobility, and structure of professional relationships, with data pre-formatted to easily reflect the frequency of collaboration.   Methodology The dataset was constructed through systematic analysis of primary sources and historical concert records, supplemented by secondary literature. Musicians were included based on the availability of sufficient biographical and performance data to support meaningful analysis. Relationships were established through documented co-appearances in concerts.   Limitations The dataset reflects the uneven survival of historical records and prioritizes musicians with sufficiently documented careers. As such, it does not represent a complete census of performers active in London during this period.   Data Integrity and Usage: This record contains original Excel databases developed as part of a doctoral dissertation. summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. This makes a benchmark result conditional on how the workflow is executed. We introduce MASSys, a benchmark for measuring this dependence in multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems. MASSys executes the same candidate-task pairs across serving substrates and load regimes, using five workload families spanning software repair, research synthesis, financial analysis, interactive control, and diagram generation. It records task quality alongside delivery, latency, cost, resource pressure, and failure evidence. In a controlled motivation diagnostic, the Star workflow falls from first to fourth in mean-latency rank under KV-cache pressure, while Chain rises from fourth to first. The substrate sweeps further show that increasing load creates long runtime tails and timeout pressure. In several task families, quality among evaluated outputs changes less than effective quality over submitted jobs: the system delivers fewer usable results even when the surviving outputs remain competitive. Tool and runtime traces reveal that these outcomes involve both model serving and non-model execution. Together, the results motivate evaluating MAS designs over explicit operating conditions and reporting which tasks are delivered, how well they are solved, and where execution breaks down.
title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates

summary: Continual learning requires a model to learn multiple new tasks sequentially while retaining performance on previous tasks. Projecting model parameters onto the Jacobian null space of previous tasks after unconstrained training on a new task has emerged as an effective paradigm. However, unidirectional projection merely minimizes the parameter distance to the new-task optimum, overlooking the new-task loss landscape. To address this limitation, we propose DUET, a bidirectional projection algorithm that imposes Jacobian null-space constraints from both previous and new tasks during post-training projection. Specifically, DUET formulates the post-training adjustment as a dually constrained optimization problem. It minimizes the distance between parameters before and after training on a new task, subject to loss preserving constraints on both tasks. To solve the optimization problem, we develop an alternating bidirectional projection algorithm, whose convergence is guaranteed by the contraction mapping theorem. For reliable multi-step projection, we rectify existing step size selection criteria via an effective-rank aware formulation, overcoming their failure under rank-deficient Jacobians. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DUET consistently outperforms existing unidirectional projection methods and achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple datasets.
title: Dually Constrained Parameter Projection for Continual Learning

summary: During iterative code modification, coding agents may continue to rely in subsequent reasoning on outdated dependency judgments whose text remains fixed in the context, leading to errors in subsequent reasoning and leaving consumer defects undetected by the original task evaluations, thereby exposing blind spots in the tested benchmarks. We study actual agent execution trajectories collected on benchmark tasks: deepseek-v4-flash runs on DeepSWE and SWE-bench Verified, supplemented by Qwen3.8-Flash cases on FeatureBench. Focusing on edit-induced consumer obligations, a full-corpus blinded human audit of the DeepSWE runs identifies terminal mismatches, including diagnoses whose task scope remains disputed. Following supplementary execution checks, all retained DeepSWE terminal events have execution support. The audit also shows that recovery within a trajectory can coexist with terminal omissions in the same run. The process analysis links the presentation of relevant consumer code to explicit dependency judgments and subsequent synchronization actions recorded in the trajectories. An explicit dependency-review prompt reduces terminal omissions under the tested conditions, supporting re-derivation of consumer obligations after edits. Local replays of selected DeepSWE cases show that synchronizing the diagnosed consumers restores the target behavior while the listed controls continue to pass. Cross-benchmark execution counterexamples show that the original task evaluations do not fully detect edit-induced dependency mismatches: patches pass those evaluations, yet additional execution checks confirm unintended defects along existing consumer paths. These findings support measuring task scores, terminal propagation states, and recovery separately.
title: Edit-Induced Dependency Mismatch: Propagation Omissions, Recovery, and Evaluation Blind Spots in Coding Agents

summary: Multi-criterion LLM judges often evaluate responses without specifying how conflicting criteria resolve, leaving the winner undetermined even under exact criterion scores. Issuing a strict verdict without declaring the required trade-off premise constitutes silent value completion. We introduce TradeoffBench to isolate this failure by separating rule execution from response scoring. On authoritative criterion vectors, six open-weight non-reasoning judges pass all dominance and equality controls yet pick unsupported winners on 9%-81% of 1,345 conflicts. All 577 order-stable choices follow an explicitly banned majority rule. Reasoning-enabled configurations drop anonymous-vector violations to 2 in 9,720 judgments under an explicit rule, yet cannot bridge omitted trade-offs or divergent component scoring. On raw TradeoffBench text with unspecified trade-offs, GPT-6.1-sol omits its completion premise in 29.8% of 400 verified conflicts. Even under an explicit rule on four-rater-consensus MultiPref conflicts, four reasoning judges still issue strict verdicts on 16/45 (GPT-6.1-sol) up to 35/46 and 25/29 (open-weight judges) of valid presentations. We propose identified-first evaluation, decoupling specification support, explicit completion, and target agreement. In MultiPref human-score audits, peer-mean substitution raises directional disagreement from 0.6% to 28.8% on 2,707 shared targets. A single-peer ablation confirms a 29.38-point gap on 2,175 targets, ruling out averaging as the cause. In HUMAINE, declared partial trade-offs add 2.5 percentage points of coverage, yet newly decided pairs incur 3.9% disagreement versus 0.9% for Pareto. Reliable LLM judging, therefore, requires auditing, specification support, declared trade-offs, and human target agreement separately.
title: When Rubrics Do Not Decide: Silent Value Completion in LLM Evaluation

summary: Students may have access to a convincing mathematical explanation without being able to reconstruct or adapt it. A course must provide opportunities to develop that understanding while keeping the work sustainable for students and teachers. This article develops a methodology for service mathematics in which a question ledger guides both course authoring and classroom decisions. Course-relative didactic units organise explanatory purposes, prerequisites and connections, initially calibrated by a five-to-seven-minute expert account. Teaching combines preparation, student exposition and supported repair with substantial teacher exposition and synthesis. Their allocation changes with the topic, audience and conditions of teaching. Compression and recovery explain how developed constructions become reusable while their grounds remain accessible. Three analyses from mathematics for computing-full Sudoku encoding, grayscale projection and a software failure contract-show how contrasting cases guide explanation and revision. The practice-informed contribution connects coherent course design with adaptable teaching and manageable preparation, and identifies questions for evaluating learning, participation and sustained teacher effort.
title: Questions, Explanation and Synthesis in Service Mathematics: Course Design with Didactic Units and Hybrid Teaching

summary: Coordinating large robot fleets, from warehouses to quadrotor swarms, requires collision-free trajectories that satisfy dynamic constraints and stay within speed and acceleration bounds. Existing kinodynamic multi-agent planners enforce these bounds during the search or through trajectory optimization after it, which limits fleet size and speed. We present Tickwise Actions to Kinodynamic Trajectories (TAKT), a framework that accounts for the dynamics before the search and reduces planning to a lattice search for double-integrator robots. TAKT analytically bounds the clearance lost when a discrete plan is smoothed and reserves this margin on the lattice. A closed-form convolution provably converts any valid plan into dynamically feasible trajectories with continuous-time collision avoidance. For robots spanning many lattice vertices, we introduce a diamond formulation that permits one-tick sideways yielding and adapt the Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) solvers PIBT and LaCAM to it. With 50 robots, our planners run over 2,000 times faster than the strongest baseline in 2D halls and over 100 times in 3D, with comparable or lower makespan and cost. They plan about a thousand robots in seconds in 2D, and tens of seconds in 3D, and replan up to a thousand robots in real time.
title: Real-Time Kinodynamic Multi-Agent Motion Planning

summary: World action models (WAMs) excel at robot manipulation by imagining future observations and decoding actions from them, yet remain confined to a single embodied agent. In practice, manipulation often requires multiple robots to collaborate across disjoint workspaces, coupled timing, and heterogeneous embodiments. Such coordination demands both spatiotemporal alignment of future interactions and awareness of individual embodiment and role identities, whereas existing decentralized per-robot policies, flat centralized models, and multi-robot VLAs fail to unite both. To bridge this gap, we present MAWAM, a multi-agent world action model that jointly predicts the future observations of multiple embodiments and decodes each agent's actions from them for collaborative manipulation. Through an agent-axis curriculum, MAWAM expands a single-agent WAM along an agent dimension to coordinate teams under shared weights. Within one unified causal sequence, joint self-attention spans all agents to spatiotemporally align their imagined futures, while hierarchical language, identity encodings, and embodiment masks bind each stream to its role, identity, and embodiment. We further formalize multi-agent-necessary manipulation along three axes (why, when, and who) and develop MA-Task Harness, a coding-agent pipeline where mutually constraining generators and evaluators co-evolve customizable simulation-data and evaluation packages. Using this pipeline, we build MA-Bench across all axes with seven tasks, pairing joint success rate with role and collaboration scores for fine-grained analysis. On MA-Bench, MAWAM reaches 82.7% mean joint success, 30.7% above the strongest baseline, and achieves real-time closed-loop collaboration on a real heterogeneous robot team.
title: MAWAM: Joint Imagination for Collaborative Robot Manipulation with a Multi-Agent World Action Model

On MA-Bench, MAWAM reaches 82.7% mean joint success, 30.7% above the strongest baseline, and achieves real-time closed-loop collaboration on a real heterogeneous robot team.
title: MAWAM: Joint Imagination for Collaborative Robot Manipulation with a Multi-Agent World Action Model

summary: We introduce CoHABIT, a framework for evaluating furniture layouts through complementary spatial rules and household routines. Static assessment captures geometric validity, ergonomic access, functional organization, and configurable design preferences, including Feng Shui. Dynamic assessment uses learned resident policies to simulate everyday activities, resource sharing, coordination, and individual burdens in multi-agent households. Controlled comparisons show how spatial criteria and household behavior reveal distinct aspects of layout quality, while resident profiles and scheduling influence furnishing rankings. Independent verification of household needs grounds dynamic comparisons in observed outcomes, enabling interpretable assessments of how furnished environments serve different households.
title: CoHABIT: Complementary Evaluation of Furniture Layouts through Spatial Rules and Household Routines

summary: Speech brain-computer interfaces aim to restore communication by translating neural activity into text, yet end-to-end decoders have historically trailed cascaded systems in accuracy. We introduce a Multi-Agent System for BraIn-to-Text (MAS-BIT), the first multi-agent framework for end-to-end brain-to-text decoding from intracortical recordings. MAS-BIT coordinates three specialized agents: a neural agent that interprets continuous neural representations, a phonetic agent that decodes soft phoneme posteriors, and an arbitration agent that integrates their complementary evidence with direct access to neural representations to generate the final transcription. The expert agents communicate with the arbiter through token-embedding-based latent communication, constructing continuous messages as probability-weighted combinations of token embeddings. These messages retain alternative token hypotheses and provide a differentiable interface through which sentence-level supervision jointly trains the neural encoders and specialized agents across participants. MAS-BIT achieves state-of-the-art end-to-end decoding performance on the Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks, with word error rates of 6.929% on '24 and 3.606% on the '25 public test set (3.892% on the private test set). These results surpass the published BIT cascade on the '25 public set and narrow the gap on '24, without ensembling independently trained models or using external language-model rescoring.
title: MAS-BIT: A Multi-Agent System for End-to-End BraIn-to-Text Decoding

summary: Semantic occupancy perception has emerged as a promising paradigm for jointly modeling 3D scene geometry and semantic information. However, this unified representation cannot compensate for missing information caused by occlusion and sensor coverage. Multi-agent cooperation alleviates this limitation, but information from different agents is not equally useful across spatial regions. Meanwhile, feature representations from each agent form the basis of reliable multi-agent fusion. Cross?modal fusion constructs such representations by integrating complementary semantic and geometric information. Despite this complementarity, jointly establishing reliable 3D correspondence across agents and preserving modality-specific structures remains challenging. To address these limitations, we propose CoopOcc, which performs cooperative 3D semantic occupancy perception through multi-agent and cross-modal fusion. CoopOcc uses ego?query cross-agent attention (EQCA) to selectively aggregate aligned features across agents, and anchor-based bidirectional feature interaction (ABFI) for cross-modal exchange at matched coordinates. We further construct SemanticVVSim, a simulation dataset, and establish a unified benchmark. For simulation-to-real transfer, we propose confidence-aware hierarchical occupancy and relational distillation (CHORD). CoopOcc performs best overall among ten evaluated methods on SemanticVVSim. On Occ3D-nuScenes, CHORD improves performance using knowledge from SemanticVVSim. The code is available at https://github.com/LOTEAT/CoopOcc.
title: CoopOcc: Cooperative 3D Semantic Occupancy Perception via Multi-Agent and Cross-Modal Fusion

summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming recommender systems from conventional preference matching toward reasoning-driven and explainable decision-making. Multi-agent collaboration further advances this paradigm by distributing recommendation reasoning across specialized agents. However, existing frameworks rarely assess the reliability of intermediate reasoning during collaboration, allowing erroneous judgments to propagate across agents and ultimately degrade recommendation quality. To address this issue, we propose Multi-Agent Debate-based Recommendation (MADRec), an evidence-grounded multi-agent framework that enhances the reliability of multi-agent recommendation reasoning. MADRec consists of three coordinated modules. First, the Multi-Agent Debate (MAD) module enables an Interaction Agent and a Semantic Agent to analyze interaction signals and content-level semantic signals from complementary perspectives, generating diverse recommendation judgments through structured debate. Second, the Evidence-Grounded Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning (EG-RAR) module grounds the Semantic Agent's reasoning in item-level evidence and refines candidate scores by assessing how well the evidence supports the corresponding semantic claims. Third, the Judge-based Ranking Calibration (JRC) module leverages debate-derived reliability cues to adaptively calibrate interaction-based and semantic ranking results for the final recommendation. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate that MADRec consistently outperforms competitive baselines and enhances the reliability of multi-agent recommendation reasoning.
title: MADRec: Reliable Multi-Agent Reasoning with Evidence-Grounded Debate for Recommendation
