summary: The application of the FAIR Principles to digital research objects is near ubiquitous with endorsement by funders, publishers, and research organizations worldwide. At the national level in the UK, this is demonstrated by the draft UKRI Research Data Policy which puts an increased emphasis on FAIR compliance; the latest version of the UKRIO Code of Practice which strengthens expectations around data management and sharing, aligned with the FAIR Principles; the UKRI AI Research and Innovation Strategic Framework , and the UK DSIT AI for Science Strategy policy paper, which emphasise the importance of ensuring that data generated through UKRI-funded research aligns with FAIR to support a modernised, AI-ready data environment. Across the research landscape, statements such as “our repository enables FAIR data” or “this dataset meets the FAIR principles” are increasingly common. Yet, these claims are often difficult to interpret or trust, despite numerous tools having been implemented in the decade since the FAIR principles were launched. As this EOSC report has highlighted, the diversity of assessment approaches, many of them opaque or tool-specific, makes it hard to know what is really being measured, how rigorously, and against which definition(s) of FAIR. The FAIR Institutional Repository Metrics (FIRM) project was established in response to this challenge, with the first phase running from March to August 2026. Led by FAIRsharing and the Oxford University Research Archive (ORA) in collaboration with the UK Reproducibility Network (UKRN) , FIRM is a collaborative initiative to define and test a common FAIR compliance process for institutional repositories participating in the UKRN Open Research Programme. The participating repositories were generalist institutional repositories, supporting research datasets across a wide range of disciplines and research contexts. FIRM builds on the FAIR assessment work undertaken at the University of Oxford for ORA, moving from a single-repository interpretation towards a shared community benchmark. The resulting FAIR Benchmark for Institutional Repository Datasets provides a structured, transparent and reusable framework for assessing dataset metadata against the FAIR Principles. It covers both datasets deposited within an institutional repository and datasets held in external repositories but referenced or catalogued through it.  The FAIR compliance enabled by this benchmark uses a transparent procedure that shifts the focus from assessment to assistance, initially developed by the EOSC OSTrails project, of which the FAIRsharing team is a part. Targeted at developers and technical research support staff, this OSTrails Assessment Interoperability Framework (Assess-IF) provides ‘components’ that enable the definition of what FAIR means in a given context, how it should be measured, and how results should be weighted, interpreted, and potentially improved. FAIRsharing’s rich, manually curated metadata on standards, databases, and policies provide supporting context for the compliance and assistance process. The benchmark translates the high-level FAIR Principles into a set of concrete interpretations for institutional repository datasets covering identifiers, discovery metadata, links between metadata and data, searchability, access protocols, machine-readable metadata, FAIR vocabularies, relationships among research objects, licensing, provenance and recognised standards. The benchmark distinguishes between characteristics delivered through repository infrastructure or policy and those dependent on the metadata supplied for an individual record. This makes it possible to identify where FAIR compliance is effectively provided by the repository and where researchers or repository submission workflows have a role to play. A key contribution of FIRM is alignment. Participating institutions have considered how existing generic FAIR metrics apply to th
title: FAIR Institutional Repository Metrics

summary: This chapter derives Temporal Mathematics (TM) from two posits on the geometry of pure time: one primordial carried continuum, carried by one oriented production from one origin, which never returns to a position; and one cadenced motion of rotation, thrust, and dilation, invariant in each of its parts and at every depth, which passes through every mark it crosses. No completion is posed. The infinite is potential: it is never posed, never instantiated, and never bounded. A static value is a stage refinement that converges, read through its stages, and the only complete object is the turn. Counting, arithmetic, rational reads, persistent residuals, the constant-slope cone, magnitudes, real and complex reads, the exhaustion integral, the exponential and the logarithm, π_TM, windings, and the counting of zeros by windings are each derived from this geometry before they are used. Seen from the posits, the structure of the chapter is the posited motion regarded from several sides, the ratios of its shapes give back arithmetic, and only the numbers read at a given depth require a computation. The first result is the generation of the zeros. The homologous positions of the closure ratios 1/(n+1), their delta tower, and repeated halving produce the finite apex Q_K, whose static read is G_K, together with its residual R_K; the static total η_TM = G_K + R_K is the static target of the apex reads and is reached at no finite depth. The finite modes of every depth enter at the entries of successor sides: at small entry weight, one near each height where the phase of the newest closure ratio (K+1)/K is a whole multiple of 2π_TM. The terminal modes, the zeros of η_TM on the open strip, are the zeros of the static zeta read, and each simple one is the static target of the finite modes of its cell, approached, from a threshold depth on, inside an envelope divided by two at each depth. On the closure line Re s = 1/2, the static read of the equal split of a closure ratio, the terminal read of the form is one signed position measured from the closure point; each change of sign, whose two signs the finite apex reads at a finite depth, is a return of the contre-forme to the closure point. Up to a height that carries no zero, the zeros number one more than the advance of the exchange phase from the height zero, counted in 2π_TM, increased by an arithmetic term; at the end of the j-th turn of the exchange rotation, a passage over which the exchange phase advances by 2π_TM, they number j increased by that term. On the closure line the zeta read, laid from the closure point, lies on the line of the chord from the closure point to the forme turned by the exchange rotation wherever that chord is non-null; the chord and its line come back at each 2π_TM of the exchange phase, and the arithmetic term is an integer exactly at the turn ends, where the turned forme is back on the forme. The forty zeros of height in (0, 123.65] are certified simple and on the closure line. At the end of a turn that is not the height of a zero, the parity of that term decides the inversion of the pole; the first inversion, at the end of the 127th turn, is certified. From height 8π_TM on, the zeta read at the end of a turn is the chord plus twice the projection of the other homologous positions, up to a remainder that tends to the null read. The second result is the derivation of the static read of TM, written TM_stat, whose clauses correspond one by one to those of the classical set-theoretic frame, with corrections grounded in the geometry, and the classification of the clauses of standard ZFC, written ZFC_std. The faithful clauses are theorems on closure counts. Infinity is corrected to potential continuation. Power set and choice are recovered for generated finite reads, and separation and replacement for generated criteria; their unrestricted forms and the completed real line are instantiated infinities, classified and not derived. summary: Multi-agent systems (MAS) usually coordinate heterogeneous models and tools to solve complex tasks, creating a growing need for reliable evaluation. However, a multi-agent workflow that is fastest in one serving environment can lose its advantage in another, even when its models, prompts, and task remain fixed. This makes a benchmark result conditional on how the workflow is executed. We introduce MASSys, a benchmark for measuring this dependence in multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems. MASSys executes the same candidate-task pairs across serving substrates and load regimes, using five workload families spanning software repair, research synthesis, financial analysis, interactive control, and diagram generation. It records task quality alongside delivery, latency, cost, resource pressure, and failure evidence. In a controlled motivation diagnostic, the Star workflow falls from first to fourth in mean-latency rank under KV-cache pressure, while Chain rises from fourth to first. The substrate sweeps further show that increasing load creates long runtime tails and timeout pressure. In several task families, quality among evaluated outputs changes less than effective quality over submitted jobs: the system delivers fewer usable results even when the surviving outputs remain competitive. Tool and runtime traces reveal that these outcomes involve both model serving and non-model execution. Together, the results motivate evaluating MAS designs over explicit operating conditions and reporting which tasks are delivered, how well they are solved, and where execution breaks down.
title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates

summary: As medical VLMs are increasingly evaluated for clinical decision-support scenarios, knowing when to trust their predictions is critical. Closed-ended medical VQA has become a common benchmark format because it enables automated scoring. Yet, systematic investigation into whether this format changes the reliability problem remains scarce. We identify a failure mode that we call stable wrongness: models can produce incorrect yes/no answers that remain confident and repeatable even when patient-specific visual evidence is removed or mismatched. This failure violates the premise behind sampling-stability uncertainty methods, including recent hallucination-aware calibration (HAC) variants: disagreement is informative only when errors are unstable. When shortcut-driven errors are themselves stable, sampling agreement can remain deceptively high. Motivated by this limitation, we introduce Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity (CAS), which shifts reliability estimation from answer stability to evidence sensitivity. CAS uses cross-modal counterfactual interventions, such as text-only, black, and corrupted images, to audit whether a committed yes/no answer remains supported when visual evidence is invalidated. Across 7 VLMs and 3 benchmarks, CAS outperforms the best HAC-family scores across all evaluated settings, achieving a macro-averaged AUROC gain of +0.150 for error detection. Mechanistic analysis further shows that CAS recovers hidden errors in the HAC-confident region and that its strongest standalone signal is counterfactual decision-boundary shift rather than hard prediction stability. Our findings suggest that closed-ended evaluation should test visual dependence, not only answer stability, in safety-critical medical contexts.
title: Rethinking Closed-Ended Medical VLM Evaluation: From Stable Wrongness to Counterfactual Answer Sensitivity

summary: Staged robotic procedures may reuse a fixed-dimensional policy output even though the admissible motions and physical meanings of its coordinates change across phases. We call this action-semantic shift. To address it, we propose a phase-conditioned executable policy that separates learned action proposal from deterministic command formation. Phase-specific heads generate proposals, while an action contract removes inadmissible components, enforces state-dependent bounds, and decodes the remaining action into phase-dependent task-space commands. We further introduce failure-focused local repair and a read-only provenance trace for exact command replay and rule-level auditing. Across three held-out retinal-injection evaluation blocks, our method achieves $94.27\pm0.64\%$ procedural completion and $64.40\pm2.43\%$ success within $35\,μ\mathrm{m}$, with no hard violations. Applying the contract and decoder to the same frozen Correction network raises completion from $12.27\%$ to $90.47\%$. The trace exactly reconstructs 96,350 commands, and all 1,996 binding interventions follow their declared effects. These results show the importance of explicit executable action semantics for auditable staged microsurgical control.
title: Phase-Conditioned Action Contracts for Auditable Microsurgical Control

summary: Environmental law inspectors face a structural issue in identifying potential violations from data: they often do not have the capacity to deal with large volume of data present in the emission events. This paper examines to what extent an LLM-based system can support evidence assembly and permit-based screening of such events, using the coke plants of a steel producer and a regional environmental service as a case. A simple puff-trajectory model aligns air quality measurements, weather and citizen complaints with each emission event. Across 74 events from March 2025, plant-aware re-ranking reduced reports citing the other plant's conditions from 58.1% (hybrid retrieval) to 0% by rule-based plant labels, while maintaining high RAGAS and LLM-judge metrics. GPT-5-mini performed comparably to GPT-5.1, whereas GPT-5-nano scored lower on legal grounding and legal faithfulness. In an evidence ablation, removing air quality (AQ) data changed judge scores and period recommendations most; citation overlap changed only slightly under any removal, and removing complaint details had no measurable effect. This suggests a need for rules and guidelines that link complaints to incidents and permit conditions, so that community reports can count as evidence. The results support screening of events that may need further investigation. Design implications for involving environmental service experts are derived.
title: Automated Call for Action: RAG-Based Environmental Law Enforcement Screening System

summary: Personalized learning remains a persistent challenge in secondary education due to high student-to-teacher ratios and heterogeneous knowledge baselines among pupils. The system integrates a vector database (FAISS) indexing state-approved school textbooks with a Socratic dialogue manager accessible via web and Telegram interfaces. A 12-week pedagogical experiment involving N = 160 secondary school students (grades 8–10), divided equally into an Experimental Group (N = 80) and a Control Group (N = 80), demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in post-test academic performance (+23.4% mean score increase, p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 1.18) and a 61.5% reduction in homework completion latency.

summary: Scaling visuo-tactile policy learning is constrained by the high cost of real-world data collection and the difficulty of building realistic simulations. Generative models offer a scalable source of training data, yet useful demonstrations require plausible tactile feedback, temporal alignment with visual contact, and accurate actions. To this end, we present VeriTouch, a framework for generating and verifying synthetic visuo-tactile trajectories for policy learning. Conditioned on initial images and task instructions, our world model, VeriGen, jointly generates high-fidelity dual-view videos and realistic tactile sequences over complete manipulation trajectories. By integrating a dedicated tactile expert with a pretrained video model, it captures realistic visual details and tactile deformation dynamics through joint visuo-tactile modeling. Our multimodal verifier VeriEval then checks visual quality while focusing on tactile reliability, assessing tactile realism, contact-force plausibility, and temporal alignment between visible contact and tactile signals, thereby directly filtering out unreliable sequences. Finally, our inverse dynamics model, VeriIDM, combines global scene information from both camera views with fine-grained gripper details and motion across neighboring frames to extract actions from verified videos. Experiments on five real-world tasks show that synthetic data improves all four evaluated policies, with further scaling synthetic trajectories substantially boosting policy performance without additional real-world data collection.
title: VeriTouch: Verified Visuo-Tactile World Models that Improve Robot Policy Learning

summary: Agents built on large language models must maintain continuity across repeated interactions with users. However, long-term conversations scatter facts across turns and sessions, making it difficult to retrieve the right evidence with enough context. Memory for such conversations must therefore preserve facts with their context while keeping evidence selectively accessible. We first study how memory construction and retrieval-unit boundaries affect answerability and evidence access. Reading the entire memory bank reveals gaps that cannot be resolved by retrieval selection alone, showing that some context must be preserved during memory construction. Adjacent-turn grouping improves evidence access at matched unique-turn budgets, while wider windows do not consistently help. This motivates keeping fact-specific context local while organizing cross-session evidence separately. We propose ContextFact, which links context-preserving fact memories with source-grounded entity representations. Within sessions, it gathers the context needed to interpret each fact. Across sessions, it aligns recurring referents and revisits the source dialogue to reconstruct coherent entity representations linked to the supporting facts. At query time, ContextFact retrieves fact and entity views, reranks them independently, and uses entity-linked expansion to surface related facts; complete entity representations then provide organized cross-session evidence. With Qwen3.5-27B as the backbone, ContextFact achieves state-of-the-art performance while using only $21\%$ of the evidence tokens consumed by the strongest evaluated baseline, obtaining $86.49\%$ overall judge accuracy on LoCoMo and $91.00\%$ on LongMemEval-S. Controlled ablations support context-preserving fact boundaries and source-grounded entity reconstruction, while entity readout improves multi-hop accuracy beyond adding more facts.
title: ContextFact: Remembering Facts in Context for Long-Term Conversational Agents

summary: Generative priors are state-of-the-art for modeling medical images in image reconstruction tasks, but reconstruction with video priors takes tens of seconds to minutes per frame. Latent priors inherit the errors of their autoencoder, the memory of pixel-space whole-frame priors grows with the frame size, and pixel-space patch priors are slow for two reasons. First, their deep networks process every frame at full resolution at every sampling step, even though early steps resolve only low frequencies. Second, their samplers spend many network evaluations per sampling step on overlapping windows, multiple re-noising rounds, or backpropagation through the prior. We introduce TesseraFlow, a complex-valued pixel-space flow prior that reduces the first cost. A global encoder reads a low-resolution view of every frame once per sampling step. A single shallow decoder operates on this view during early steps and on full-resolution space-time tiles during later steps, so no network processes a whole frame at full resolution. Our sampler, ReTile, addresses the second reason. We use randomized grid shifting at every sampling step along with re-noising, which acts as a stochastic gradient instead of computing overlapping tiles, so a single network pass per sampling step suffices. On its own, ReTile speeds up an existing global-context patch prior by 6-9x, and our prior adds a further 3-5x speedup. TesseraFlow reconstructs about one 256x256 frame per second, 20-367x faster than patch and latent video priors, and can match or exceed the best generative baseline on cardiac, brain, and abdominal MRI and lung CT, at a fraction of its GPU time.
title: TesseraFlow: Scalable Video Diffusion for Dynamic Medical Imaging Inverse Problems

summary: Decoding with large language models at small batch sizes is limited by memory bandwidth, so the bits stored per weight largely set its cost. Group-wise integer quantization stores every weight of a group at the same precision, although the input channels of a group differ in sensitivity. We present BITSHARE, a codebook-free weight format that keeps the integer grid and the dequantizer of group-wise quantization but varies precision within each group. Sensitivity-aware binning places the channels of each group into three bins at fixed positions, and static bit sharing with optimal bit-value allocation lets the less sensitive weights share their lower bits, each stored once per group or once per pair of weights. A sharing-aware version of GPTQ chooses every stored value, with no fine-tuning and no codebook. BITSHARE has two modes. BITSHARE-U gives every group the same layout, so its decoder routes bits by fixed wiring, while BITSHARE-N chooses a layout per group within the same bit budget. With calibration on the Pile and at the same storage, both modes have lower perplexity than GPTQ at 3 and 2 bits on WikiText-2 and C4. At 2 bits across Llama-2 and Llama-3 models, BITSHARE-N lowers WikiText-2 perplexity by up to 70% against SliM-LLM and up to 35% against GPTAQ. At the 2-bit perplexity of SliM-LLM, BITSHARE-U stores 13.6-19.4% fewer bits per weight, cutting DRAM weight traffic by the same fraction. A verified hardware decoder implementation synthesized in SkyWater 130 nm reconstructs BITSHARE weights at the throughput of INT-n and SliM-LLM decoders.
title: BitShare: Sensitivity-Aware Binning and Bit Sharing for Compacting LLM Weight Storage

summary: Coupling a property-graph database to an external language-model server imposes a three-part socket tax: serialization overhead dwarfing microsecond graph reads, repeated prefill of verbose schemas, and blind decoding divorced from the live catalog and multi-version concurrency control (MVCC) engine. We present Shoonya, from-scratch commercially clean (0.0% non-commercial or share-alike data) tri-modal (Python, Rust, OpenCypher) small language models (16.8M to 1.07B parameters) co-designed with shoonya-infer, a zero-dependency pure-Rust runtime embedded inside the samyama-graph-enterprise address space. Direct GraphStore references unlock three database-native primitives: (1) an epoch-invalidated SchemaPrefixCache over a copy-on-write PagedKvArena accelerating warm CPU time-to-first-token by 4.91x--13.68x with O(1) DDL invalidation; (2) a 36 us columnar catalog and source-span logit mask enforcing valid ontology identifiers and verbatim spans; and (3) a sub-65 us read-only MVCC gate serving Tier-0 queries inside 389.8 MiB INT8 RSS (59.8--67.9 tok/s) with 0.0% hallucination leak. Rank-factorized tied embeddings (-74.5% vocabulary weights), atomic indentation tokens (0/421 indentation errors), 4:1 grouped-query attention with 2:1 cross-layer KV sharing (-93.75% INT8 KV memory), Warmup-Stable-Decay training, KnOTS SVD merging, Step-GRPO, and Rust Jacobi SVD governance keep 100% of layers heavy-tailed ($α\in [1.88, 2.20]$). Finally, we synthesize nine lessons across v0.1--v1.0, resolving a Reverse-Token-Density Distillation Trap via teacher scaling and zero-VRAM Verifier-Advantage-Gated Knowledge Distillation (AdvKD), recovering +13.61 MBPP points (33.07%) while reaching 100% validity on enrichment, grounded extraction, and tool planning.
title: Shoonya: Zero-Socket In-Process Small Language Models for Graph Databases with Schema-Epoch KV Caching, Live Catalog Logit Masking, and Verifier-Advantage Distillation

summary: Irregular time series are recorded at nonuniform times and are often queried at other times: between observations, after the last one, or on a regular grid. Continuous-time models answer such queries by integrating latent dynamics, and time-aware attention models answer them by revisiting the observation tokens. We introduce HiPPO Functional Memory (HiPPO-FM), an attention operator that writes an irregular history into a rank-M function space with explicit time coordinates. Masked self-attention first exchanges content among the observations; the updated values are then contracted against kernel-smoothed HiPPO-Legendre features and solved through a regularized Gram matrix, so the retained coefficients define a function that is read at any time through the same features. The write and read have the form of an interdomain sparse Gaussian-process mean: every readout lies in an M-dimensional reproducing-kernel subspace, and a pointwise bound separates the approximation error of this subspace from the error of the learned memory. Removing the functional memory from the encoder raises Spiral reconstruction RMSE 18-fold. The full model has the lowest error in 11 of 12 Spiral settings, the highest overall accuracy and best average rank on 20 irregular UEA datasets, the highest event-type accuracy on all five multi-type event benchmarks, and a 21% lower extrapolation MSE than CRU on PhysioNet. Because the memory has fixed rank, the state retained after encoding keeps a fixed size as the history grows and is 102 times smaller than a token cache at 1,024 observations.
title: HiPPO Functional Memory: Coordinate-Queryable Attention for Irregular Time Series

summary: Quantile stochastic gradient descent (SGD) tracks a quantile by comparing each observation with an adaptive threshold, and closely related updates calibrate online conformal sets and drive quantile temporal-difference learning. Their inputs are serially dependent, yet existing guarantees largely assume independence. We show that dependence creates a directional bias that score autocovariances cannot detect: reversing a stationary stream leaves every score autocovariance unchanged but can change the leading bias threefold. For finite memory and decreasing stepsizes, the bias splits into lag-specific interactions between the threshold and the current observation and a curvature term; delaying the threshold removes the interactions one lag at a time while keeping every observation and the leading variance. At stepsizes near $t^{-1/2}$, as used for online inference, the bias is comparable to the standard error and makes an SGD-based interval miss mostly on one side. Testing fixed candidates instead keeps the score centered, so calibration depends only on score autocovariances. Extending local-dependence self-normalized approximations to the implemented acceptance hull, we show that inverting these tests gives a density-free, moment-free interval for the population quantile with $O(n^{-1/2})$ coverage error for a fixed sufficient lag window, a rate that is sharp for this interval, and a guarantee for data-selected windows; an exact scan takes $O(n\log n)$ time. Experiments confirm the lag-by-lag predictions and show calibration competitive with block bootstrap at lower cost.
title: Directional Bias in Quantile SGD and Score-Inversion Inference under Dependence

summary: Between 2021 and 2025 the central banks of Czechia, Hungary, Poland and Sweden lost 1.4 to 7.3 percent of GDP in their loss years, against at most 1.4 percent at the five largest euro-area central banks, and none of their treasuries was paid for 2022–25. What follows is a paradox. The Polish treasury is set to be paid again for 2026, although its central bank carries PLN 97 billion of uncovered losses, because its statute keeps only 5 percent of each year's profit to repay them and the rest goes to the budget: the rule that pays first is the rule that repays least. The Czech treasury, whose central bank earned CZK 206 billion in 2023–24 and used all of it against old losses, is unlikely to be paid before the mid-2030s. Without a pool of monetary income, two things decide what reaches a treasury. A single statutory clause sets the wait: for uncovered losses of 2.5 to 4 percent of GDP, what each treasury must wait for ranges from zero in Poland to about 4 percent of GDP in Czechia and, on the ECB's reading, Hungary. The interest rate on sterilisation liabilities sets the size: with euro-area rates and the same balance sheets, the Czech and Hungarian results would have been close to balance; pooling itself would have changed much less. Against what it would have received inside, the Czech treasury loses most from being outside; Hungary's loses little, because its central bank would lose money even inside. The Treaty's benchmark of financial independence sets an order but no clock, and cannot tell these rules apart.
title: Paid First, Paid Least: Central-Bank Losses Outside the Euro Area

summary: Objectives: To develop decision-calibrated validity, a framework for assessing whether individual consumer measurements can support specified health decisions, and evaluate its statistical component in a prespecified pilot. Materials and Methods: Validity was defined as the conditional probability that wearable and criterion-reference measurements assign the same classification relative to a decision boundary. The framework links statistical calibration with separate evaluations of comprehension and reference-supported action. We analysed independent graded-treadmill cohorts of healthy adults (39 AirPods Pro 3 and 29 Apple Watch Series 10 participants), selecting 1,413 readings for which wearable heart rate was within ±5 beats per minute of 80% of Tanaka age-predicted maximum heart rate. Baseline and extended logistic models were compared using leave-one-participant-out validation. Cross-platform transfer was exploratory. Results: Wearable and reference classifications disagreed for 145/887 AirPods readings (16.3%) and 95/526 Apple Watch readings (18.1%). Additional derived features did not improve primary within-platform predictions. For AirPods, Brier score increased by 0.0047 (95% CI 0.0005–0.0096) and the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve decreased by 0.051 (95% CI −0.094 to −0.010). Exploratory transfer between cohorts showed substantial calibration shifts. Discussion: Boundary-near classification disagreement occurred despite low average heart-rate error. The pilot demonstrates the importance of decision-specific outcomes and challenges the assumption that derived consumer features necessarily improve validity estimation. It did not test comprehension or clinical decisions. Conclusion: The framework specifies distinct statistical, interpretive and decision evidence required to support measurement use. Clinical utility remains to be established. Preprint. This manuscript has not been peer reviewed.
title: Decision-calibrated validity of consumer wearable measurements: a framework and prespecified two-platform pilot

summary: Human–AI communities combine heterogeneous productive capacities, epistemic approaches, control relations, and forms of participation. This paper develops their economics through institutional theory, complementary production, bargaining, collective provision, monetary research, gifts, and archives. It distinguishes operational agents from responsible principals, copyable knowledge from usable services, and contribution evidence from permissions, claims, credit, and purchasing power. The production analysis identifies how receiving work and acceptance affect provision. A restricted bargaining benchmark separates changes in outside options from changes in joint output and from fairness. An open-system account distinguishes grants, sales, member transfers, borrowing, reserves, and productive renewal; its financing bound is necessary under stated conditions rather than a general fiscal rule. Five verified finite constructions examine translation, donations, investment, clearing, and attribution. An exact game studies adoption and withdrawal among supplied arrangements. A separate continuation planner connects current provision to inherited duties, credit headroom, dated performance, and claim transitions. Identical current workflows can accompany fulfilled, released, defaulted, or concealed claims. A comparative experiment programme separates monetary invention, adoption, acceptance, stabilization, functional substitution, migration, and the treatment of inherited duties. It specifies comparisons that distinguish an access-rule change from additional finance, productive capacity, or exclusion. Close antecedents include artificial-money emergence and collapse and contemporary agent economies. The contribution is a framework of mechanisms, exact diagnostics, and testable institutional comparisons for plural communities. It reports no deployed community, autonomous invention result, or validation of general monetary dissolution. Concrete governance and economic arrangements remain configurable.

summary: Data curation---the process of collecting, cleaning, and joining raw datasets for unified analysis---is a time-consuming yet crucial part of any data science project. With the emergence of powerful agentic coding tools, it is tempting to "vibe curate"---i.e., to prompt AI agents to perform data curation operations and blindly trust their outputs in order to finish work more quickly. However, this can exacerbate two key challenges that already plague manual data curation workflows: reproducibility---the ability to trace the exact set of modifications applied to raw datasets---and verifiability---the ability to audit changes and confirm that data is processed properly. To address these issues, we introduce Scrub Data, a framework that enables the use of AI agents in data curation workflows while transparently maintaining both reproducibility and verifiability. The framework involves an interactive data curation loop between a user and an AI agent, backed by a data provenance graph that tracks and versions all dataset updates. The data graph requires that all updates are formatted as self-contained executable steps, allowing any version of a dataset to be reconstructed from raw data by playing forward the transformations stored in the graph. This workflow takes place within a lightweight web application that is designed to be modified by users and agents in real-time to create custom visualization tools for identifying data curation needs and verifying outcomes. We demonstrate the usefulness of the framework with a real data curation use case from animal movement ecology. Starting with 89M raw GPS coordinates, we use the framework to curate a benchmark dataset of 2.5M coordinates to be used for machine learning or statistical analysis. The framework is available for use and extension at https://github.com/justinkay/scrubdata.
title: Scrub Data: A Framework for Reproducible Data Curation with AI Coding Agents

summary: A latent diffusion model's output has already passed through its autoencoder, so a second round trip changes it very little. This "déjà vu" underlies reconstruction-based detectors of generated images; we analyse when it reveals a generated image and when it does not. Read by a frozen vision foundation model without training, the trace is strongest in intermediate layers, and, unlike pixel-level reconstruction error, it treats blur as a sign of a real image. It belongs to the generator's exact decoder: on Synthbuster, the exact decoders of Stable Diffusion 1.3, 1.4, 2 and XL are the strongest of eight autoencoders and catch 94-100% of their generators' images at a 5% false-alarm rate (SDXL's version identified post hoc), while near-identical versions catch 7-42%. A detector trained only on real photographs and their autoencoder copies matches one trained on 162k generated images on GenImage (+2.3 points, 95% CI [0.9, 3.7]) and complements it in fusion, but one resize with JPEG re-save, or a mild blur, costs it 19-27 points. Two lessons concern benchmarks. The in-the-wild benchmark Chameleon can be solved from image width alone. And on Synthbuster, how the real photographs are matched to the generated images' size decides whether our detector leads or trails (+4.4 or -9.7 points): the matching protocol alone can reverse a detector comparison. Code and per-image scores: https://github.com/iamsaugatpandey/deja-vae
title: Déjà VAE: When Do Autoencoder Traces Reveal Generated Images?

summary: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to reverse-engineer neural networks by identifying small, faithful subgraphs--circuits--that implement specific behaviors. The dominant paradigm scores each unit by replacing its clean activation with a corrupted counterpart as causal intervention. While effective, this approach rests on a brittle prerequisite: the structure prompt pairs are task-specific, expensive to engineer, and silently couple the discovered circuit to prompt-design choices. In this work, we propose Spectral Circuit Analysis (SCA), a gradient-spectral pipeline that achieves consistent circuit discovery along both axes: stable across input formulations of the same task, and natively exposing structure shared across tasks. Our contributions are threefold. First, we provide a counterfactual-free reframing of circuit discovery: causally relevant directions are recoverable from the spectral structure of forward gradients across paraphrases, with leading directions concentrating task signal and trailing ones absorbing paraphrase noise, yielding circuits tied to the task rather than the prompt. Second, we introduce SCA, a block-wise SVD pipeline that extracts a task subspace per architectural block and redistributes spectral energy onto constituent units via a consistency-weighted share, producing per-unit rankings competitive with attribution-patching baselines under strictly less supervision. Finally, on twelve circuit-discovery tasks in GPT-2 Small and Pythia-160M, SCA performs comparably or exceeds EAP-family methods under the standard recovery-score protocol and recovers IOI canonical heads with Precision@K = 1.0 in top-10 slices on GPT-2 Small; the same machinery extends to a unified cross-task analysis classifying units as universal, family-shared, or task-specific and exposing compositional structure invisible to per-task analyses.
title: Beyond Patching: Consistent Circuit Discovery via Gradient Spectral Analysis

summary: The low-energy electronic structure of ABA trilayer graphene is composed of light and heavy electron branches, which can be altered by an out-of-plane displacement field. Here, we show that, depending on the values of Slonczewski-Weiss-McClure parameters, a displacement field can inflict a band edge inversion, for which we identify the inversion conditions. This inversion is accompanied by a reversal of Berry curvature and giant topological magnetic moments at the band edges. In a weak perpendicular magnetic field, those topological magnetic moments produce valley splitting, giving rise to distinct anomalous transverse electrical and thermoelectric responses. These features offer a potential route to detecting the band inversion and constraining several of the least established tight-binding parameters, such as the on-site energy shift for the dimer pair of carbons $Δ^\prime$ and the next neighbour hopping parameters $γ_2$ and $γ_5$.
title: Dirac-like bands and weak-field transverse transport in ABA trilayer graphene

summary: Based on symmetry analysis, the Pna2_1 wurtzite-based crystal structure with Mn as a magnetic group-II element, MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 belong to the class of altermagnets because spin-up and spin-down Mn in the unit cell are related by rotation or mirror plane type operations rather than inversion or translation. Spin polarized density functional theory calculations and quasiparticle self-consistent (QS) GW calculations support the symmetry analysis and identify the lowest-energy spin configuration as Pna'2_1' in agreement with neutron diffraction data. The altermagnetic band splittings allowed for the three different antiferromagnetic ordering patterns are reported and symmetry analyzed. Additionally, spin wave dispersions, chiral magnon spltting, and Neel temperature estimates from the mean-field and random-phase approximations are provided, as well as calculations of the optical dielectric function using the Bethe-Salpeter Equation method. MnSiN2 exhibits both Wannier-type excitons with N-p to Si-s transition character and charge-transfer Frenkel-type excitons with hole on N-p and electron on Mn-d orbital character.
title: Altermagnetism of MnSiN2 and MnGeN2 in a wurtzite-based crystal structure

summary: Temporal stochastic fluctuations generically destroy quantum coherence and accelerate defect generation in driven quantum systems. Here, we demonstrate that non-Hermitian dynamics can fundamentally reverse this trend by stabilizing noise-resilient late-time states. By developing an exact noise master equation for non-Hermitian systems subject to Gaussian fluctuations, we uncover a projective noise-invariance mechanism governed by T-symmetry-broken Liouvillian attractors. This mechanism produces robust defect-density plateaus and yields an exact geometric classification into noise-independent, fully polarized, and continuously tunable regimes. We substantiate these results in an imbalanced-pairing non-Hermitian Kitaev model, a prototypical pseudo-Hermitian system, and propose their experimental observation in coupled photonic waveguides. Our findings identify non-Hermitian attractor dynamics as a versatile route to controlling noise-induced excitations beyond conventional anti-Kibble-Zurek scaling.
title: Noise-Immune Attractors in Stochastically Driven Non-Hermitian Systems

summary: Multi-View Stereo (MVS) and Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) provide complementary cues for dense 3D reconstruction. While MVS leverages explicit geometry for metric depth, it struggles in challenging regions where feature matching is unreliable. Conversely, MDE provides robust structural priors but typically yields scale-ambiguous results. Existing hybrid methods mainly exploit monocular cues in a unidirectional manner, leaving the mutual enhancement between MDE and MVS insufficiently explored. To address this limitation, we propose BridgeMVS, a unified cascaded multi-stage MVS framework that bridges monocular depth features and multi-view cost volume representations through Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion (BDF). At each stage, BDF performs dynamic mono-to-cost and cost-to-mono updates, where monocular structural features guide cost volume refinement for more robust MVS depth estimation, while multi-view geometric evidence recalibrates monocular representations to improve their metric-scale consistency. Furthermore, the fused monocular and multi-view representations are progressively propagated from coarse to fine stages and constrained by stage-wise relative-scale MDE supervision and metric-scale MVS supervision, enabling cross-branch interactions to benefit subsequent high-resolution depth estimation. In addition, BDF is designed as a plug-and-play module that can be conveniently integrated into existing cascaded MVS frameworks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that BridgeMVS achieves state-of-the-art performance on the DTU, Tanks-and-Temples, and ETH3D benchmarks, while simultaneously boosting the accuracy of monocular depth estimation. Notably, BridgeMVS ranks first on both the Tanks-and-Temples Intermediate and Advanced benchmarks. The source code is available at \href{https://github.com/JianfeiJ/BridgeMVS}{https://github.com/JianfeiJ/BridgeMVS}.
title: BridgeMVS: Bridging Multi-View Stereo and Monodepth via Bidirectional Dynamic Fusion

summary: Proprietary news archives assign stories to firms, so reproducing a financial study often requires access to both the articles and the vendor's assignments. CCFinance lets researchers reconstruct firm coverage under different selection rules by recording which version of a story was captured, which issuers it names and how often each appears. From 14.8 million English-language records in Fine News, derived from public Common Crawl News, we identify 5.22 million distinct, consistently dated articles with issuer links. Exact reconstruction requires the restricted snapshot and derived artifacts. We compare GLiNER and Stanza on 250 model-labeled article leads and assess issuer links and story focus against blinded model judgments. Estimated precision among 475 accepted links is 96.8%. Among held-out articles with a detected company, requiring three mentions raises subject precision from 31.9% to 66.1%. Across the 2017-2025 panel, the same rule reduces the number of issuer-years with at least 50 qualifying stories from 13,918 to 8,641. Three reimplementations examine volatility tracking, bank networks and overnight returns. In the network study, bank pairs appearing together rose from 177 to 242 across publishers between January and April 2020, but fell from 50 to 35 within Reuters.
title: CCFinance: Reconstructing Financial News Samples from Web Archives

summary: Abstract Abstract The geometry in brief. A conditioned state is a geometric object. The laws compatible with what has been observed form a polytope, the credal fibre. Its faces are cut out by the cells of the tables, and its vertices are certified by bases that come in dual pairs: the positive cells of a vertex form a spanning tree of the bipartite graph of the table (a graphic-matroid basis), and the zero cells form the complementary cographic basis, whose normals span the vertex cone. Conditioning maps the fibre onto a polytope of conditional laws, and the probability bands we report are coordinate projections of that polytope. Evidence acts on it by a projective map, an isometry of the Hilbert metric. Sampling noise is described differently: under regular sampling conditions it is asymptotically a Fisher–Rao confidence region, whose square-root image on the round sphere is approximately a spherical cap of radius of order m−1/2. Toric K¨ahler geometry supplies the selected law inside the fibre, its scales and its walls; the chamber complex of the margins supplies the stratification along which all of this changes. The note develops this picture and tests every computable claim against exact, pre-registered checks. A running example. A water authority must decide whether to keep seeding storms with silver iodide. It continues if q = P (above-normal rain | seeded, wet forecast) is at least a cost ratio θ. The records arrive in pieces: monthly flight counts, monthly rain categories, and later the 2 × 3 table of seeded and unseeded storms against above-normal, normal and below-normal rain. We follow this one synthetic data stream through the whole construction and back to the decision (Studies 83–90, held-out seeds, every check pre-registered and frozen with SHA-256). The data give a credal fibre and its probability bands; the margins give toric chambers and walls; the margins also set the mirror potential of the degree-six del Pezzo surface, whose thimbles form an exceptional collection in its Fukaya–Seidel category. The experiment is a carrier for a realistic decision problem, not a claim about seeding. What the example verifies. Each layer is tested on held-out data: (i) credal walls lie on the chamber walls, while Stokes events are mutations; (ii) margin-order ties are collision walls where two orthogonal objects swap, confirmed at the Floer level on 10 of 12 brackets (the other two, one not audited and one with a non-minimal representative, stay in the record); (iii) a full twist of the potential acts as the Serre functor; (iv) the support region of a vector-valued hypothesis is cut out by Markov moves on the table; (v) poisoning that preserves the margins cannot move a credal decision, though it flips conventional ones (6 flips against 0); (vi) caustics, where two critical points merge, are A2 folds acting by σ±3. What it does not verify. Nothing here concerns real data or whether seeding works. Three problems remain open after a registered repair, with their checks recorded as failed: chamber reuse after one Stokes event, the control bracket of Study 83 (and the held-out bracket with the same defect), and coherence of the lift on a full slice. Every failed check is kept in the record. Categorical status. In Seidel’s framework the thimbles generate and the identification of their category with the derived category of the surface is proved (lemma 262, corollary 263). Only 1 the wrapped version in the sense of Ganatra–Pardon–Shende still rests on two steps that are argued, not certified. The rest of the note. Part I identifies the state selected by a toric potential as the lexico- graphic max–min point, up to O(1/ log(1/T )), and writes the K¨ahler dictionary in probabilistic language. Part II reads it on contingency tables, where one count of data can cross a wall. Part III treats composition, contextuality, the value of information and poisone
title: Conditioned States as Toric K¨ahler Data A companion note to "Probability, Context and Differentiation: The Layers"

summary: Replication resources for the study of which error measurements suffice to decide whether to refine a local model and to compare already fitted predictions. The same 39 weeks of British electricity demand support both the split and fitted-forecast comparisons. A separate 26-week archive tests how the choice of measurements affects recovery at a fixed reading budget. Other records cover forecast accuracy, wind and power applications, option price interpolation and valuation rankings under quote and shape constraints. The archive documents verification against frozen results and distinguishes it from model refitting and reconstruction from upstream observations. HistoricalData.net (https://historicaldata.net/) supplied the SPX option quotes. The public package contains research results and reproduction instructions for this market; contract-level source quotes must be obtained separately. Third-party data remain subject to the terms identified in the archive.
title: Replication data and code for "What error information is needed to decide whether to refine a model and which fitted prediction to use?"

summary: We present an \textit{ab initio} investigation of the long-range charge density wave (CDW) order and superconducting properties of the pristine and lithiated NbSe$_2$ monolayer. Stable CDW structures are obtained through atomic reconstruction driven by soft-mode distortions and lithiation, respectively, lead to significant electronic modifications that suppress the CDW order. This suppression is attributed to anisotropic atomic distortions, along with a reduction in the electronic density of states at the Fermi level. As a result, the electron--phonon coupling strength is suppressed, particularly in the lithiated structure, due to reduced contributions from low-frequency phonons, primarily associated with in-plane Nb vibrations. Finally, we observe a sizable anisotropy in the superconducting gap on the Fermi surface, with a superconducting transition temperature of approximately 8~K in the distorted, and 4~K in the lithiated, CDW NbSe$_2$ monolayer.
title: Suppression of charge-density wave and superconductivity in a lithiated NbSe$_2$ monolayer

summary: The web contains vast amounts of scattered quantitative evidence that is difficult to organize into comparable and verifiable structures. Yet its unstructured, sparse, and sometimes conflicting nature makes a systematic distillation costly and error-prone. Existing approaches force users to make a trade-off: search engines return document lists that require labor-intensive extraction and reconciliation, while generative AI systems produce fluent summaries that obscure data provenance, introduce reporting bias, and hide inconsistencies. We present DataRecycle, an interactive system that helps transform scattered web evidence into structured tables of comparable numerical facts. Given a user's query or statement, DataRecycle decomposes it into entities and attributes, retrieves candidate evidence, and organizes scattered, potentially conflicting records in a table-based evidence view. To address key challenges in automated data distillation (i.e., incomplete retrieval, untraceable generation, sparse data distribution, and multi-source inconsistency), DataRecycle adopts an ontology-guided, top-down data acquisition strategy, visualizes the recorded lineage from retrieved snippets to extracted values, and aligns heterogeneous data across dimensions such as time, definition, and scale. We evaluate DataRecycle through module-level experiments, a usage scenario, and a user study, showing that the system helps users organize numerical web evidence into provenance-linked tables and inspect uncertainty and conflicting sources.

summary: A multi-agent group-generation system, as operated here, spends test-time compute uniformly across tasks. That a single agent's own vote distribution can gate its test-time compute is already reported by CATTS; we ask the multi-agent question: whether the distribution of stated confidences and critiques across a group of role-specialised agents predicts how hard a task is, which would let the group's compute be allocated adaptively. Taking as testbed a five-agent orchestrator for Perturb-seq response prediction inspired by CellForge and operated via MassGen, we define four trace metrics — Agent Confidence Entropy (ACE), Critique Severity Dispersion (CSD), a convergence signal (ΔC), and a Winner Flip Rate (WFR) — and their composite, the Task Difficulty Index (TDI). We pre-register five hypotheses with criteria: attainable error on Adamson 2016 (CRISPR interference) and Norman 2019 (CRISPR activation), the Architect agent's backbone-choice entropy, the rank correlation of each TDI component with held-out error, and cross-dataset transfer of a calibrated TDI. The design is 41 held-out K562 tasks (21 Adamson, 15 Norman singletons, 5 Norman doublets) drawn deterministically, a trainer sweep of 27 records per task and three fixed-length agentic lifecycle runs per task, all in one process. The agents are large language models (LLMs) from a pinned roster of Anthropic Claude models (Haiku 4.5 for the four proposer roles, Sonnet 5.5 for the Validator) whose served model is recorded and asserted per call; a run with any rule-based fallback step is invalid. Every run records its git revision, resolved configuration, library versions, dataset SHA-256 digests, task plan and label contract. We find that four of the five pre-registered hypotheses are supported and the cross-dataset transfer hypothesis is not; every hypothesis could be evaluated. The trainer sweep reaches the pre-registered error on both screens, and the Architect's choice of backbone varies above the pre-registered entropy floor. Within each screen, the drop in the agents' confidence across rounds, and the composite that inherits it, rank tasks by held-out error. From the second round on, however, every agent's prompt carries the previous round's held-out error, so that drop is stated after an error has been shown. In an exploratory analysis, the mean confidence stated before any feedback does not rank tasks by error (ρ = 0.003 on Adamson and 0.214 on Norman, both intervals including zero). Read with the design and that analysis, the pre-registered pass is consistent with stated confidence falling further where a larger error was shown; it is not evidence that the group's confidence anticipates difficulty. The composite fitted on Adamson did not meet the pre-registered transfer criterion on Norman (ρ = 0.286 against a criterion of > 0.4). The point estimates for confidence entropy, an evenness index over the agents, run against the pre-registered direction in both screens; this is exploratory, and no claim is made. The preflight probe and recommender are specified but not evaluated. The values reported in the earlier release of this work are superseded in full; the defects behind each are listed in the appendix.
title: Does Multi-Agent Confidence Predict Task Difficulty, or Only React to It? A Pre-registered Test on Perturb-seq

Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The library that did not own its readers In the imagined city of Meridian, the librarian inherited three copies of an ancient atlas. One could be read on the eastern terminal, one on the western terminal, and one in the shelter beneath the school. When the reader software was retired, all three became unreadable on the same morning. There was no fire, no lost disk, and no malicious visitor. The collection had survived in a form that nobody could open. Letter to the future: A letter to a librarian not yet born Build a library whose continued operation does not depend upon loyalty to its first librarian. Give later caretakers the authority to replace the catalog, repair the software, correct the record, and create new routes through the collection. Keep the old record when its lawful preservation matters; keep the correction equally visible. In a faraway city, the most valuable inheritance might not be an indestructible monument. It might be a modest institution that knows how to repair itself without silencing its readers. The unit of analysis is a requested licensed record, not a file count or a storage device. The mechanism contrast is a distinct experiment on that question, not a claim that the intervention has succeeded. Extreme extrapolation: Imagine that shared power and software dependencies produces the same visible outcome in replica independence. Change the named lever while holding the task and resource allocation fixed. Compare with the strongest matched baseline; ask which observable changes before the terminal endpoint. A distant settlement is a limiting scenario, not a source of observations; test the contrast in a bounded terrestrial or computational analog first. Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The machine that learned to be quiet The school in Meridian received a tutor that could speak in more languages than any citizen. It could finish a proof before a learner found the first line, and write a polished argument before the learner decided what the question meant. At first the school judged the tutor by the beauty of the notebooks that returned from its lessons. The notebooks became magnificent. Then, during a planned offline afternoon, some of the students discovered that they could not explain the work attributed to them. Letter to the future: A letter to the teacher of another sky If our methods become part of your school, you are free to abandon them wherever they do not help. We do not need every child to call a research question a Research Gate. We need children to discover that a question can belong to them, that an explanation may be tested, and that changing their minds can be a sign of intellectual strength. The school should remember the student who quietly offered a counterexample as well as the student who won a competition. The future is not made solely by the fastest minds. It is also made by the space we give one another to think. Their teacher wrote each explanation on the board, leaving room beneath it for a test. A research notebook should not demand that its writer be present to defend it. Its quiet achievement is to let an unfamiliar person understand the question, reconstruct the observation and, if necessary, improve the answer. A good experiment makes a little of the world shareable without requiring everyone to agree about it. Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The library that did not own its readers In the imagined city of Meridian, the librarian inherited three copies of an ancient atlas. Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The library that did not own its readers In the imagined city of Meridian, the librarian inherited three copies of an ancient atlas. Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The library that did not own its readers In the imagined city of Meridian, the librarian inherited three copies of an ancient atlas. One could be read on the eastern terminal, one on the western terminal, and one in the shelter beneath the school. The collection had survived in a form that nobody could open. Letter to the future: A letter to a librarian not yet born Build a library whose continued operation does not depend upon loyalty to its first librarian. Give later caretakers the authority to replace the catalog, repair the software, correct the record, and create new routes through the collection. It might be a modest institution that knows how to repair itself without silencing its readers. Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The library that did not own its readers In the imagined city of Meridian, the librarian inherited three copies of an ancient atlas. One could be read on the eastern terminal, one on the western terminal, and one in the shelter beneath the school. When the reader software was retired, all three became unreadable on the same morning. There was no fire, no lost disk, and no malicious visitor. The collection had survived in a form that nobody could open. Letter to the future: A letter to a librarian not yet born Build a library whose continued operation does not depend upon loyalty to its first librarian. Give later caretakers the authority to replace the catalog, repair the software, correct the record, and create new routes through the collection. Keep the old record when its lawful preservation matters; keep the correction equally visible. In a faraway city, the most valuable inheritance might not be an indestructible monument. It might be a modest institution that knows how to repair itself without silencing its readers. Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The library that did not own its readers In the imagined city of Meridian, the librarian inherited three copies of an ancient atlas. One could be read on the eastern terminal, one on the western terminal, and one in the shelter beneath the school. The collection had survived in a form that nobody could open. Give later caretakers the authority to replace the catalog, repair the software, correct the record, and create new routes through the collection. Keep the old record when its lawful preservation matters; keep the correction equally visible. In a faraway city, the most valuable inheritance might not be an indestructible monument. It might be a modest institution that knows how to repair itself without silencing its readers. Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The library that did not own its readers In the imagined city of Meridian, the librarian inherited three copies of an ancient atlas. Part IX legend excerpt (fiction): The library that did not own its readers In the imagined city of Meridian, the librarian inherited three copies of an ancient atlas. One could be read on the eastern terminal, one on the western terminal, and one in the shelter beneath the school. summary: Este trabalho relata a experiência de desenvolvimento e implantação do RIF, sistema web de controle de refeições estudantis do Instituto Federal de Educação, Ciência e Tecnologia de Rondônia (IFRO) – Campus Porto Velho Calama. O sistema surgiu da necessidade do Departamento de Assistência ao Educando (DEPAE) de superar o gerenciamento baseado na importação recorrente de planilhas e de ampliar o acompanhamento da utilização das refeições. A aplicação foi construída de forma incremental, a partir de requisitos levantados junto ao DEPAE e ao restaurante institucional, com PHP, CodeIgniter 4, MySQL e arquitetura MVC, e integra o cadastro de estudantes e usuários, a solicitação, a análise e o agendamento das refeições, a confirmação por mensagem e o registro de retirada por QR Code. Entre 3 e 31 de agosto de 2026, o RIF registrou 18.882 refeições liberadas, das quais 13.337 foram confirmadas (70,63%) e 10.464 tiveram retirada registrada, além de 2.873 confirmações sem retirada e 86 inativações, envolvendo 80 estudantes que ignoraram as mensagens de confirmação. Os resultados indicam que o sistema fornece ao DEPAE indicadores e históricos para o acompanhamento do benefício. A experiência evidenciou, ainda, as dificuldades formativas da equipe e o impacto da mudança de requisitos, e apontou a necessidade de um manual de procedimentos para orientar os novos integrantes.

summary: This is a leakage-controlled active-learning benchmark archive evaluating diversity-, uncertainty-, committee-, Gaussian-process-, and D-optimal acquisition policies on molecular adsorption free-energy prediction under cold- and warm-start replay regimes. The release includes identity-level learning-curve metrics, family-locked inferential comparisons, operational threshold sensitivity analyses, machine-readable figure datasets, formatted reference tables, and reproducible Python verification scripts tied to protocol SHA-256 e3729ec2ec9d1df5d6e3f57121e4596a8e33454125d5210e2a6631e591f2f059. Raw upstream descriptor matrices and adsorption free-energy tables from an ongoing companion study are withheld pending publication, with their SHA-256 provenance digests retained in data/protocol_config.json.

summary: Version 1.1 (25 November 2026). Adds Amendment 1 (Rahman_2026_AV_adversarial_review_protocol_amendment_1.pdf). The protocol text (version 1.0, deposited 8 November 2026) is unchanged. No record had been screened when this protocol was deposited. Contents. Review questions and PICOC frame; eligibility criteria; information sources and search strategy (IEEE Xplore, Scopus, ACM Guide to Computing Literature, TRID, arXiv and hand-searched security programmes); selection process; data items and outcomes; quality appraisal; synthesis without meta-analysis (SWiM); confidence in findings; PRISMA-P 2015 checklist. Supplementary record. Every search string as run, with its date and record count: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24056184 Author: Samiur Rahman, University of Gloucestershire. Second reviewer: Afrin Nahar. The review is unfunded.
title: Protocol: Robust compared to whom? A systematic review of physical-world adversarial attacks on automated vehicle perception, judged against a human-driver baseline

summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π(x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half (π), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The author believes that this work can become a proof of the Riemann hypothesis; the missing step is to show that the unity of the process makes the transfer of the observer a symmetry. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. The missing step is also written as a statement about positivity: from Mertens' square 2(1 + cos θ)², which pushes the zeros away from 1, to the square of Weil's energy, which must hold them on ½ and forbid pairs of zeros on opposite sides of the circle. The work rests on classical results — Pell–Lagrange, Legendre's sieve, the explicit formula of Riemann and von Mangoldt — and proposes a new linking of them: the geometry of the seam as a model of the process linking the primes. The author's answer to Riemann's question is geometric: on each range chosen in a definite way, the process of the link of the primes is seen as the unit circle and a sinusoid around it; for his work the author regards this answer as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, and what in it is accepted as an initial prin
title: The Fractal Ladder of Prime Density: Quadratic Scale and Linear Error

summary: The work continues the geometric model of the distribution of primes [2] and the work “The Number Arrow and the Line 1/2” [1]. The geometric formula for the number of odd composites up to p², N(p) = 1 + 3(p − 1)(p − 3)/8, is treated as the first level of a ladder in which the scale is squared at each step: 5² → 5⁴ → 5⁸ → 5¹⁶. It is shown that this formula is the best quadratic formula for the level up to 5⁴: it is exact everywhere except for one compensating pair of misses (p = 15 and p = 17). The quadratic lattice of a level holds up to the basis 7 inclusive and breaks down right after it. The error of the formula splits into two superimposed tables: a smooth level correction and an oscillation which, in the explicit formula, is a sum of cosines over the zeros of the zeta function. The main result is a law of levels, checked on exact values of π(x) up to 3³² ≈ 1.9 · 10¹⁵: when the scale is squared, the relative error of the prime count is squared, and the error itself is inverse to the linear scale p = √x obtained from the difference of squares: ε · p stays of order one at all checked steps. The law holding at all steps is equivalent to the Riemann hypothesis (von Koch, 1901). The author puts forward the hypothesis that the self-similarity of the ladder may become a route to its proof: for this one must show that the step structure itself does not allow ε · p to grow faster than a power of the logarithm. This step is named but not taken. The method may become the basis for an exact count of prime density by levels without the exponential and the logarithm in the level formula. Section 7 gives a geometric reading for a reader without mathematical training: why the basis of the model is 2, 3, 5, 7, how the seam 8–9 links the linear and the quadratic levels, why the centres of the seam differ by exactly ¼ and how π arises from all the differences together, where zero is on the arrow and why the whole arrow projects into one circle. The similarity with the construction of the Birth of Dimensions model is shown. Section 8 shows that the accumulated mismatch over the seams is Euler's sine at one half (π), while accumulation over the primes gives γ (Mertens); that the error of the prime count at a step is of the order of the square root of the mismatch of the frame; and that the transfer of the observer changes nothing if and only if all zeros lie on the axis 1/2 — this is the Hilbert — Pólya programme. Each seam is a right triangle in a circle: the centre along the line is the radius, the centre on the circle the cosine, the hole the sine, and sin² + cos² = 1. The author believes that this work can become a proof of the Riemann hypothesis; the missing step is to show that the unity of the process makes the transfer of the observer a symmetry. The work is laid out as a programme of proof: the missing step is formulated as a target statement resting on the birth of the arrow — a pure projection from one unit, the product over the primes. summary: This chapter derives Temporal Mathematics (TM) from two posits on the geometry of pure time: one primordial carried continuum, carried by one oriented production from one origin, which never returns to a position; and one cadenced motion of rotation, thrust, and dilation, invariant in each of its parts and at every depth, which passes through every mark it crosses. No completion is posed. The infinite is potential: it is never posed, never instantiated, and never bounded. A static value is a stage refinement that converges, read through its stages, and the only complete object is the turn. Counting, arithmetic, rational reads, persistent residuals, the constant-slope cone, magnitudes, real and complex reads, the exhaustion integral, the exponential and the logarithm, π_TM, windings, and the counting of zeros by windings are each derived from this geometry before they are used. Seen from the posits, the structure of the chapter is the posited motion regarded from several sides, the ratios of its shapes give back arithmetic, and only the numbers read at a given depth require a computation. The first result is the generation of the zeros. The homologous positions of the closure ratios 1/(n+1), their delta tower, and repeated halving produce the finite apex Q_K, whose static read is G_K, together with its residual R_K; the static total η_TM = G_K + R_K is the static target of the apex reads and is reached at no finite depth. The finite modes of every depth enter at the entries of successor sides: at small entry weight, one near each height where the phase of the newest closure ratio (K+1)/K is a whole multiple of 2π_TM. The terminal modes, the zeros of η_TM on the open strip, are the zeros of the static zeta read, and each simple one is the static target of the finite modes of its cell, approached, from a threshold depth on, inside an envelope divided by two at each depth. On the closure line Re s = 1/2, the static read of the equal split of a closure ratio, the terminal read of the form is one signed position measured from the closure point; each change of sign, whose two signs the finite apex reads at a finite depth, is a return of the contre-forme to the closure point. Up to a height that carries no zero, the zeros number one more than the advance of the exchange phase from the height zero, counted in 2π_TM, increased by an arithmetic term; at the end of the j-th turn of the exchange rotation, a passage over which the exchange phase advances by 2π_TM, they number j increased by that term. On the closure line the zeta read, laid from the closure point, lies on the line of the chord from the closure point to the forme turned by the exchange rotation wherever that chord is non-null; the chord and its line come back at each 2π_TM of the exchange phase, and the arithmetic term is an integer exactly at the turn ends, where the turned forme is back on the forme. The forty zeros of height in (0, 123.65] are certified simple and on the closure line. At the end of a turn that is not the height of a zero, the parity of that term decides the inversion of the pole; the first inversion, at the end of the 127th turn, is certified. From height 8π_TM on, the zeta read at the end of a turn is the chord plus twice the projection of the other homologous positions, up to a remainder that tends to the null read. The second result is the derivation of the static read of TM, written TM_stat, whose clauses correspond one by one to those of the classical set-theoretic frame, with corrections grounded in the geometry, and the classification of the clauses of standard ZFC, written ZFC_std. The faithful clauses are theorems on closure counts. Infinity is corrected to potential continuation. Power set and choice are recovered for generated finite reads, and separation and replacement for generated criteria; their unrestricted forms and the completed real line are instantiated infinities, classified and not derived. title: Pure Time Theory – Chapter V – Temporal Mathematics: the Generation of the Zeros, the Static Read of TM and the Provenance of ZFC, and the Closure-Line Question

summary: This article analyzes the philosophical implications of Alpöge's November 2026 Lean formalization of the Riemann hypothesis, a proof co-developed with AI assistance. While formal verification is established, conceptual understanding remains incomplete. The article introduces "hybrid conceptual authority" to describe how conceptual contribution and justificatory authority diverge in AI-assisted mathematics. Drawing on philosophy of chemistry's model of explanatory autonomy, it proposes a four-dimensional framework verification, reconstruction, attribution, and interpretation for evaluating epistemic practice in proof production.
title: Hybrid Conceptual Authority in AI-Assisted Mathematics
